# ef — Embedding Flow

**A facade for boilerplate-less semantic search, corpus indexing, and
RAG-plug-in readiness.**

`ef` makes the modern embedding pipeline — corpus → segment → embed → vector
store → retrieve — usable with *progressive disclosure*: the light case (a list
of strings, search in one or two lines) and the heavy case (huge corpora, many
segmentations and embedders, varied sources and vector DBs) share **one
facade**. `ef` is *not* a RAG framework — it returns ranked context; you bring
your own LLM.

```python
import ef

index = ef.ingest(
    [
        "The cat sat on the mat",
        "Dogs are loyal companions",
        "Neural networks learn from data",
    ]
)

for hit in index.search("loyal dogs", limit=2):
    print(hit.score, hit.segment["text"])
```

That is the whole light path — no configuration, no install beyond `ef` itself.
`ingest` returns a `SearchableCorpus` ready to `search`.

## Installation

```bash
pip install ef                       # core: search, indexing, refresh, eval
pip install "ef[openai]"             # OpenAI embeddings
pip install "ef[sentence-transformers]"  # local sentence-transformers embeddings
pip install "ef[explore]"            # the L5 explore layer (UMAP, HDBSCAN)
pip install "ef[imbed]"              # imbed-backed components & cluster labelling
```

The core install needs only **numpy** (plus `dol`, `i2`, `vd`). The default
embedder is dependency-free — feature hashing, lexical not semantic; for real
semantic search pass a `sentence-transformers` or provider embedder (see below).

## What `ef` is

`ef` is a **facade, not a framework**. It owns the schemas (`Segment`,
`Embedder`, `Segmenter`, `Corpus`), the indexing core, refresh, and the
RAG-plug-in surface — and it stops there: no agent loops, no prompt templating,
no answer synthesis. “Bring your own LLM, your own agent framework, your own UI.”

It is built on five layers, the same facade covering all of them:

```default
L0 Sources    Corpus = MutableMapping[source_id, Source]   (dol store: fs/S3/API/RAM)
L1 Parse      pluggable text extraction
L2 Segment    Segmenter facade (chunkers)
L3 Embed      Embedder facade (provider / local adapters)
L4 Index      vd.Collection  (ef writes; vd owns the index)
L5 Derive     project / cluster / label   ("explore the corpus")
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   Search     search(query) -> ranked SearchHits
   RAG plug   retrieve(query) -> list[Segment]  handed to your LLM/agent
```

## Choosing an embedder

`ingest` and `SourceManager` take an `embedder=` — a string, a callable, a URL,
or an `Embedder`. The `as_embedder` seam normalizes all of them:

```python
from ef import as_embedder, openai_embedder, sentence_transformers_embedder

index = ef.ingest(corpus, embedder=sentence_transformers_embedder("all-MiniLM-L6-v2"))
index = ef.ingest(corpus, embedder=openai_embedder("text-embedding-3-small"))
index = ef.ingest(
    corpus, embedder=as_embedder("cohere:embed-v4.0")
)  # also voyage:/gemini:
index = ef.ingest(corpus, embedder=as_embedder(my_callable, model_id="custom@768"))
```

Hosted-API adapters: `openai_embedder` (needs `ef[openai]`) plus
`cohere_embedder`, `voyage_embedder` and `gemini_embedder` — the latter three
speak their providers’ REST endpoints directly, so they need only an API key,
no SDK. Each translates `ef`’s canonical `input_type` (`query` / `document` /
`classification` / `clustering`) to the vendor’s own task name. Local options:
`sentence_transformers_embedder`, `http_embedder` (any TEI-style service), and
the dependency-free `HashingEmbedder` default.

An `Embedder` is just a batch callable `Iterable[str] -> ndarray(n, dim)` with a
little metadata. Composition wrappers — `CachedEmbedder`, `RetryingEmbedder`,
`MultiEmbedder`, `NormalizingEmbedder`, `InstructionEmbedder` — each wrap an inner embedder.

For instruction-tuned models (E5-instruct, BGE, GTE, Qwen3-Embedding), condition the query side on the task: `InstructionEmbedder(inner, query_instruction="Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: ")` prefixes query texts and leaves documents bare, or pass `query_prompt=` / `prompt_names={"query": "query"}` to `sentence_transformers_embedder`. Either way the conditioned roles show up in `honored_input_types` and the instruction text is baked into `model_id`, so caches never mix vectors. Only trust this on an instruction-tuned model; on `all-MiniLM` it should be a near no-op.

## The heavy case — `SourceManager`

For large or changing corpora, multiple segmentations/embedders, and explicit
control, use `SourceManager`. Configs that share a pipeline step **share its
artifacts for free** — the indexing core is a content-addressed producer graph,
so a second embedder or segmenter re-uses everything upstream of it.

```python
from ef import SourceManager

manager = SourceManager(corpus, store="my_vectors")
manager.ingest(segmenter="recursive", embedder="openai:text-embedding-3-small")
index = manager.searchable()
```

## Keeping an index fresh

As sources change, an index drifts. `SourceManager` diagnoses and repairs it:

```python
report = manager.diagnose()  # the four staleness conditions
manager.refresh(mode="incremental")  # none | incremental | full | scoped_full
manager = SourceManager(corpus, store="my_vectors", auto_refresh=True)  # live
```

## RAG plug-in & evaluation

`ef` hands a corpus to *your* RAG/agent framework and measures retrieval
quality — it does not synthesize answers.

```python
segments = index.retrieve("how do neural networks learn?", limit=5)
context = "\n\n".join(s["text"] for s in segments)  # feed context to your LLM

from ef import evaluate_retrieval, evaluate_rag

retrieval = evaluate_retrieval(index.retrieve, qrels, queries)  # BEIR-shaped, NDCG@10
rag = evaluate_rag(samples)  # deterministic lexical metrics
```

`retrieve()` returns plain `Segment`s (provenance preserved in
`metadata["source"]`); `search()` returns scored `SearchHit`s. `with_reranker`
adds a two-stage reranking pass. `as_ragas_dataset` bridges to Ragas for
LLM-judged metrics.

## Exploring a corpus (layer L5)

The secondary “see the shape of the corpus” surface — `ef`’s visualization
heritage, the backend an `app_ef` corpus map consumes. Three functions, each
taking a corpus *or* a vector matrix:

```python
coords = ef.project(index, dims=2)  # PCA -> UMAP, 2-D coordinates
labels = ef.cluster(index, n_clusters=8)  # k-means (or method="hdbscan")
titles = ef.label_clusters(segments, labels)  # LLM-titled clusters (via imbed)
```

`project` and `cluster` import numpy-only; their default paths (PCA, k-means)
need no extra. `method="umap"`, `method="hdbscan"` and `label_clusters` use the
`ef[explore]` / `ef[imbed]` extras, imported lazily.

## What `ef` is *not*

No agent loops, no tool-calling, no conversation memory, no prompt templating,
no **LLM answer synthesis**, no bundled UI, no global config singleton. The
RAG-plug-in surface is the boundary: `ef` returns `retrieve(query) -> list[Segment]`; the application (or `srag` / `raglab` / LangGraph) takes it from
there.

## Links

- **GitHub**: https://github.com/thorwhalen/ef
- **vd** (vector-store interface): https://github.com/i2mint/vd
- **imbed** (heavy embedding/clustering implementations): https://github.com/thorwhalen/imbed

## Skills

ef ships a **developer** agent skill — install it into your agent host with
[`gh skill`](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_skill) (don’t have it?
[install gh](https://cli.github.com/)) before working in this repo:

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/ef ef-architecture --agent claude-code
```

| Skill             | Use it when…                                                                                                                     |
|-------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `ef-architecture` | (developer) starting any non-trivial change in the ef repo — refactoring, the Embedder/Segmenter facades, the Corpus abstraction |

# _autosummary/ef.ablation.html.md

# ef.ablation

Embedder ablations on a graded benchmark: run named *arms* over one corpus.

An ablation asks “which change to the embedder moved the metric?”. Each **arm**
is one embedding configuration (a query-side embedder, optionally a different
document-side one); every arm ranks the *same* segmented corpus for the *same*
queries and is scored by [`evaluate_retrieval()`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.evaluate_retrieval), so the only
thing that varies is the embedder.

Simple use, an A/B over any two embedders:

```default
bench = read_graded_cases("cases.jsonl", "named_sets.json")
report = run_arms(corpus, {"A": Arm(emb_a), "B": Arm(emb_b)}, bench)
print(report)
```

The instruction-embedding experiment of ef#34 is one instance:
[`instruction_arms()`](_autosummary/ef.ablation.html.md#ef.ablation.instruction_arms) builds its four arms (A: plain model, B: plain model +
instruction, the control, C: instruction-tuned model + instruction, C’: the same
model without it) and [`instruction_verdict()`](_autosummary/ef.ablation.html.md#ef.ablation.instruction_verdict) checks its success line.

Ranking is dense and document-level: every segment is embedded once per
*document-side* embedder (`input_type="document"`), a query is embedded with
the arm’s embedder (`input_type="query"`), and a document scores the best
cosine of any of its segments (max-pooling). Arms that share a document-side
embedder share its vectors: pass `doc_vectors` (any `MutableMapping`, e.g. a
`dol` store) to keep them across calls too. Only the query side differs between
an instructed arm and its bare twin, so the corpus is embedded once per model.

The labels format [`read_graded_cases()`](_autosummary/ef.ablation.html.md#ef.ablation.read_graded_cases) reads is the one `ir.eval` writes:
a JSONL of `{"artifact_id", "labels": {theme: level}}` cases with an optional
`{"__meta__": {"probes": {theme: query}}}` header, plus an optional
`{theme: {"distractors": [...], "hard_positives": [...]}}` JSON of named sets.

| [`DFLT_TOPICAL_INSTRUCTION`](_autosummary/ef.ablation.html.md#ef.ablation.DFLT_TOPICAL_INSTRUCTION) | The topical instruction for the instruction-tuned arm, in Qwen3-Embedding's format (`Instruct: <task>\nQuery:` with the query appended directly; E5-instruct wants `Query: `` with a space, so pass ``instruction=` there). |

| [`instruction_verdict`](_autosummary/ef.ablation.html.md#ef.ablation.instruction_verdict)(metrics, \*[, k, fp_cut, ...])  | Check ef#34's success line from `{arm: {"fp_rate@20": ..., ...}}`.        |
| [`read_graded_cases`](_autosummary/ef.ablation.html.md#ef.ablation.read_graded_cases)(cases_path[, ...])                | Load an `ir.eval`-style graded case file (and named sets) as a benchmark. |

### *class* ef.ablation.Arm(embedder, doc_embedder=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One embedding configuration: `embedder` for queries, `doc_embedder` for documents.

`doc_embedder` defaults to `embedder`. Give an instructed arm its bare
twin as `doc_embedder` when the instruction is query-side only, so the
corpus vectors are shared rather than recomputed. Either may be anything
[`ef.as_embedder()`](_autosummary/ef.html.md#ef.as_embedder) accepts (an `Embedder`, a spec string, a callable).

### ef.ablation.DFLT_GRADES *: [Mapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]* *= {'core': 2.0, 'strong': 1.0}*

Graded level -> relevance. Levels absent here count as not relevant, so
recall is “core/strong recall”.

### ef.ablation.DFLT_TOPICAL_INSTRUCTION *= 'Instruct: Given a topic, retrieve software packages whose main purpose is that topic, not packages that only mention related words\\nQuery:'*

The topical instruction for the instruction-tuned arm, in Qwen3-Embedding’s
format (`Instruct: <task>\nQuery:` with the query appended directly; E5-instruct
wants `Query: `` with a space, so pass ``instruction=` there). It asks for
what a document is *about*, which a plain model confuses with surface keywords.

### *class* ef.ablation.GradedBenchmark(qrels, queries, distractors=dict(), hard_positives=dict())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Queries, graded qrels and the named diagnostic sets, keyed by query id.

```pycon
>>> b = GradedBenchmark(qrels={'t': {'d1': 2.0, 'd9': 1.0}}, queries={'t': 'x'},
...                     distractors={'t': ('d2', 'd8')})
>>> b.restrict(['d1', 'd2']).qrels, b.restrict(['d1', 'd2']).distractors
({'t': {'d1': 2.0}}, {'t': ('d2',)})
```

#### restrict(doc_ids)

The same benchmark with every judgement limited to `doc_ids`.

Use it when some labelled documents could not be put in the corpus: a
document that cannot be retrieved would otherwise count as a miss for
every arm alike, diluting the differences.

* **Return type:**
  [`GradedBenchmark`](_autosummary/ef.ablation.html.md#ef.ablation.GradedBenchmark)

### *class* ef.ablation.MaxPoolRetriever(doc_ids, vectors, query_embedder)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Rank documents by the best cosine of any of their segments to the query.

```pycon
>>> from ef.embedders import HashingEmbedder
>>> emb = HashingEmbedder()
>>> segs = {'fruit': ['red apple', 'ripe pear'], 'car': ['blue car engine']}
>>> r = MaxPoolRetriever.from_segments(segs, emb)
>>> r('apple', limit=1)
['fruit']
```

### ef.ablation.instruction_arms(base, tuned=None, , instruction='Instruct: Given a topic, retrieve software packages whose main purpose is that topic, not packages that only mention related words\\nQuery:', base_instruction=None)

The four arms of the instruction experiment (A, B, C, C’).

- `A`: `base` as is (the plain baseline);
- `B`: `base` with the instruction on queries: the **control**, expected
  to move little, since a plain model was not trained to read instructions;
- `C`: `tuned` (an instruction-tuned model) with the instruction;
- `C'`: `tuned` without it, attributing C’s gain to the instruction
  rather than to the bigger model.

Instructions are query-side only (documents bare), so each model embeds the
corpus once. `base` / `tuned` are embedders or [`ef.as_embedder()`](_autosummary/ef.html.md#ef.as_embedder)
specs; without `tuned` only A and B are built.

* **Parameters:**
  * **base** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – the plain embedder (e.g. `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`).
  * **tuned** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – the instruction-tuned embedder (e.g. Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B).
  * **instruction** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the query prefix for C, verbatim (model separator included).
  * **base_instruction** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the query prefix for B; defaults to `instruction`.
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Arm`](_autosummary/ef.ablation.html.md#ef.ablation.Arm)]

```pycon
>>> from ef.embedders import HashingEmbedder
>>> sorted(instruction_arms(HashingEmbedder(), HashingEmbedder()))
['A', 'B', 'C', "C'"]
```

### ef.ablation.instruction_verdict(metrics, , k=20, fp_cut=0.5, control_tolerance=0.02, control_metrics=('ndcg', 'recall', 'fp_rate'))

Check ef#34’s success line from `{arm: {"fp_rate@20": ..., ...}}`.

Success = C cuts the named-distractor `fp_rate@k` by at least `fp_cut`
(relative) vs A, at equal-or-better `recall@k` (core/strong recall), and
the control B moves every `control_metrics` at `k` by less than
`control_tolerance` (absolute; 0.02 = 2 points). Also reports whether C
beats its bare twin C’ on `fp_rate@k` (the gain is the instruction’s).
If A has no distractor in its top `k` there is nothing to cut:
`fp_baseline_zero` is set and the verdict is not a success.

* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – when an arm (A, B, C) or one of its metrics at `k` is missing.
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

Accepts `BenchmarkReport.rows` turned into a mapping, e.g.
`{r['embedder']: r for r in report.rows}`.

```pycon
>>> m = {'A': {'fp_rate@20': .2, 'recall@20': .4, 'ndcg@20': .7},
...      'B': {'fp_rate@20': .2, 'recall@20': .41, 'ndcg@20': .7},
...      'C': {'fp_rate@20': .05, 'recall@20': .5, 'ndcg@20': .8},
...      "C'": {'fp_rate@20': .15, 'recall@20': .45, 'ndcg@20': .75}}
>>> v = instruction_verdict(m)
>>> v['success'], round(v['fp_reduction'], 2), v['instruction_beats_bare']
(True, 0.75, True)
```

### ef.ablation.read_graded_cases(cases_path, named_sets_path=None, , grades={'core': 2.0, 'strong': 1.0}, probes=None)

Load an `ir.eval`-style graded case file (and named sets) as a benchmark.

Each theme is one query: its text comes from `probes` or, failing that, the
`__meta__` header’s `probes`; its qrels are the cases whose level for that
theme is in `grades`. A theme with no such case is left out.

* **Parameters:**
  * **cases_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)) – JSONL of `{"artifact_id", "labels": {theme: level}}`.
  * **named_sets_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – optional JSON `{theme: {"distractors", "hard_positives"}}`.
  * **grades** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]) – level -> relevance grade; other levels are not relevant.
  * **probes** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `{theme: query text}`, overriding the header’s.
* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – when a labelled theme has no query text.
* **Return type:**
  [`GradedBenchmark`](_autosummary/ef.ablation.html.md#ef.ablation.GradedBenchmark)

### ef.ablation.run_arms(corpus, arms, benchmark, , k_values=(10, 20), segmenter=None, doc_vectors=None)

Score every arm on the same segmented corpus; one row per arm.

* **Parameters:**
  * **corpus** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – `{doc_id: text}` (segmented with `segmenter`) or
    `{doc_id: [segment, ...]}` (used as is).
  * **arms** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Arm`](_autosummary/ef.ablation.html.md#ef.ablation.Arm) | [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]) – `{name: Arm}`; a bare embedder is taken as `Arm(embedder)`.
  * **benchmark** ([`GradedBenchmark`](_autosummary/ef.ablation.html.md#ef.ablation.GradedBenchmark)) – what to score against ([`read_graded_cases()`](_autosummary/ef.ablation.html.md#ef.ablation.read_graded_cases)).
  * **k_values** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]) – rank cutoffs.
  * **segmenter** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – for string documents; see [`segment_corpus()`](_autosummary/ef.ablation.html.md#ef.ablation.segment_corpus).
  * **doc_vectors** ([`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), `ndarray`] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – cache of segment matrices keyed by
    `"<document-side model_id>/<digest of the segmented corpus>"`, so a
    persistent store (e.g. a `dol` store) can be reused across runs and
    corpora. A fresh dict by default; embedders without a `model_id`
    are never cached.
* **Return type:**
  [`BenchmarkReport`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.BenchmarkReport)

```pycon
>>> from ef.embedders import HashingEmbedder
>>> bench = GradedBenchmark({'q': {'fruit': 1.0}}, {'q': 'apple'})
>>> rep = run_arms({'fruit': 'red apple', 'car': 'blue car'},
...                {'A': HashingEmbedder()}, bench, k_values=(1,))
>>> rep.rows[0]['embedder'], rep.rows[0]['recall@1']
('A', 1.0)
```

### ef.ablation.segment_corpus(corpus, , segmenter=None)

`{doc_id: [segment text, ...]}`: strings are segmented, sequences kept.

`segmenter` is anything [`ef.as_segmenter()`](_autosummary/ef.html.md#ef.as_segmenter) accepts (default: the
recursive character splitter). Empty segments are dropped; a document left
with none is represented by its id, so it stays rankable.

```pycon
>>> segment_corpus({'a': ['x', ''], 'b': ''})
{'a': ['x'], 'b': ['b']}
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]


# _autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md

# ef.artifact_graph

The `ArtifactGraph` — `ef`’s content-addressed corpus-indexing core.

The corpus-indexing engine is **not a pipeline** — a pipeline is the wrong
abstraction. It is a *declared, content-addressed producer graph* (a DAG). The
one idea this module is built on:

```default
Cascade invalidation and configuration branching are the same operation.
```

A source edit changes a leaf’s content hash; a parameter change changes a leaf’s
content hash. Both produce a new `artifact_id` whose downstream cone needs
(re-)materialization — and the graph does not distinguish them. “Incremental
refresh”, “experiment tracking”, “hot reload”, “cache invalidation” and
“reactivity” are five names for that one operation.

Every artifact is addressed by **what produced it**:

```default
artifact_id = H(op, op_version, inputs, params)
```

so two configs that share an upstream step (same `op`, same `params`, same
`inputs`) share the *same* artifact id — each segment is computed once, each
vector once, no matter how many configs branch through the graph. Bumping an
`op_version` (or any `param`, or any input) yields a *new* id; the old
artifact keeps its old id and its old cached value, still valid for the config
that produced it. Config branching is therefore free.

The module’s surface:

- [`ProducerSpec`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec) — the declarative recipe for one produced artifact:
  *which op*, *which version*, *over which inputs*, *with which params*. It is
  fully serializable (string `op` key, not a raw callable — see below), so an
  [`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph)’s stores can be persisted.
- [`artifact_id()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.artifact_id) — the content-addressed id of a [`ProducerSpec`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec).
- [`producer_spec()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.producer_spec) — an ergonomic [`ProducerSpec`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec) constructor
  (positional inputs, keyword params).
- [`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph) — the graph itself: four injectable
  `MutableMapping`s (a content-addressed cache `store`, the `producers`
  registry, a reverse-`edges` index, an `ops` registry) and the four
  contract operations [`materialize()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.materialize) (lazy backward),
  [`mark_stale()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.mark_stale) / [`delete_cascade()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.delete_cascade)
  > (forward) and [`freshness()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.freshness).

\*\*Why `op` is a string, not a callable.\*\* The design wants the dependency
graph to scale to ~10⁷ nodes, which means the `producers` registry must be
*persistable* (a `dol` store — SQLite-backed for the heavy case). A raw
`Callable` cannot be serialized; an op *name* can. So [`ProducerSpec`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec)
records a string op-key, and the [`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph) resolves it to the
actual function through an injected `ops` registry at materialize time. Every
store (`store` / `producers` / `edges`) is a plain `MutableMapping`;
`ef` itself takes no SQLite dependency — you swap the backend in.

This module is the *engine*. Wiring it to a corpus — turning a Phase-3
[`ChangeEvent`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeEvent) into a [`delete_cascade()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.delete_cascade),
exposing the sources-and-configs facade — is the job of later phases
(`source_manager.py` / `refresh.py`); [`delete_cascade()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.delete_cascade)
is exactly the cascade a `"deleted"` / `"modified"` event will trigger.

Example — a two-step graph, a source “change”, a recompute:

```pycon
>>> graph = ArtifactGraph()
>>> _ = graph.register_op('upper', str.upper)
>>> _ = graph.register_op('repeat', lambda s, *, times: s * times)
>>> src = graph.put('src', 'ab')                       # a leaf source
>>> shout = graph.add(producer_spec('upper', src, op_version='1'))
>>> echo = graph.add(producer_spec('repeat', shout, op_version='1', times=3))
>>> graph.materialize(echo)                            # lazy backward compute
'ABABAB'
>>> graph.freshness(echo)
'materialized'
>>> _ = graph.mark_stale(src)                          # the source 'changed'
>>> graph.freshness(echo)                              # downstream invalidated
'stale'
>>> graph.materialize(echo)                            # rebuilt from the recipe
'ABABAB'
```

### *class* ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph(, store=None, producers=None, edges=None, ops=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A content-addressed producer graph — the corpus-indexing & refresh core.

The graph holds two kinds of node:

- **Leaves** — externally content-addressed inputs (an L0 source, hashed by
  [`ef.corpus.content_hash()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.content_hash)). A leaf has a *value* but no recipe; it is
  > supplied via [`put()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.put).
- **Produced artifacts** — a node with a [`ProducerSpec`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec) recipe,
  registered via [`add()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.add). Its id *is* [`artifact_id()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.artifact_id) of its recipe.

and four small `MutableMapping` stores, every one injectable so the graph
can be backed by RAM (the default) or by a persistent `dol` store:

- `store` — the content-addressed cache: `artifact_id -> value`.
- `producers` — the recipe registry: `artifact_id -> ProducerSpec`.
- `edges` — the reverse index: `artifact_id -> (dependent ids, ...)`,
  so the *downstream* cone of any node is one lookup away.
- `ops` — the op registry: `op_key -> callable`. The one store that is
  *not* persisted (callables are not serializable) — repopulate it with
  [`register_op()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.register_op) each process.

The four contract operations:

- [`materialize()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.materialize) — lazy *backward*: compute a node by recursively
  materializing its inputs, then memoize.
- [`mark_stale()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.mark_stale) — *forward*: drop the cached values of a node’s
  produced downstream cone, keeping the recipes (they will rebuild).
- [`delete_cascade()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.delete_cascade) — *forward*: remove a node and its whole downstream
  cone entirely (values, recipes and edges).
- [`freshness()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.freshness) — query a node’s state ([`Freshness`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.Freshness)).

plus the reachability queries [`descendants()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.descendants) (the downstream cone) and
[`ancestors()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.ancestors) (lineage — what an artifact was produced from).

* **Parameters:**
  * **store** ([`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the content-addressed value cache. Defaults to a fresh `dict`.
  * **producers** ([`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`ProducerSpec`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the recipe registry. Defaults to a fresh `dict`. If passed
    already-populated (a resumed/persisted graph) and `edges` is left
    empty, the reverse index is rebuilt from it on construction.
  * **edges** ([`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis)]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the reverse-dependency index. Defaults to a fresh `dict`; if
    passed already-populated it is trusted as-is (not rebuilt).
  * **ops** ([`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the op registry. Defaults to a fresh `dict`; [`register_op()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.register_op)
    adds to it.

```pycon
>>> graph = ArtifactGraph()
>>> _ = graph.register_op('join', lambda a, b, *, sep: f'{a}{sep}{b}')
>>> x = graph.put('x', 'hello')
>>> y = graph.put('y', 'world')
>>> both = graph.add(producer_spec('join', x, y, op_version='1', sep=', '))
>>> graph.materialize(both)
'hello, world'
>>> sorted(graph.descendants('x'))
[...]
>>> graph.delete_cascade('y')                     # the 'y' source is removed
frozenset(...)
>>> graph.freshness(both)                         # its consumer is gone too
'unknown'
```

#### add(spec)

Register a producer recipe; return its content-addressed id.

Idempotent: the id *is* the recipe, so adding an equal [`ProducerSpec`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec)
twice (or adding the shared upstream step of two branching configs)
registers one node and returns the same id — the basis of free config
branching. Inputs need not exist yet; the graph is declarative and
[`materialize()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.materialize) resolves them lazily.

```pycon
>>> graph = ArtifactGraph()
>>> a = graph.add(producer_spec('op', 'leaf', op_version='1'))
>>> a == graph.add(producer_spec('op', 'leaf', op_version='1'))  # idempotent
True
>>> len(graph.producers)
1
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### ancestors(key)

The lineage of `key` — every artifact it was transitively produced from.

Excludes `key` itself. Answers “what produced this?” — provenance /
lineage queries. The leaves of the returned set are the original
sources the artifact ultimately derives from.

```pycon
>>> graph = ArtifactGraph()
>>> _ = graph.register_op('id', lambda x: x)
>>> a = graph.add(producer_spec('id', 'src', op_version='1'))
>>> b = graph.add(producer_spec('id', a, op_version='1'))
>>> graph.ancestors(b) == {'src', a}
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### delete_cascade(key)

Remove `key` and its whole downstream cone — *forward*; return what was removed.

Deletes every artifact in `{key} ∪ descendants(key)` *entirely* —
cached value, recipe and edges — and detaches the cone from any upstream
inputs that survive it. Unlike [`mark_stale()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.mark_stale) this removes the
recipes too: use it when an artifact can never be rebuilt, the canonical
case being a **deleted source** (its segments, vectors and index entries
cascade away with it).

Returns the ids actually removed (those that had a value or a recipe).

```pycon
>>> graph = ArtifactGraph()
>>> _ = graph.register_op('id', lambda x: x)
>>> graph.put('s', 'v')
's'
>>> a = graph.add(producer_spec('id', 's', op_version='1'))
>>> graph.delete_cascade('s') == {'s', a}
True
>>> 's' in graph, a in graph
(False, False)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### descendants(key)

The downstream cone of `key` — every artifact transitively produced from it.

Excludes `key` itself. This is the set of artifacts a change to
`key` would invalidate; [`mark_stale()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.mark_stale) and [`delete_cascade()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.delete_cascade)
are built on it.

```pycon
>>> graph = ArtifactGraph()
>>> _ = graph.register_op('id', lambda x: x)
>>> a = graph.add(producer_spec('id', 'src', op_version='1'))
>>> b = graph.add(producer_spec('id', a, op_version='1'))
>>> graph.descendants('src') == {a, b}
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### freshness(key)

Report the state of `key` — [`Freshness`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.Freshness).

`"materialized"` if a value is cached; `"stale"` if a recipe exists
but no value (a [`materialize()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.materialize) will build it); `"unknown"` if the
graph has neither.

Because the graph is content-addressed, a *cached* value is always
correct *for its id* — staleness here means “not yet computed”, never
“computed wrong”. The richer staleness conditions (orphan / missing /
misconfigured, computed against `vd` index metadata) belong to a later
diagnostics phase, not to the graph core.

```pycon
>>> graph = ArtifactGraph()
>>> _ = graph.register_op('id', lambda x: x)
>>> graph.put('s', 'v')
's'
>>> a = graph.add(producer_spec('id', 's', op_version='1'))
>>> graph.freshness('s'), graph.freshness(a), graph.freshness('?')
('materialized', 'stale', 'unknown')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[`'materialized'`, `'stale'`, `'unknown'`]

#### mark_stale(key)

Invalidate `key`’s produced downstream cone — *forward*; return that cone.

Drops the **cached values** of every produced artifact in
`{key} ∪ descendants(key)`, *keeping the recipes* — so the next
[`materialize()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.materialize) recomputes them. Leaf nodes (inputs, no recipe) are
never touched: they cannot be recomputed, so dropping their value would
be data loss — use [`delete_cascade()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.delete_cascade) to remove an input.

This is the invalidation half of a refresh: when an op’s implementation
changes, or to force a recompute. (A *source* change is usually a
[`delete_cascade()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.delete_cascade) of the old content hash — the new content yields
a new leaf id.) Returns the produced artifacts that are now stale.

```pycon
>>> graph = ArtifactGraph()
>>> _ = graph.register_op('id', lambda x: x)
>>> graph.put('s', 'v')
's'
>>> a = graph.add(producer_spec('id', 's', op_version='1'))
>>> _ = graph.materialize(a)
>>> graph.mark_stale('s') == {a}        # the leaf 's' itself is not "stale"
True
>>> graph.freshness(a)
'stale'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### materialize(key)

Compute (or fetch the cached value of) the artifact `key` — lazy *backward*.

If `key` is already cached in `store` its value is returned
directly. Otherwise its recipe’s inputs are materialized recursively
(depth-first), the op is called `op(*input_values, **params)`, and the
result is memoized in `store` before being returned — so a second
[`materialize()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.materialize) is a cache hit, and a shared upstream artifact is
computed exactly once however many configs depend on it.

* **Raises:**
  * [**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) – if `key` is neither cached nor has a producer recipe
        (an unresolved leaf — supply it with [`put()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.put)).
  * [**LookupError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#LookupError) – if a recipe’s `op` is not in the `ops` registry.
  * [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – if the producer graph contains a cycle (a content-
        addressed graph cannot — this guards a hand-corrupted registry).
* **Return type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

```pycon
>>> graph = ArtifactGraph()
>>> _ = graph.register_op('double', lambda x: x * 2)
>>> graph.put('n', 21)
'n'
>>> out = graph.add(producer_spec('double', 'n', op_version='1'))
>>> graph.materialize(out)
42
```

#### put(key, value)

Store a **leaf** `value` (an external input) under `key`; return `key`.

A leaf has a value but no recipe — typically an L0 source keyed by its
[`ef.corpus.content_hash()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.content_hash). Returns `key` so the call composes:

```default
src = graph.put(content_hash(text), text)
```

```pycon
>>> graph = ArtifactGraph()
>>> graph.put('doc-1', 'some text')
'doc-1'
>>> graph.freshness('doc-1')
'materialized'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### register_op(name, fn)

Register the callable `fn` under the op key `name`; return `fn`.

[`materialize()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.materialize) resolves a [`ProducerSpec`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec)’s string `op`
through this registry. The op is called `fn(*input_values, **params)`:
the materialized inputs positionally, the spec’s `params` as keywords.

```pycon
>>> graph = ArtifactGraph()
>>> graph.register_op('upper', str.upper)
<method 'upper' of 'str' objects>
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactId

A content-addressed artifact identifier — a `sha256` hex digest for a
produced artifact ([`artifact_id()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.artifact_id)), or a caller-supplied content hash
for a leaf (e.g. [`ef.corpus.content_hash()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.content_hash) of an L0 source).

### ef.artifact_graph.Freshness

The state of an artifact, reported by [`ArtifactGraph.freshness()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.freshness):
`"materialized"` (a value is cached), `"stale"` (a recipe exists but no
cached value — [`materialize()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.materialize) will (re)build it) or
`"unknown"` (the graph has neither a value nor a recipe for the id).

alias of [`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[‘materialized’, ‘stale’, ‘unknown’]

### ef.artifact_graph.OpKey

The key an [`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph) resolves to a producer callable through its
`ops` registry. A short, stable operation name, e.g. `"segment"` or
`"embed"`.

### *class* ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec(op, op_version, inputs=(), params=dict())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A declarative recipe for one produced artifact — the graph’s node type.

A [`ProducerSpec`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec) says: *this artifact is produced by op* `op` \*at
version\* `op_version`, *applied to the artifacts* `inputs`  *(passed
positionally), with the keyword parameters* `params`. It does **not**
hold the producer callable — only the string `op` key — so a spec is
fully serializable ([`as_dict()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec.as_dict) / [`from_dict()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec.from_dict)) and the graph’s
`producers` registry can be persisted.

The recipe is the artifact’s *identity*: [`artifact_id()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.artifact_id) hashes exactly
these four fields. Treat an instance as immutable — it is frozen, and
mutating `params` in place would silently desynchronize it from its id.

#### op

the op key, resolved to a callable via the graph’s `ops` registry.

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### op_version

the op’s version string. It participates in the id, so a
behavior change to an op **must** be paired with a version bump —
reusing a version for changed behavior silently serves stale cached
values (the graph trusts the version; it cannot inspect the code).

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### inputs

the input artifact ids, in the order the op receives them
positionally. Order is significant — it is part of the id.

* **Type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis)]

#### params

the op’s keyword arguments. Key order is *not* significant
(the id is computed over canonical, sorted-key JSON); pass
defaults-filled, fully-named params so that two semantically equal
calls hash equal.

* **Type:**
  [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

```pycon
>>> spec = producer_spec('embed', 'seg-1', op_version='3', model='small')
>>> spec.op, spec.inputs, spec.op_version
('embed', ('seg-1',), '3')
>>> spec.params == {'model': 'small'}
True
```

#### as_dict()

Return a plain-`dict` form of the spec — JSON-serializable.

The inverse of [`from_dict()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec.from_dict). Use it to persist a `producers`
registry to a `dol` JSON store.

```pycon
>>> producer_spec('embed', 'a', 'b', op_version='1', dim=256).as_dict()
{'op': 'embed', 'op_version': '1', 'inputs': ['a', 'b'], 'params': {'dim': 256}}
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

#### *classmethod* from_dict(d)

Rebuild a [`ProducerSpec`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec) from its [`as_dict()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec.as_dict) form.

```pycon
>>> spec = producer_spec('embed', 'a', 'b', op_version='1', dim=256)
>>> ProducerSpec.from_dict(spec.as_dict()) == spec
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`ProducerSpec`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec)

### ef.artifact_graph.artifact_id(spec)

Content-addressed id of `spec` — `sha256` over its four fields.

The id is `sha256` of canonical (sorted-key) JSON of
`{op, op_version, inputs, params}`. Two specs that describe the same
computation hash *identically*; any change to the op, its version, its
inputs (including their order) or its params yields a *different* id. That
is what makes the graph content-addressed: the id *is* the recipe.

```pycon
>>> a = producer_spec('embed', 'seg-1', op_version='2', model='small')
>>> artifact_id(a) == artifact_id(producer_spec(
...     'embed', 'seg-1', op_version='2', model='small'))
True
>>> len(artifact_id(a))
64
>>> artifact_id(a) == artifact_id(producer_spec(
...     'embed', 'seg-1', op_version='3', model='small'))   # version bump
False
>>> artifact_id(producer_spec('op', 'x', 'y', op_version='1')) == artifact_id(
...     producer_spec('op', 'y', 'x', op_version='1'))      # input order matters
False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### ef.artifact_graph.producer_spec(op, \*inputs, op_version, \*\*params)

Build a [`ProducerSpec`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec) ergonomically — inputs positional, params keyword.

The natural way to write a recipe: the input artifact ids are positional
(their order is significant — it is the order the op receives them), and
every keyword argument is an op parameter. `op_version` is keyword-only
and required — an op without a stated version cannot be content-addressed
safely.

```pycon
>>> spec = producer_spec('segment', 'doc-1', op_version='1', size=512, overlap=64)
>>> spec.op, spec.inputs
('segment', ('doc-1',))
>>> spec.params == {'size': 512, 'overlap': 64}
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`ProducerSpec`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec)


# _autosummary/ef.config.html.md

# ef.config

The config layer — declarative, content-addressable pipeline specs.

A *pipeline* in `ef` is not an object graph you wire by hand — it is **data**.
A [`PipelineSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.PipelineSpec) declares the segment→embed chain; each step is a
[`TransformSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.TransformSpec) (an op key, an op version, and the keyword params that
feed the content hash). Because a spec is fully serializable and content-hashed
([`config_id()`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.config_id)), two configs that share a step share that step’s artifacts
in the [`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph) for free — config branching
costs nothing beyond the divergent cone (design notes §3.1).

This module is the *bridge* between an ordinary Python call and a content-
addressed graph node. For content addressing to be **correct**, two
semantically-equal calls must produce identical params — so `op(text)` and
`op(text, size=512)` (`512` being the default) must hash the same. The
canonical `i2` idiom does exactly that normalization:

- [`full_kwargs()`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.full_kwargs) — the raw recipe (design notes §3.8): a call `(args,
  kwargs)` → a fully-named, defaults-filled kwargs dict.
- [`step_params()`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.step_params) — its spec-building application: the canonical *keyword*
  params of an op, with the leading positional *input* slots (the upstream
  artifact ids) dropped, since those become [`ProducerSpec.inputs`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec.inputs), not params.

Phase 4’s [`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph) takes [`ProducerSpec`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec)s as given; this module (and
[`ef.ops`](_autosummary/ef.ops.html.md#module-ef.ops) / [`ef.source_manager`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#module-ef.source_manager)) is where ordinary calls *become*
those specs.

Example — two pipelines, equal segment step, divergent embed step:

```pycon
>>> seg = TransformSpec(op='segment:recursive', op_version='1', params={})
>>> embed_a = TransformSpec(op='embed:m-a', op_version='1', params={})
>>> embed_b = TransformSpec(op='embed:m-b', op_version='1', params={})
>>> pa = PipelineSpec(segment=seg, embed=embed_a)
>>> pb = PipelineSpec(segment=seg, embed=embed_b)
>>> config_id(pa) == config_id(pb)        # different embedders → different config
False
>>> config_id(pa) == config_id(PipelineSpec.from_dict(pa.as_dict()))
True
```

### Module Attributes

| [`ConfigId`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.ConfigId)   | A content-addressed pipeline identifier — the `sha256` hex digest of a [`PipelineSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.PipelineSpec) ([`config_id()`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.config_id)).   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`full_kwargs`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.full_kwargs)(op[, args, kwargs])         | Normalize a call into a canonical, fully-named, defaults-filled kwargs dict.                                       |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`step_params`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.step_params)(op[, raw_params, n_inputs]) | The canonical *keyword* params of an op step — its inputs dropped.                                                 |
| [`config_id`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.config_id)(spec)                         | Content-addressed id of a [`PipelineSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.PipelineSpec) — `sha256` over its steps. |

### Classes

| [`ConfigId`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.ConfigId)                                | A content-addressed pipeline identifier — the `sha256` hex digest of a [`PipelineSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.PipelineSpec) ([`config_id()`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.config_id)).   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`TransformSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.TransformSpec)(op, op_version[, params]) | One step of a pipeline — a serializable recipe for an op application.                                                                                                                                  |
| [`PipelineSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.PipelineSpec)(segment, embed)            | A whole indexing pipeline as data — the segment→embed chain.                                                                                                                                           |

### ef.config.ConfigId

A content-addressed pipeline identifier — the `sha256` hex digest of a
[`PipelineSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.PipelineSpec) ([`config_id()`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.config_id)). It is what `ef` writes into
`vd` index metadata as `config_hash` so a later phase can tell which
pipeline produced a vector.

### *class* ef.config.PipelineSpec(segment, embed)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A whole indexing pipeline as data — the segment→embed chain.

A [`PipelineSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.PipelineSpec) is the declarative description of one *config*: a
[`TransformSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.TransformSpec) for the segmenter and one for the embedder. It is
fully serializable ([`as_dict()`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.PipelineSpec.as_dict) / [`from_dict()`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.PipelineSpec.from_dict)) and content-hashed
by [`config_id()`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.config_id). Registering a second [`PipelineSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.PipelineSpec) that
differs only in its embed step shares the segment artifacts in the
[`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph) — that is config branching, and
the graph gives it for free.

The `segment``→``embed` ordering *is* the input wiring: the embed step
consumes the segment step’s output. (Phase 5 fixes this two-step shape; a
later phase may generalize it to an arbitrary step list.)

```pycon
>>> seg = TransformSpec(op='segment:r', op_version='1', params={})
>>> emb = TransformSpec(op='embed:m@8', op_version='1', params={'input_type': 'document'})
>>> spec = PipelineSpec(segment=seg, embed=emb)
>>> spec.embed.params['input_type']
'document'
>>> PipelineSpec.from_dict(spec.as_dict()) == spec
True
```

#### as_dict()

Return a plain-`dict` (JSON-serializable) form of the pipeline.

```pycon
>>> seg = TransformSpec(op='segment:r', op_version='1', params={})
>>> emb = TransformSpec(op='embed:m', op_version='1', params={})
>>> PipelineSpec(segment=seg, embed=emb).as_dict()['segment']['op']
'segment:r'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

#### *classmethod* from_dict(d)

Rebuild a [`PipelineSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.PipelineSpec) from its [`as_dict()`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.PipelineSpec.as_dict) form.

* **Return type:**
  [`PipelineSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.PipelineSpec)

### *class* ef.config.TransformSpec(op, op_version, params=dict())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One step of a pipeline — a serializable recipe for an op application.

A [`TransformSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.TransformSpec) names *which op* (`op`, a key resolved through
the [`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph)’s `ops` registry), \*at which
version\* (`op_version` — it participates in every downstream hash), and
*with which keyword params* (`params`). It does **not** record the step’s
inputs: those are wired structurally by the [`PipelineSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.PipelineSpec) (the embed
step consumes the segment step’s output). It is the per-step counterpart of
a [`ProducerSpec`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec).

The op key carries the *component identity* — e.g. `"embed:openai:text-
embedding-3-large@1024"` or `"segment:<segmenter-identity>"` (see
[`ef.ops`](_autosummary/ef.ops.html.md#module-ef.ops)) — so two configs with different components get disjoint
artifact cones automatically.

```pycon
>>> ts = TransformSpec(op='embed:m@8', op_version='2', params={'input_type': 'document'})
>>> ts.op, ts.op_version
('embed:m@8', '2')
>>> TransformSpec.from_dict(ts.as_dict()) == ts
True
```

#### as_dict()

Return a plain-`dict` (JSON-serializable) form of the spec.

```pycon
>>> TransformSpec(op='segment:r', op_version='1', params={}).as_dict()
{'op': 'segment:r', 'op_version': '1', 'params': {}}
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

#### *classmethod* from_dict(d)

Rebuild a [`TransformSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.TransformSpec) from its [`as_dict()`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.TransformSpec.as_dict) form.

* **Return type:**
  [`TransformSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.TransformSpec)

### ef.config.config_id(spec)

Content-addressed id of a [`PipelineSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.PipelineSpec) — `sha256` over its steps.

The id is `sha256` of the canonical (sorted-key) JSON of
[`PipelineSpec.as_dict()`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.PipelineSpec.as_dict). Two pipelines that describe the same
computation hash identically; any change to a step’s op, version or params
yields a different id. `ef` writes this digest into `vd` index metadata
as `config_hash`.

```pycon
>>> seg = TransformSpec(op='segment:r', op_version='1', params={})
>>> emb = TransformSpec(op='embed:m@8', op_version='1', params={})
>>> cid = config_id(PipelineSpec(segment=seg, embed=emb))
>>> len(cid)
64
>>> cid == config_id(PipelineSpec(segment=seg, embed=emb))
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### ef.config.full_kwargs(op, args=(), kwargs=None)

Normalize a call into a canonical, fully-named, defaults-filled kwargs dict.

The `i2.Sig` recipe of design notes §3.8. A call expressed as positional
`args` + keyword `kwargs` is mapped onto `op`’s signature: every
parameter is named, and any parameter the call left implicit is filled with
its default. The result is therefore *stable* — `op(x)` and
`op(x, size=512)` (`512` the default) yield the **same** dict, which is
what makes a content hash built from it correct.

* **Parameters:**
  * **op** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]) – the callable whose signature defines the parameter names/defaults.
  * **args** ([`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any), [`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis)]) – the call’s positional arguments — for an [`ef.ops`](_autosummary/ef.ops.html.md#module-ef.ops) op these
    are the upstream artifact ids; [`step_params()`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.step_params) drops them again.
  * **kwargs** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the call’s keyword arguments.
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

```pycon
>>> def embed(segments, *, input_type='document', dim=None): ...
>>> full_kwargs(embed, ('seg-1',), {'input_type': 'query'})
{'segments': 'seg-1', 'input_type': 'query', 'dim': None}
>>> full_kwargs(embed, ('seg-1',))                 # defaults filled in
{'segments': 'seg-1', 'input_type': 'document', 'dim': None}
```

### ef.config.step_params(op, raw_params=None, , n_inputs=1)

The canonical *keyword* params of an op step — its inputs dropped.

An [`ef.ops`](_autosummary/ef.ops.html.md#module-ef.ops) op is called `op(*input_values, **params)`: the first
`n_inputs` positional parameters are upstream artifacts (they belong in
[`ProducerSpec.inputs`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec.inputs), not in
the params), and every remaining parameter is a hashable step param. This
runs [`full_kwargs()`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.full_kwargs) with placeholder inputs, then drops those input
slots — leaving exactly the params, defaults filled, ready for a
[`TransformSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.TransformSpec).

* **Parameters:**
  * **op** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]) – the op callable whose signature is the param contract.
  * **raw_params** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the keyword params the caller actually supplied; anything
    omitted is defaulted.
  * **n_inputs** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – how many leading positional parameters are upstream inputs.
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

```pycon
>>> def embed(segments, *, input_type='document'): ...
>>> step_params(embed, {'input_type': 'query'})
{'input_type': 'query'}
>>> step_params(embed)                              # default filled in
{'input_type': 'document'}
>>> def segment(source): ...
>>> step_params(segment)                            # no params at all
{}
```


# _autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md

# ef.corpus

The `Corpus` abstraction — `ef`’s source layer (L0) — and change detection.

A *corpus* is the entry point of the pipeline: the set of source documents to
be segmented, embedded and indexed. In `ef` a corpus is deliberately *not* a
new class — it is just a mapping:

```default
Corpus = MutableMapping[source_id, Source]
```

Any `dol`-style mapping is a corpus: a plain `dict` (RAM), a filesystem
folder, an S3 bucket, an API-backed store. The backing store is swappable
because the rest of `ef` only ever sees a `MutableMapping`. This module
provides:

- [`Source`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.Source) / [`Corpus`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.Corpus) — the type aliases that name the contract.
- [`as_corpus()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.as_corpus) — the dependency-injection seam: `None` / a mapping / a
  directory path / an iterable of strings → a corpus. Mirrors
  [`as_embedder()`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.as_embedder) and
  [`as_segmenter()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenter_adapters.html.md#ef.segmenter_adapters.as_segmenter).
- [`content_hash()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.content_hash) — the content hash of a source, the basis of change
  detection. Hashes *normalized* content (via [`ef.hashing`](_autosummary/ef.hashing.html.md#module-ef.hashing)); for a
  structured source it hashes the text only, so metadata-only edits never
  trigger a spurious re-embed.
- [`ChangeDetectingCorpus`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeDetectingCorpus) — a corpus *wrapper* that content-hashes
  values and reports what changed, both through-the-wrapper (via an
  `on_change` callback) and out-of-band (via [`scan()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeDetectingCorpus.scan)).

[`ChangeDetectingCorpus`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeDetectingCorpus) is the  *“something changed”* half of incremental
refresh; the downstream cascade is the `ArtifactGraph` (a later phase). The
`on_change` callback is the seam those two halves meet at.

Example — detect changes as they are written:

```pycon
>>> events = []
>>> corpus = ChangeDetectingCorpus(on_change=events.append)
>>> corpus['doc1'] = 'hello world'
>>> corpus['doc1'] = 'hello world'      # identical content — idempotent, no event
>>> corpus['doc1'] = 'hello there'      # a real change
>>> del corpus['doc1']
>>> [(e.source_id, e.kind) for e in events]
[('doc1', 'added'), ('doc1', 'modified'), ('doc1', 'deleted')]
```

### Module Attributes

| [`Source`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.Source)     | A source document.                                                                                  |
|-------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`Corpus`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.Corpus)     | a mapping from `source_id` to [`Source`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.Source).              |
| [`ChangeKind`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeKind) | The kinds of change [`ChangeDetectingCorpus`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeDetectingCorpus) reports. |

### Functions

| [`content_hash`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.content_hash)(source, \*[, content_keys])   | Content hash of a source document — `sha256` of its normalized content.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`as_corpus`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.as_corpus)([x])                             | Normalize `x` into a corpus (`MutableMapping[source_id, Source]`).        |

### Classes

| [`ChangeEvent`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeEvent)(source_id, kind[, old_hash, ...])     | A single detected change to a source in a corpus.                        |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`CorpusDiff`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.CorpusDiff)([added, modified, deleted, unchanged]) | The result of comparing a corpus's content against known content hashes. |
| [`ChangeDetectingCorpus`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeDetectingCorpus)([corpus, on_change, ...])   | A corpus wrapper that content-hashes values and reports what changed.    |

### *class* ef.corpus.ChangeDetectingCorpus(corpus=None, , on_change=None, hashes=None, content_keys=None, fingerprint=None)

Bases: [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)

A corpus wrapper that content-hashes values and reports what changed.

Wraps any inner corpus (a `MutableMapping[source_id, Source]`) and adds
change detection *without* altering its mapping behavior — reads, writes and
deletes pass straight through to the inner store. It is to a corpus what
[`CachedEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md#ef.embedder_wrappers.CachedEmbedder) is to an embedder: a
transparent, composable layer.

Changes are noticed two ways:

- **Through the wrapper.** A `corpus[id] = source` or `del corpus[id]`
  that actually changes content fires the injected `on_change` callback
  with a [`ChangeEvent`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeEvent). Writing *identical* content is a no-op (no
  event) — the basis of idempotent ingestion.
- **Out of band.** When the backing store is edited directly (a file
  changed on disk, an S3 object replaced), [`scan()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeDetectingCorpus.scan) re-reads every
  source, compares hashes, fires events for what differs and returns a
  [`CorpusDiff`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.CorpusDiff). [`diff()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeDetectingCorpus.diff) runs the same comparison with no side
  > effects.

The `on_change` callback is the seam the downstream `ArtifactGraph`
plugs into: a `"modified"` / `"deleted"` event is exactly the trigger
for a cascade invalidation.

On construction a *baseline* is established: the current content hashes of
the inner corpus are recorded silently (no events). Pass an already-populated
`hashes` registry to instead resume from a persisted baseline — then call
[`scan()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeDetectingCorpus.scan) to reconcile any drift.

* **Parameters:**
  * **corpus** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – the inner corpus to wrap. Coerced via [`as_corpus()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.as_corpus), so a
    directory path / `dict` / iterable of sources / `None` all work.
  * **on_change** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`ChangeEvent`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeEvent)], [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – called with each [`ChangeEvent`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeEvent). Defaults to a no-op.
    It should be cheap and not raise; an exception propagates to the
    caller *after* the corpus and registry are already consistent.
  * **hashes** ([`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the hash registry — a `MutableMapping[source_id, str]` of the
    last-known content hash per source. Injectable so it can be
    persisted (e.g. a `dol` store); defaults to an in-RAM `dict`.
    If passed already-populated it is trusted as the baseline.
  * **content_keys** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – forwarded to [`content_hash()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.content_hash) — metadata keys that
    participate in the hash.
  * **fingerprint** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Hashable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Hashable)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – an optional cheap `source_id -> Hashable` callback (an
    mtime / etag prefilter). When given, [`scan()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeDetectingCorpus.scan) / [`diff()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeDetectingCorpus.diff)
    skip re-hashing a source whose fingerprint is unchanged. The
    content hash always remains the source of truth — the fingerprint
    is only a speed optimization, never trusted to *declare* a change.

```pycon
>>> backing = {'a': 'one', 'b': 'two'}
>>> corpus = ChangeDetectingCorpus(backing)   # baseline adopts 'a' and 'b'
>>> backing['a'] = 'ONE'                      # edited behind the wrapper's back
>>> backing['c'] = 'three'
>>> del backing['b']
>>> d = corpus.scan()
>>> (d.added, d.modified, d.deleted)
(('c',), ('a',), ('b',))
```

#### diff()

Compare current corpus content against the registry — **no side effects**.

Detects out-of-band edits (changes made to the backing store directly)
without firing events or updating the registry. [`scan()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeDetectingCorpus.scan) is the
effectful counterpart.

* **Return type:**
  [`CorpusDiff`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.CorpusDiff)

#### scan()

Reconcile the registry with the corpus, fire events, return the diff.

Use this to pick up **out-of-band** edits — changes made to the backing
store directly rather than through this wrapper. Every detected change
fires a [`ChangeEvent`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeEvent) and the registry (and fingerprints) are
advanced to the new state, so a second [`scan()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeDetectingCorpus.scan) with nothing
further changed is a no-op. [`diff()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeDetectingCorpus.diff) is the side-effect-free version.

* **Return type:**
  [`CorpusDiff`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.CorpusDiff)

### *class* ef.corpus.ChangeEvent(source_id, kind, old_hash=None, new_hash=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A single detected change to a source in a corpus.

Emitted by [`ChangeDetectingCorpus`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeDetectingCorpus) to its `on_change` callback.
`old_hash` is `None` for an `"added"` event, `new_hash` is `None`
for a `"deleted"` one.

#### source_id

the key of the source that changed.

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### kind

`"added"`, `"modified"` or `"deleted"`.

* **Type:**
  [`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[`'added'`, `'modified'`, `'deleted'`]

#### old_hash

the source’s previous content hash, if any.

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### new_hash

the source’s new content hash, if any.

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### ef.corpus.ChangeKind

The kinds of change [`ChangeDetectingCorpus`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeDetectingCorpus) reports.

alias of [`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[‘added’, ‘modified’, ‘deleted’]

### ef.corpus.Corpus

a mapping from `source_id` to [`Source`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.Source). `ef` never
requires a dedicated class — any `dol`-style `MutableMapping` (RAM,
filesystem, S3, API) *is* a corpus. [`as_corpus()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.as_corpus) builds one.

* **Type:**
  A corpus

alias of [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]

### *class* ef.corpus.CorpusDiff(added=(), modified=(), deleted=(), unchanged=())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The result of comparing a corpus’s content against known content hashes.

The four fields partition the corpus’s source ids; each is a sorted tuple,
so a [`CorpusDiff`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.CorpusDiff) is deterministic and JSON-friendly. Truthiness
reports whether *anything* changed.

```pycon
>>> d = CorpusDiff(added=('b',), modified=('a',))
>>> bool(d), d.changed
(True, ('b', 'a'))
>>> bool(CorpusDiff(unchanged=('a', 'b')))
False
```

#### *property* changed *: [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), ...]*

The source ids that are new or modified — the set to (re-)materialize.

### ef.corpus.Source *= str | collections.abc.Mapping[str, typing.Any]*

A source document. Either plain `text`, or a `Mapping` carrying a
`text` key alongside metadata — the same shape a
[`Segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.Segmenter) accepts as input.

### ef.corpus.as_corpus(x=None, , \*\*kwargs)

Normalize `x` into a corpus (`MutableMapping[source_id, Source]`).

The single dependency-injection seam through which every `ef` entry point
accepts a user-supplied corpus — the mirror of
[`as_embedder()`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.as_embedder) and
[`as_segmenter()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenter_adapters.html.md#ef.segmenter_adapters.as_segmenter). Accepts, in order:

1. `None` — a fresh empty in-RAM `dict`;
2. a `Mapping` — returned **unchanged** (a `dict`, a `dol` store,
   another corpus: it already *is* a corpus);
3. a directory path (`str` / `os.PathLike` naming an existing
   directory) — a `dol` filesystem store of the text files under it
   (`dol` is imported lazily; only this branch needs it);
4. an iterable of sources (strings or mappings) — an in-RAM `dict` keyed
   by each source’s [`content_hash()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.content_hash) (content-addressed, so duplicate
   sources collapse to one entry).

Extra `**kwargs` are forwarded to the `dol` filesystem store (the
directory branch only) and ignored otherwise.

* **Raises:**
  [**TypeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#TypeError) – if `x` is a non-directory string, or none of the above.

```pycon
>>> as_corpus()
{}
>>> as_corpus({'a': 'x'})                 # a mapping passes straight through
{'a': 'x'}
>>> sorted(as_corpus(['alpha', 'beta']).values())
['alpha', 'beta']
>>> len(as_corpus(['dup', 'dup']))        # content-addressed: duplicates collapse
1
```

### ef.corpus.content_hash(source, , content_keys=None)

Content hash of a source document — `sha256` of its normalized content.

This is the basis of change detection: re-reading an unchanged source
yields an identical hash, so a refresh that finds the same hash does
nothing. Hashing *normalized* content (NFC, no BOM, `\n` line endings —
