see [`ef.hashing`](_autosummary/ef.hashing.html.md#module-ef.hashing)) means cosmetic encoding differences never look like
a change.

The treatment of a `Mapping` source is deliberate:

- a plain `str` source — the hash covers the text;
- a `Mapping` with a `text` key — the hash covers `source['text']`
  **only**. A change to title, tags, ACL or any other metadata does *not*
  change the hash, so it never triggers a spurious re-segment/re-embed
  (embedding is the pipeline’s most expensive step). Name the metadata keys
  that *do* feed downstream in `content_keys` and changes to those keys
  will be detected;
- a `Mapping` *without* a `text` key — treated as a structured document
  and hashed via canonical (sorted-key) JSON of the whole mapping;
- `bytes` — hashed raw (no text normalization is possible pre-parse).

* **Parameters:**
  * **source** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – a `str`, `bytes`, or a `Mapping` (ideally with a `text`
    key).
  * **content_keys** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – metadata keys whose values join the text in the hash.
    Each key is looked up at the top level of `source` or inside a
    `source['metadata']` sub-mapping. Use this *only* for metadata
    that genuinely affects the L1–L4 pipeline (e.g. a title prepended
    to the text before embedding); key order does not matter.
* **Raises:**
  [**TypeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#TypeError) – if `source` is not a `str`, `bytes` or `Mapping`.
* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

```pycon
>>> content_hash('hello') == content_hash('hello')
True
>>> content_hash('hello') == content_hash('hello world')
False
>>> content_hash('a\r\nb') == content_hash('a\nb')   # line endings normalized
True
>>> a = {'text': 'body', 'metadata': {'tags': ['x']}}
>>> b = {'text': 'body', 'metadata': {'tags': ['y']}}
>>> content_hash(a) == content_hash(b)                # metadata ignored by default
True
>>> content_hash(a, content_keys=['tags']) == content_hash(b, content_keys=['tags'])
False
>>> content_hash({'text': 'body'}) == content_hash('body')  # wrapper is transparent
True
```


# _autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md

# ef.diagnostics

Staleness diagnostics — has an indexed corpus drifted from its source?

Phase 5 wired `corpus → segment → embed → vd` and recorded provenance on
every `vd` document: `source_id`, `source_hash` and `config_hash` ride
in the document metadata (see `ef.source_manager._RESERVED_METADATA_KEYS`).
This module reads that provenance back and answers a single question — \*is the
index still a faithful picture of the corpus?\* — by computing the \*\*four
staleness conditions\*\* (`ef_use_cases.md` §C):

The detection is a set comparison, exactly as the design intends — the
`vd` collection is the single source of truth for *what is indexed*, the
corpus for *what should be indexed*, and the current
[`ConfigId`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.ConfigId) for *how*:

- `orphan` / `missing` partition the symmetric difference of the two id
  sets;
- `stale` compares each indexed source’s recorded `source_hash` against a
  freshly recomputed [`content_hash()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.content_hash);
- `misconfigured` compares each document’s recorded `config_hash` against
  the config being diagnosed.

This module is **read-only** — it never mutates the corpus, the collection or
the graph. Acting on a [`StalenessReport`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.StalenessReport) is [`ef.refresh`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#module-ef.refresh)’s job.

Example — diagnose a config whose corpus has since drifted:

```pycon
>>> from ef import SourceManager
>>> sm = SourceManager({'a': 'alpha', 'b': 'beta'}, embedder='hashing')
>>> _ = sm.materialize()
>>> sm.corpus['b'] = 'beta changed'          # an edit, behind the index's back
>>> sm.corpus['c'] = 'gamma'                 # a brand-new source
>>> del sm.corpus['a']                       # and a deletion
>>> report = sm.diagnose()
>>> report.orphan, report.missing, report.stale
(('a',), ('c',), ('b',))
>>> bool(report)                             # True — the index has drifted
True
```

### Functions

| [`indexed_state`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.indexed_state)(collection)            | Group a `vd` collection's documents by source — its recorded state.     |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`corpus_state`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.corpus_state)(corpus)                 | The current content hash of every source in `corpus`.                   |
| [`diagnose`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.diagnose)(corpus, collection, config) | Compute the four staleness conditions of `collection` against `corpus`. |

### Classes

| [`IndexedSource`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.IndexedSource)(source_id, doc_ids, ...)          | The provenance a `vd` collection records for one source document.                                                       |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`StalenessReport`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.StalenessReport)(config[, orphan, missing, ...]) | The four staleness conditions of one config — what [`diagnose()`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.diagnose) returns. |

### *class* ef.diagnostics.IndexedSource(source_id, doc_ids, source_hashes, config_hashes)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The provenance a `vd` collection records for one source document.

A source is segmented into several documents; they all carry the same
`source_id` and *should* carry one `source_hash` / `config_hash` each.
[`indexed_state()`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.indexed_state) groups a collection’s documents into one of these per
source — collecting the hashes as **sets** so a partially re-indexed source
(documents disagreeing on a hash) is detectable rather than papered over.

#### source_id

the corpus key of the source these documents were cut from.

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### doc_ids

the ids of every `vd` document belonging to the source.

* **Type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis)]

#### source_hashes

the distinct `source_hash` values its documents record
— a single-element set for a cleanly indexed source.

* **Type:**
  [`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### config_hashes

likewise the distinct `config_hash` values.

* **Type:**
  [`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### *class* ef.diagnostics.StalenessReport(config, orphan=(), missing=(), stale=(), misconfigured=(), fresh=())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The four staleness conditions of one config — what [`diagnose()`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.diagnose) returns.

Each field is a sorted tuple of `source_id`s, so a report is
deterministic and JSON-friendly. `orphan` and `missing` are disjoint
from the rest (a source absent from one side cannot also be compared); a
source can be **both** `stale` and `misconfigured` (its content changed
*and* the config did) — the conditions are reported independently.
`fresh` is the complement: indexed, current and built by this config.

Truthiness reports whether *anything is wrong* — `bool(report)` is
`False` only for a perfectly in-sync index.

```pycon
>>> r = StalenessReport(config='c0', stale=('a',), fresh=('b',))
>>> bool(r), r.needs_reindexing
(True, ('a',))
>>> bool(StalenessReport(config='c0', fresh=('a', 'b')))
False
```

#### *property* needs_reindexing *: [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), ...]*

Sources whose vectors must be recomputed — `stale` ∪ `misconfigured`.

### ef.diagnostics.corpus_state(corpus)

The current content hash of every source in `corpus`.

The *what should be indexed* half of [`diagnose()`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.diagnose): a fresh
[`content_hash()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.content_hash) per source — recomputed, not read from any
registry, so it reflects out-of-band edits to the backing store. It matches
the `source_hash` [`SourceManager`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager) writes into
`vd` (both are `content_hash` of the source with no `content_keys`).

```pycon
>>> sorted(corpus_state({'a': 'one', 'b': 'two'}))
['a', 'b']
>>> corpus_state({'a': 'x'})['a'] == corpus_state({'a': 'x'})['a']
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### ef.diagnostics.diagnose(corpus, collection, config)

Compute the four staleness conditions of `collection` against `corpus`.

The pure core of `ef`’s diagnostics — no side effects. It reads what the
`vd` `collection` records ([`indexed_state()`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.indexed_state)), what the `corpus`
currently holds ([`corpus_state()`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.corpus_state)), and partitions every source id into
exactly the buckets it belongs in:

- **orphan** — in the collection, not in the corpus;
- **missing** — in the corpus, not in the collection;
- **stale** — in both, but the recorded `source_hash` ≠ the current one;
- **misconfigured** — in both, but a recorded `config_hash` ≠ `config`;
- **fresh** — in both, content current and config matching.

* **Parameters:**
  * **corpus** ([`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]] | [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]) – the source corpus.
  * **collection** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – the `vd` collection backing the config being diagnosed.
  * **config** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the [`ConfigId`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.ConfigId) the collection *should* hold
    — documents recording any other `config_hash` are misconfigured.
* **Return type:**
  [`StalenessReport`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.StalenessReport)
* **Returns:**
  a [`StalenessReport`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.StalenessReport).

### ef.diagnostics.indexed_state(collection)

Group a `vd` collection’s documents by source — its recorded state.

Iterates the collection (a `MutableMapping` of `vd` documents) and
folds every document `ef` wrote into an [`IndexedSource`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.IndexedSource) keyed by
its `source_id`. Documents with no `source_id` metadata (not written by
`ef`) are skipped. This is the *what is indexed* half of [`diagnose()`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.diagnose).

* **Parameters:**
  **collection** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – the `vd` collection backing one config.
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`IndexedSource`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.IndexedSource)]
* **Returns:**
  a `{source_id: IndexedSource}` mapping.


# _autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md

# ef.embedder_adapters

Concrete [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder) adapters and the DI seam.

Adapters are **lazily-imported factory functions** — heavy dependencies
(`openai`, `sentence-transformers`) are imported inside the factory, never
at module load, and live in optional extras. Importing this module costs only
numpy + the stdlib.

- [`openai_embedder()`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.openai_embedder) — OpenAI embeddings (sync + the async Batch API).
  Needs `ef[openai]`.
- [`sentence_transformers_embedder()`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.sentence_transformers_embedder) — local PyTorch models. Needs
  `ef[sentence-transformers]`.
- [`http_embedder()`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.http_embedder) — any remote HTTP embedding service (TEI, infinity,
  …). Stdlib-only.
- [`cohere_embedder()`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.cohere_embedder), [`voyage_embedder()`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.voyage_embedder), [`gemini_embedder()`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.gemini_embedder) —
  the Cohere / Voyage / Gemini hosted embedding APIs, spoken over their REST
  endpoints directly. Stdlib-only (no SDK dependency); each needs only an API
  key. The whole point of these adapters is translating the canonical
  [`InputType`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.InputType) vocabulary to the vendor’s own task name.
- [`as_embedder()`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.as_embedder) — the single dependency-injection seam: turns a string
  (model name / `openai:` / `cohere:` / `voyage:` / `gemini:` prefix /
  URL), a bare callable, or an existing embedder into an
  [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder).

The **canonical task vocabulary** ([`InputType`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.InputType)) is
translated to each vendor’s own name *at the adapter boundary* — that
translation is the whole point of having adapters.

Example — the DI seam in action (no network / no heavy deps needed):

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from ef.embedders import Embedder
>>> e = as_embedder(lambda ts: np.ones((len(ts), 5)), model_id='ones@5')
>>> isinstance(e, Embedder)
True
>>> e(['x', 'y']).shape
(2, 5)
>>> as_embedder(e) is e          # an Embedder passes straight through
True
```

### Functions

| [`openai_embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.openai_embedder)([model, dim, api_key, ...])       | Build an OpenAI-embeddings [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder).          |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`sentence_transformers_embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.sentence_transformers_embedder)([model_name, ...]) | Build a local sentence-transformers [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder). |
| [`http_embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.http_embedder)(url, \*[, model_id, dim, ...])      | Build an [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder) over a remote HTTP service. |
| [`cohere_embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.cohere_embedder)([model, dim, api_key, ...])       | Build a Cohere-embeddings [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder).           |
| [`voyage_embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.voyage_embedder)([model, dim, api_key, ...])       | Build a Voyage AI [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder).                   |
| [`gemini_embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.gemini_embedder)([model, dim, api_key, ...])       | Build a Google Gemini [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder).               |
| [`as_embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.as_embedder)(x, \*\*kwargs)                        | Normalize `x` into an [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder) — the DI seam. |

### ef.embedder_adapters.as_embedder(x, \*\*kwargs)

Normalize `x` into an [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder) — the DI seam.

The single place every `ef` entry point coerces a user-supplied embedder
argument. Accepts, in order:

1. an existing [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder) — returned unchanged;
2. a URL string (`http://` / `https://`) — [`http_embedder()`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.http_embedder);
3. a provider-prefixed string — `"openai:<model>"`, `"cohere:<model>"`,
   `"voyage:<model>"` or `"gemini:<model>"` — the matching hosted-API
   adapter;
4. the bare string `"hashing"` — the dependency-free
   [`HashingEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.HashingEmbedder) (`ef`’s zero-install default);
5. an `"st:<model>"` string, or any other bare model name —
   [`sentence_transformers_embedder()`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.sentence_transformers_embedder) (the local neural default);
6. a bare callable — wrapped in
   [`FunctionEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.FunctionEmbedder) (the `imbed`-embedder bridge).

Extra `**kwargs` are forwarded to the chosen factory.

* **Raises:**
  [**TypeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#TypeError) – if `x` is none of the above.
* **Return type:**
  [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder)

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> e = as_embedder(lambda ts: np.zeros((len(ts), 2)), model_id='zero@2')
>>> type(e).__name__
'FunctionEmbedder'
```

### ef.embedder_adapters.cohere_embedder(model='embed-v4.0', , dim=None, api_key=None, batch_size=96, timeout=60.0)

Build a Cohere-embeddings [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder).

Talks to Cohere’s `/v2/embed` REST endpoint directly — no `cohere` SDK,
no extra dependency. Cohere’s v3+ models *require* a task hint; this adapter
supplies one for every canonical [`InputType`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.InputType) and
defaults to the document role when none is given.

* **Parameters:**
  * **model** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – A Cohere embedding model name.
  * **dim** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Matryoshka-truncated width (`embed-v4.0` only). Omit for the
    model’s native width. The dim is part of the embedder’s identity —
    set it once here, not per call.
  * **api_key** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Cohere API key. Falls back to `CO_API_KEY` / `COHERE_API_KEY`.
  * **batch_size** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Texts per request (capped at Cohere’s 96 limit).
  * **timeout** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Per-request timeout in seconds.
* **Return type:**
  [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder)
* **Returns:**
  An [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder) over the Cohere API.

### ef.embedder_adapters.gemini_embedder(model='gemini-embedding-001', , dim=None, api_key=None, batch_size=100, timeout=60.0)

Build a Google Gemini [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder).

Talks to the Generative Language `batchEmbedContents` REST endpoint
directly — no `google-genai` SDK, no extra dependency.

* **Parameters:**
  * **model** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – A Gemini embedding model name (a leading `models/` is
    tolerated and stripped).
  * **dim** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Matryoshka-truncated width (`gemini-embedding-001` only). Omit
    for the model’s native width. Note that Gemini, unlike OpenAI, does
    *not* re-normalize MRL-truncated output — a truncated embedder
    therefore reports `normalized=False`.
  * **api_key** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Gemini API key. Falls back to `GEMINI_API_KEY` /
    `GOOGLE_API_KEY`.
  * **batch_size** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Texts per request (capped at Gemini’s 100 limit).
  * **timeout** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Per-request timeout in seconds.
* **Return type:**
  [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder)
* **Returns:**
  An [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder) over the Gemini API.

### ef.embedder_adapters.http_embedder(url, \*, model_id=None, dim=None, normalized=False, batch_size=64, headers=None, timeout=30.0, payload_builder=<function \_tei_payload>, response_parser=<function \_tei_parse>)

Build an [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder) over a remote HTTP service.

Defaults target the Text-Embeddings-Inference / infinity shape (a POST of
`{"inputs": [...]}` returning a JSON list of vectors). For a different
service, override `payload_builder` and/or `response_parser`.

* **Parameters:**
  * **url** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The embedding endpoint.
  * **model_id** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Vector-identity string (defaults to `"http:<url>"`).
  * **dim** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Output width; inferred from the first response if omitted.
  * **normalized** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Whether the service returns unit vectors.
  * **batch_size** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Texts per request (used with length-sorted batching).
  * **headers** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Extra HTTP headers (e.g. an auth token).
  * **timeout** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Per-request timeout in seconds.
  * **payload_builder** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]], [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)]) – `texts -> request body bytes`.
  * **response_parser** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)], [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]) – `decoded JSON -> array-like (n, dim)`.
* **Return type:**
  [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder)

Uses only the stdlib — no extra dependency.

### ef.embedder_adapters.openai_embedder(model='text-embedding-3-small', , dim=None, api_key=None, client=None, batch_size=2048, poll_interval=30.0)

Build an OpenAI-embeddings [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder).

* **Parameters:**
  * **model** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – An OpenAI embedding model name.
  * **dim** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Matryoshka-truncated output width (`text-embedding-3-*` only).
    Omit for the model’s native dimension. The dim is part of the
    embedder’s identity — set it once here, not per call.
  * **api_key** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – OpenAI API key (else the SDK’s usual env-var resolution).
  * **client** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – A pre-built `openai.OpenAI` client (overrides `api_key`).
  * **batch_size** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Texts per request (capped at OpenAI’s 2048 limit).
  * **poll_interval** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Seconds between polls when blocking on a Batch-API job.
* **Return type:**
  [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder)
* **Returns:**
  An embedder whose `embed_batch` uses the async OpenAI Batch API.

Requires the `openai` package (`pip install 'ef[openai]'`).

### ef.embedder_adapters.sentence_transformers_embedder(model_name='all-MiniLM-L6-v2', , device=None, normalize=False, batch_size=128, model_path=None, query_prompt=None, document_prompt=None, prompt_names=None, \*\*st_kwargs)

Build a local sentence-transformers [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder).

Instruction-tuned models (bge, gte, e5-instruct, Qwen3-Embedding…) are
conditioned per `input_type`: pass a literal `query_prompt` (and, rarely,
`document_prompt`), or map input types to prompts the model defines itself
with `prompt_names` (e.g. `{"query": "query"}` for Qwen3-Embedding). Those
roles are then advertised in `honored_input_types`, and the prompt text is
baked into `model_id`. Only trust prompts on genuinely instruction-tuned
models; on `all-MiniLM` they are expected to be a near no-op. Prefer these
over wrapping the adapter in [`InstructionEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md#ef.embedder_wrappers.InstructionEmbedder):
sentence-transformers knows the prompt’s length, so models that pool without
the prompt tokens (INSTRUCTOR, GRIT) stay correct. Needs
sentence-transformers >= 2.3.

* **Parameters:**
  * **model_name** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – A sentence-transformers model name (also used in
    `model_id`).
  * **device** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Torch device (`"cuda"` / `"cpu"` / `"mps"`); `None`
    auto-selects.
  * **normalize** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Whether to L2-normalize outputs. sentence-transformers does
    **not** normalize by default — set this truthfully.
  * **batch_size** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Encoding batch size (smaller on CPU).
  * **model_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – A local filesystem path to load from instead of the hub —
    for air-gapped use. Loading still records `model_name` in
    `model_id`.
  * **query_prompt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Prompt prepended to `input_type="query"` texts (passed
    as `encode(prompt=...)`).
  * **document_prompt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Prompt for `input_type="document"` texts (usually
    none: the asymmetric pattern leaves documents bare). `""` means an
    explicit empty prompt, which stops a model’s `default_prompt_name`
    from being applied to documents.
  * **prompt_names** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – `{input_type: name}` of prompts defined in the model’s
    own `prompts` config (passed as `encode(prompt_name=...)`).
    An explicit `prompt=` / `prompt_name=` in a call overrides both.
  * **\*\*st_kwargs** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – Forwarded to the `SentenceTransformer` constructor.
* **Return type:**
  [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder)

Requires `sentence-transformers` (`pip install 'ef[sentence-transformers]'`).

### ef.embedder_adapters.voyage_embedder(model='voyage-3.5', , dim=None, api_key=None, batch_size=1000, timeout=60.0)

Build a Voyage AI [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder).

Talks to Voyage’s `/v1/embeddings` REST endpoint directly — no
`voyageai` SDK, no extra dependency. Voyage embeddings are L2-normalized.
Voyage distinguishes only `query` from `document`; a `classification`
or `clustering` hint is simply not sent.

* **Parameters:**
  * **model** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – A Voyage embedding model name.
  * **dim** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Matryoshka-truncated width (the `voyage-3.5` family and
    `voyage-code-3` only). Omit for the model’s native width.
  * **api_key** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Voyage API key. Falls back to `VOYAGE_API_KEY`.
  * **batch_size** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Texts per request (capped at Voyage’s 1000 limit).
  * **timeout** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Per-request timeout in seconds.
* **Return type:**
  [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder)
* **Returns:**
  An [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder) over the Voyage API.


# _autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md

# ef.embedder_wrappers

Composition wrappers for [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder).

Each wrapper *takes an inner embedder and is itself an embedder* — they compose
freely (`CachedEmbedder(RetryingEmbedder(NormalizingEmbedder(inner)), store)`).
This keeps the core protocol tiny: caching, retries, routing and normalization
are opt-in layers, not protocol obligations.

- [`CachedEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md#ef.embedder_wrappers.CachedEmbedder) — memoize vectors in any `MutableMapping` store.
- [`RetryingEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md#ef.embedder_wrappers.RetryingEmbedder) — exponential backoff + jitter, retryable-aware.
- [`MultiEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md#ef.embedder_wrappers.MultiEmbedder) — route texts to different embedders by a predicate.
- [`NormalizingEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md#ef.embedder_wrappers.NormalizingEmbedder) — L2-normalize an inner embedder’s output.
- [`InstructionEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md#ef.embedder_wrappers.InstructionEmbedder) — prepend a per-`input_type` instruction
  (task-conditioned, asymmetric query/document embedding).

They delegate their metadata (`model_id` / `dim` / `normalized` /
`honored_input_types`) to the inner embedder, except where the wrapper changes
the vector ([`NormalizingEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md#ef.embedder_wrappers.NormalizingEmbedder) reports `normalized=True`;
[`InstructionEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md#ef.embedder_wrappers.InstructionEmbedder) bakes its instructions into `model_id` and adds the
conditioned roles to `honored_input_types`).

The inner argument must already be an [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder); use
[`ef.embedder_adapters.as_embedder()`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.as_embedder) to coerce a string / callable first.

Example — cache an embedder so repeats are free:

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from ef.embedders import FunctionEmbedder
>>> calls = []
>>> def toy(texts):
...     calls.extend(texts)
...     return np.ones((len(texts), 3))
>>> cached = CachedEmbedder(FunctionEmbedder(toy, model_id='toy@3'), store={})
>>> _ = cached(['a', 'b'])
>>> _ = cached(['b', 'c'])   # 'b' served from cache
>>> calls                    # 'b' embedded once
['a', 'b', 'c']
```

### Classes

| [`CachedEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md#ef.embedder_wrappers.CachedEmbedder)(inner, store, \*[, cache_queries])   | Memoize embeddings in a `MutableMapping` store.                                                         |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`RetryPolicy`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md#ef.embedder_wrappers.RetryPolicy)([max_attempts, base_delay, ...])        | Exponential-backoff retry policy for [`RetryingEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md#ef.embedder_wrappers.RetryingEmbedder). |
| [`RetryingEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md#ef.embedder_wrappers.RetryingEmbedder)(inner[, policy, sleep])            | Retry an inner embedder's calls on transient failures.                                                  |
| [`MultiEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md#ef.embedder_wrappers.MultiEmbedder)(routes, predicate, \*[, default])     | Route each text to one of several embedders by a predicate.                                             |
| [`NormalizingEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md#ef.embedder_wrappers.NormalizingEmbedder)(inner)                          | L2-normalize an inner embedder's output.                                                                |
| [`InstructionEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md#ef.embedder_wrappers.InstructionEmbedder)(inner, \*[, ...])               | Prepend a per-`input_type` instruction before delegating to `inner`.                                    |

### *class* ef.embedder_wrappers.CachedEmbedder(inner, store, , cache_queries=False)

Bases: [`BaseEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.BaseEmbedder)

Memoize embeddings in a `MutableMapping` store.

On each call, texts already in the store are served from it; only the misses
are forwarded to the inner embedder (in a single batch) and then written
back. The store can be any `dol`-style mapping — an in-RAM `dict`, a
directory of `.npy` files, a key-value DB.

Document embeddings are cached unconditionally; *query* embeddings are
skipped by default (they are rarely repeated) — pass `cache_queries=True`
to cache them too.

* **Parameters:**
  * **inner** ([`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder)) – The embedder to memoize.
  * **store** ([`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.MutableMapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), `ndarray`]) – A `MutableMapping[str, ndarray]` keyed by `cache_key()`.
  * **cache_queries** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Whether to also cache `input_type="query"` calls.

#### *property* honored_input_types *: [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)['query', 'document', 'classification', 'clustering'], ...]*

If iterable is specified the tuple is initialized from iterable’s items.

If the argument is a tuple, the return value is the same object.

#### *property* normalized *: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*

bool(x) -> bool

Returns True when the argument x is true, False otherwise.

### *class* ef.embedder_wrappers.InstructionEmbedder(inner, , query_instruction=None, document_instruction=None, classification_instruction=None, clustering_instruction=None)

Bases: [`BaseEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.BaseEmbedder)

Prepend a per-`input_type` instruction before delegating to `inner`.

Instruction-tuned embedding models (E5-instruct, BGE, GTE, Qwen3-Embedding…)
are trained to read a task description in front of the text, typically on the
*query* side only, with documents embedded bare. That asymmetry is where the
gain comes from: the query says *what kind of relevance* is wanted (topic vs.
keyword), which a plain model cannot be told. This wrapper adds that to any
embedder: a text embedded with `input_type="query"` becomes
`query_instruction + text`, and so on per role. Roles without an instruction
(and calls with `input_type=None`) pass through unchanged.

**Only trust the prefix on a genuinely instruction-tuned model.** On a plain
model (e.g. `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`) the prefix is expected to be a near no-op or
noise: use that as the control arm of an experiment, not as an improvement.

The instruction strings are used verbatim, so include the model’s expected
separator (e.g. `"Instruct: ...\nQuery: "` for Qwen3/E5-instruct,
`"Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: "` for BGE).

Metadata:

- `model_id` bakes in a digest of the instructions (they change the vector),
  so [`CachedEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md#ef.embedder_wrappers.CachedEmbedder) and content-addressed artifacts never mix vectors
  made with different instructions.
- `honored_input_types` is the inner embedder’s plus every instructed role.
- `input_type` is still forwarded to `inner`; a backend that also acts on
  it natively (Cohere, Voyage, Gemini, or a sentence-transformers adapter
  built with `query_prompt=`) would then be conditioned twice, so use this
  wrapper for backends that ignore the hint. For sentence-transformers models
  prefer the adapter’s own `query_prompt=`.

* **Parameters:**
  * **inner** ([`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder)) – The embedder to condition.
  * **query_instruction** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Prefix for `input_type="query"`.
  * **document_instruction** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Prefix for `input_type="document"` (usually none).
  * **classification_instruction** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Prefix for `input_type="classification"`.
  * **clustering_instruction** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Prefix for `input_type="clustering"`.

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from ef.embedders import FunctionEmbedder
>>> seen = []
>>> def toy(texts):
...     seen.extend(texts)
...     return np.ones((len(texts), 2))
>>> base = FunctionEmbedder(toy, model_id='toy@2')
>>> emb = InstructionEmbedder(base, query_instruction='Find packages about: ')
>>> _ = emb(['graphs'], input_type='query')
>>> _ = emb(['a DAG library'], input_type='document')
>>> seen
['Find packages about: graphs', 'a DAG library']
>>> emb.honored_input_types
('query',)
>>> emb.model_id.startswith('toy@2+instruct:')
True
```

#### embed_batch(texts, , input_type=None, \*\*backend)

Prefix, then use the inner embedder’s own (possibly async) batch API.

#### *property* honored_input_types *: [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)['query', 'document', 'classification', 'clustering'], ...]*

The inner embedder’s honored roles plus every instructed role.

#### *property* model_id *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*

The inner `model_id` plus a digest of the instructions.

#### *property* normalized *: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*

bool(x) -> bool

Returns True when the argument x is true, False otherwise.
The builtins True and False are the only two instances of the class bool.
The class bool is a subclass of the class int, and cannot be subclassed.

### *class* ef.embedder_wrappers.MultiEmbedder(routes, predicate, , default=None)

Bases: [`BaseEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.BaseEmbedder)

Route each text to one of several embedders by a predicate.

Useful for domain-specific models (e.g. a code embedder for code, a prose
embedder for prose). All routes must share the same `dim` — the output is
a single `(n, dim)` array, with each row produced by its text’s route.

* **Parameters:**
  * **routes** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Mapping)[[`Hashable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Hashable), [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder)]) – `{route_key: Embedder}`.
  * **predicate** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Hashable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Hashable)]) – `text -> route_key` — picks a route per text.
  * **default** ([`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Embedder for texts whose `route_key` is not in `routes`
    (otherwise an unknown key raises `EmbedderError`).

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from ef.embedders import FunctionEmbedder
>>> short = FunctionEmbedder(lambda ts: np.zeros((len(ts), 2)), model_id='s@2')
>>> long = FunctionEmbedder(lambda ts: np.ones((len(ts), 2)), model_id='l@2')
>>> m = MultiEmbedder({'s': short, 'l': long},
...                   predicate=lambda t: 's' if len(t) < 4 else 'l')
>>> m(['hi', 'hello']).tolist()
[[0.0, 0.0], [1.0, 1.0]]
```

### *class* ef.embedder_wrappers.NormalizingEmbedder(inner)

Bases: [`BaseEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.BaseEmbedder)

L2-normalize an inner embedder’s output.

Use this for MRL-truncated vectors (which lose unit norm when sliced to a
smaller dimension) or any backend that does not normalize by construction.
Reports `normalized=True`; `cache_key()` keys on `normalized`, so a
normalized and an un-normalized view of the same model never collide in a
shared cache.

* **Parameters:**
  **inner** ([`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder)) – The embedder whose output to renormalize.

#### *property* honored_input_types *: [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)['query', 'document', 'classification', 'clustering'], ...]*

Built-in immutable sequence.

If no argument is given, the constructor returns an empty tuple.
If iterable is specified the tuple is initialized from iterable’s items.

If the argument is a tuple, the return value is the same object.

### *class* ef.embedder_wrappers.RetryPolicy(max_attempts=4, base_delay=1.0, max_delay=30.0, jitter=0.3, retry_on=<function \_default_is_retryable>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Exponential-backoff retry policy for [`RetryingEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md#ef.embedder_wrappers.RetryingEmbedder).

#### max_attempts

Total tries (the first call counts as attempt 1).

* **Type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

#### base_delay

Seconds before the first retry; doubles each attempt.

* **Type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

#### max_delay

Upper bound on any single backoff sleep.

* **Type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

#### jitter

Random fraction (`0..1`) of the delay added on top, to
de-correlate concurrent clients.

* **Type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

#### retry_on

Predicate deciding whether an exception is worth retrying.

* **Type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`BaseException`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#BaseException)], [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)]
* **Return type:**
  [*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

#### retry_on()

Heuristic: retry transient failures (429, 5xx, connection/timeout).

Per-request 400-class errors are *not* retried — the same request would fail
identically. Recognizes the `status_code`/`status` attribute carried by
most HTTP-client SDK exceptions (incl. the OpenAI SDK).

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

# _autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md

# ef.embedders

The `Embedder` facade — `ef`’s embed layer (L3).

An *embedder* is, fundamentally, a batch callable:

```default
Iterable[str] -> ndarray of shape (n, dim)
```

Everything else — batching, async/batch-APIs, normalization, task hints,
caching, retries — is *layered scaffolding* over that one contract.

This module defines the small, structural core of the facade:

- [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder) — the `@runtime_checkable` protocol (a callable plus four
  introspectable metadata attributes). It is a protocol, **not** an ABC: any
  object with the right shape *is* an embedder.
- [`BatchHandle`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.BatchHandle) / [`ready_handle()`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.ready_handle) — a uniform poll/result shape that
  collapses synchronous embedding and provider Batch APIs into one thing.
- [`BaseEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.BaseEmbedder) — an implementation convenience base (supplies a default
  synchronous [`embed_batch()`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.BaseEmbedder.embed_batch) and a `repr`). Subclassing it
  is optional; satisfying [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder) structurally is what matters.
- [`FunctionEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.FunctionEmbedder) — wraps a bare `texts -> vectors` callable into a
  full [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder) (the bridge for e.g. `imbed`’s embedder functions).
- [`HashingEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.HashingEmbedder) — a dependency-free embedder (the feature-hashing
  trick, numpy only); `ef`’s zero-install default when no embedder is given.
- [`cache_key()`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.cache_key) — a deterministic key pinning everything that changes a
  vector, for [`CachedEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md#ef.embedder_wrappers.CachedEmbedder).
- [`embed_length_sorted()`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.embed_length_sorted) — length-sorted batching with order
  reconstruction; a 5–10× throughput win that `ef` owns so users never have
  to think about padding or sort order.

Composition wrappers live in [`ef.embedder_wrappers`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md#module-ef.embedder_wrappers); concrete provider /
local adapters and the [`as_embedder()`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.as_embedder) dependency
-injection seam live in [`ef.embedder_adapters`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#module-ef.embedder_adapters).

Example — wrap a plain function and embed two strings:

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> def toy(texts):  # a bare callable: list[str] -> array(n, 3)
...     return np.array([[len(t), t.count(' '), 1.0] for t in texts])
>>> embedder = FunctionEmbedder(toy, model_id='toy@3')
>>> vectors = embedder(['hello', 'a b c'])
>>> vectors.shape
(2, 3)
>>> embedder.dim  # inferred on first call
3
>>> isinstance(embedder, Embedder)
True
```

### *class* ef.embedders.BaseEmbedder

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Implementation base for embedders (optional — [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder) is structural).

Subclasses set `model_id` / `dim` / `normalized` /
`honored_input_types` and implement `__call__`; they then satisfy
[`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder) structurally. In return they get:

- a default *synchronous* [`embed_batch()`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.BaseEmbedder.embed_batch) (`ready_handle(self(...))`) —
  override it only for a genuinely async provider Batch API;
- a readable `repr`.

#### embed_batch(texts, , input_type=None, \*\*backend)

Default: embed synchronously and return a finished handle.

* **Return type:**
  [`BatchHandle`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.BatchHandle)

### *class* ef.embedders.BatchHandle(poll, result, cancel=<function BatchHandle.<lambda>>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A poll/result handle over an in-flight (or already-finished) embed job.

Batch-and-poll is just a special case of async. A synchronous backend
returns a *ready* handle (via [`ready_handle()`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.ready_handle)); a provider Batch API
returns a genuinely pending one. Either way the caller sees one shape.

#### poll

`() -> BatchStatus` — non-blocking status check.

* **Type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[], [`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[`'pending'`, `'done'`, `'failed'`]]

#### result

`() -> np.ndarray` — blocks until done, returns `(n, dim)`.

* **Type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[], `ndarray`]

#### cancel

`() -> None` — best-effort cancellation.

* **Type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[], [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]

alias of [`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[‘pending’, ‘done’, ‘failed’]

### *class* ef.embedders.Embedder(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

Structural type for an embedder: a batch callable plus metadata.

An embedder maps `Iterable[str]` to an `ndarray` of shape `(n, dim)`.
The four metadata attributes are the single source of truth \*on the object
itself\* — no global registry, no config singleton.

#### model_id

Identity that bakes in everything affecting the vector —
`"openai:text-embedding-3-large@1024"` (`provider:model@dim`).
Works directly as a cache namespace.

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### dim

Output dimensionality. May be `None` until first call for
lazily-probed embedders (e.g. a bare callable of unknown width).

* **Type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### normalized

`True` iff `||v|| == 1` by construction.

* **Type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

#### honored_input_types

The [`InputType`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.InputType) values this embedder acts on
(empty if it ignores the task hint).

* **Type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[`'query'`, `'document'`, `'classification'`, `'clustering'`], [`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis)]

#### embed_batch(texts, , input_type=None, \*\*backend)

Submit an embed job, returning a [`BatchHandle`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.BatchHandle).

* **Return type:**
  [`BatchHandle`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.BatchHandle)

### *class* ef.embedders.FunctionEmbedder(func, , model_id=None, dim=None, normalized=False, honored_input_types=(), pass_backend=True)

Bases: [`BaseEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.BaseEmbedder)

Promote a bare `texts -> vectors` callable to a full [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder).

This is the bridge for embedder *functions* that carry no metadata — most
importantly `imbed`’s registered embedders. The wrapped callable is asked
only for `func(texts)` (it knows nothing of `input_type`); the wrapper
advertises `honored_input_types=()` accordingly.

* **Parameters:**
  * **func** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]) – A callable mapping a list of strings to an array-like of shape
    `(n, dim)` (a numpy array or a nested sequence — both accepted).
  * **model_id** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Vector-identity string. Defaults to `"function:<name>"`.
  * **dim** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Output width. If `None` it is inferred (and frozen) on the first
    call.
  * **normalized** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Whether `func` already returns unit vectors.
  * **honored_input_types** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[`'query'`, `'document'`, `'classification'`, `'clustering'`]]) – Task hints `func` honors (usually none).
  * **pass_backend** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – If `True` (default), forward any `**backend` kwargs to
    `func`; set `False` for callables with a strict `(texts,)`
    signature.

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> e = FunctionEmbedder(lambda ts: np.ones((len(ts), 4)), model_id='ones@4')
>>> e(['a', 'b', 'c']).shape
(3, 4)
```

### *class* ef.embedders.HashingEmbedder(, dim=512, ngram_range=(1, 2), sublinear_tf=True)

Bases: [`BaseEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.BaseEmbedder)

A dependency-free embedder — the feature-hashing trick, numpy only.

[`HashingEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.HashingEmbedder) is `ef`’s **zero-install default**: the embedder
[`ingest()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.ingest) resolves to when none is given, so the
headline `ingest([...]).search(query)` works on a bare `pip install ef`
— no torch, no model download, no network.

It is a *lexical* embedder, not a neural one. Each text is tokenized into
lowercased word n-grams; every token is hashed into one of `dim` buckets
with a sign (the hashing trick — no vocabulary, no fitting, fixed memory);
the signed, sublinear-tf-weighted bucket counts are L2-normalized. The
cosine similarity of two vectors then ranks by shared vocabulary — enough
for demos, doctests and offline tests, and a sane fallback in production.
For genuine semantic quality install a real embedder (`ef[sentence-transformers]`,
`ef[openai]`) and pass it explicitly.

Every parameter that changes a vector is baked into `model_id`, so a
[`HashingEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.HashingEmbedder)’s artifacts stay correctly content-addressed in the
[`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph).

* **Parameters:**
  * **dim** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Output width. Wider → fewer hash collisions, larger vectors.
  * **ngram_range** ([`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]) – Inclusive `(min, max)` word-n-gram sizes. The default
    `(1, 2)` mixes single words with adjacent pairs — a little phrase
    sensitivity at no real cost.
  * **sublinear_tf** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Weight a token by `1 + log(count)` rather than its raw
    `count`, damping a word repeated many times in one text.

```pycon
>>> e = HashingEmbedder()
>>> e.model_id
'hashing:v1@512'
>>> import numpy as np
>>> v = e(['the quick brown fox'])
>>> v.shape
(1, 512)
>>> bool(np.isclose(np.linalg.norm(v[0]), 1.0))  # rows are L2-normalized
True
>>> a, b = e(['hello world']), e(['hello world'])
>>> round(float(a[0] @ b[0]), 5)  # identical text → cosine similarity 1.0
1.0
>>> isinstance(e, Embedder)
True
```

### ef.embedders.InputType

Canonical embedding-task vocabulary. Every provider names the same
distinction differently (`input_type` / `task_type` / `task` /
`prompt_name`); `ef` defines *one* canonical set and each adapter
translates it at its boundary. This is the facade’s single most valuable
normalization. Backends that ignore the hint advertise an empty
`honored_input_types`.

alias of [`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[‘query’, ‘document’, ‘classification’, ‘clustering’]

### ef.embedders.cache_key(embedder, text, input_type=None)

Deterministic cache key for one `(embedder, text, input_type)` triple.

The key pins everything that changes the resulting vector. `model_id` is
the embedder-identity SSOT — it already bakes in provider, model and `dim`
— so `dim` is *not* keyed separately (keying it would also break
[`FunctionEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.FunctionEmbedder)’s lazy `dim` inference). `normalized` is keyed
because a [`NormalizingEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md#ef.embedder_wrappers.NormalizingEmbedder) shares its
inner’s `model_id` yet yields different vectors.

Returns `"<model_id>/<sha256>"` — a namespaced key safe for any
`MutableMapping` store.

```pycon
>>> class _E:
...     model_id, normalized = 'm@8', False
>>> k1 = cache_key(_E(), 'hello', 'document')
>>> k2 = cache_key(_E(), 'hello', 'query')
>>> k1 == k2  # input_type participates
False
>>> k1.startswith('m@8/')
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### ef.embedders.embed_length_sorted(texts, encode, , batch_size=128)

Encode `texts` in length-sorted batches; return vectors in caller order.

Transformer self-attention is O(n²) in sequence length and a batch is padded
to its longest member, so grouping similar-length texts together avoids
wasted compute — a 5–10× speedup on skewed corpora. `ef` owns this so
callers never sort, pad, or un-sort themselves.

* **Parameters:**
  * **texts** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – The strings to embed.
  * **encode** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]], [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]) – Maps a list of strings to an array-like of shape `(k, dim)`.
  * **batch_size** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Texts per call to `encode`.
* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`
* **Returns:**
  A `float32` array of shape `(len(texts), dim)` in the *original*
  order of `texts`.

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> def enc(batch):  # toy encoder: vector = [length]
...     return np.array([[len(t)] for t in batch], dtype=np.float32)
>>> out = embed_length_sorted(['aaa', 'a', 'aaaaa', 'aa'], enc, batch_size=2)
>>> out.ravel().tolist()  # order preserved despite internal sorting
[3.0, 1.0, 5.0, 2.0]
```

### ef.embedders.ready_handle(array)

Wrap an already-computed array in a finished [`BatchHandle`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.BatchHandle).

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> h = ready_handle(np.zeros((2, 3)))
>>> h.poll()
'done'
>>> h.result().shape
(2, 3)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`BatchHandle`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.BatchHandle)


# _autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md

# ef.evaluation

Evaluation hookpoints — measuring retrieval and RAG quality.

Phase 7 makes an indexed `ef` corpus **measurable**. It stays a *facade*: it
computes the standard, deterministic metrics and provides the standard data
shapes, but it never synthesizes an answer and never requires an LLM (the §6
boundary). LLM-judged metrics are reached through a thin Ragas bridge.

Two journeys (`ef_use_cases.md` §F7–F8), two evaluation conventions
(`ef_design_notes.md` §6):

- **Retrieval evaluation** — [`evaluate_retrieval()`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.evaluate_retrieval), BEIR/MTEB-shaped. The
  inputs are the BEIR triple — a corpus, a set of `queries` and `qrels`
  (graded relevance judgements) — and the primary metric is **NDCG@10**. The
  metric primitives ([`ndcg_at_k()`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.ndcg_at_k), [`recall_at_k()`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.recall_at_k), …) are pure
  functions, usable on their own. [`read_beir()`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.read_beir) / [`write_beir()`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.write_beir) move
  the triple to and from the on-disk `corpus.jsonl` / `queries.jsonl` /
  `qrels.tsv` format.
- **RAG evaluation** — [`evaluate_rag()`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.evaluate_rag), Ragas `SingleTurnSample`-shaped.
  A sample is `(user_input, response, retrieved_contexts, reference)`;
  [`RagSample`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.RagSample) names that shape. [`evaluate_rag()`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.evaluate_rag) computes only
  > **deterministic, reference-based lexical metrics** ([`exact_match()`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.exact_match),

  [`token_f1()`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.token_f1), [`context_recall()`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.context_recall), [`context_precision()`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.context_precision)) — no LLM.

  For the LLM-judged metrics (faithfulness, answer relevancy, …) hand the
  samples to [`as_ragas_dataset()`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.as_ragas_dataset) and run Ragas with your own LLM.

Example — score a retriever against a tiny BEIR-shaped triple:

```pycon
>>> qrels = {'q1': {'d1': 1.0, 'd2': 1.0}, 'q2': {'d3': 1.0}}
>>> queries = {'q1': 'first query', 'q2': 'second query'}
>>> rankings = {'first query': ['d1', 'd9', 'd2'], 'second query': ['d9', 'd3']}
>>> def retriever(query, *, limit=10):
...     return rankings[query][:limit]
>>> report = evaluate_retrieval(retriever, qrels, queries, k_values=(1, 3))
>>> report.metrics['recall@3']
1.0
>>> round(report.primary_at(1), 3)        # NDCG@1, averaged over the two queries
0.5
```

### *class* ef.evaluation.BenchmarkReport(rows, reports)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One row per embedder: its `{metric: value}` (plus an `embedder` key).

`reports` keeps each full [`RetrievalEvalReport`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.RetrievalEvalReport) for drill-down
(e.g. `distractor_hits`). `to_frame()` gives a pandas DataFrame
(pandas is imported lazily).

```pycon
>>> r = BenchmarkReport(rows=[{'embedder': 'a', 'ndcg@10': 0.5}], reports={})
>>> r.to_records()
[{'embedder': 'a', 'ndcg@10': 0.5}]
```

### ef.evaluation.Qrels

Graded relevance judgements — `{query_id: {doc_id: relevance}}`. A
`relevance` of `0` means *judged non-relevant*; `> 0` means relevant
(graded judgements feed [`ndcg_at_k()`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.ndcg_at_k), binary relevance the rest). This
is the in-memory form of a BEIR `qrels.tsv`.

alias of [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]]

### ef.evaluation.RETRIEVAL_METRICS *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [Mapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)], [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)], [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]]* *= {'map': <function average_precision>, 'mrr': <function reciprocal_rank>, 'ndcg': <function ndcg_at_k>, 'precision': <function precision_at_k>, 'recall': <function recall_at_k>}*

The retrieval metrics [`evaluate_retrieval()`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.evaluate_retrieval) can compute, each keyed by
the short name used in the `metrics=` argument and in report keys. Public
so downstream packages (e.g. `ir.eval`) can consume this single source of
truth — the name→function registry *and* the set of valid metric names —
instead of hand-mirroring it.

### *class* ef.evaluation.RagEvalReport(metrics, coverage, n_samples)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The outcome of [`evaluate_rag()`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.evaluate_rag) — lexical RAG metrics over a sample set.

`metrics` maps each metric to its mean over the samples it applied to;
`coverage` records how many samples that was (a metric needing a
`reference` skips samples without one). `n_samples` is the total scored.

```pycon
>>> report = RagEvalReport(
...     metrics={'exact_match': 0.5}, coverage={'exact_match': 4}, n_samples=4)
>>> report.metrics['exact_match']
0.5
```

### *class* ef.evaluation.RagSample

Bases: [`TypedDict`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.TypedDict)

One end-to-end RAG interaction — the unit [`evaluate_rag()`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.evaluate_rag) scores.

The field names match Ragas’ `SingleTurnSample` exactly, so a
[`RagSample`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.RagSample) is the interchange shape `app_ef` / `srag` / `raglab`
produce and [`as_ragas_dataset()`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.as_ragas_dataset) forwards unchanged. `ef` itself fills
only `retrieved_contexts` (from [`retrieve()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.retrieve));
`response` is the *caller’s* LLM output — `ef` does not synthesize it.

Keys:
: user_input: the user’s question.
  response: the generated answer (the caller’s LLM produced it).
  retrieved_contexts: the context passages handed to the LLM — what
  <br/>
  > [`retrieve()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.retrieve) returned, as text.
  <br/>
  reference: the ground-truth answer, if known.
  reference_contexts: the ground-truth context passages, if known.

### *class* ef.evaluation.RetrievalEvalReport(metrics, per_query, n_queries, k_values, distractor_hits=dict())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The outcome of [`evaluate_retrieval()`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.evaluate_retrieval) — metrics over a query set.

`metrics` maps a `"<name>@<k>"` key (e.g. `"ndcg@10"`) to the mean of
that metric over every scored query; `per_query` keeps the same keys per
query for drill-down. `n_queries` is how many queries were actually
scored (a query with no positive judgement is skipped).

```pycon
>>> report = RetrievalEvalReport(
...     metrics={'ndcg@10': 0.83}, per_query={}, n_queries=12, k_values=(10,))
>>> report.primary
0.83
```

#### distractor_hits *: [Mapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Mapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]]*
