  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### ef.openai_embedder(model='text-embedding-3-small', , dim=None, api_key=None, client=None, batch_size=2048, poll_interval=30.0)

Build an OpenAI-embeddings [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder).

* **Parameters:**
  * **model** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – An OpenAI embedding model name.
  * **dim** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Matryoshka-truncated output width (`text-embedding-3-*` only).
    Omit for the model’s native dimension. The dim is part of the
    embedder’s identity — set it once here, not per call.
  * **api_key** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – OpenAI API key (else the SDK’s usual env-var resolution).
  * **client** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – A pre-built `openai.OpenAI` client (overrides `api_key`).
  * **batch_size** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Texts per request (capped at OpenAI’s 2048 limit).
  * **poll_interval** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Seconds between polls when blocking on a Batch-API job.
* **Return type:**
  [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder)
* **Returns:**
  An embedder whose `embed_batch` uses the async OpenAI Batch API.

Requires the `openai` package (`pip install 'ef[openai]'`).

### ef.plan_refresh(report, , mode='full', scope=None)

Turn a [`StalenessReport`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.StalenessReport) into a [`RefreshPlan`](_autosummary/ef.html.md#ef.RefreshPlan).

The pure, side-effect-free core of the refresh policy. Every source that is
`missing`, `stale` or `misconfigured` is (re-)materialized; what gets
*deleted* is what the `mode` dictates:

- `none` — delete nothing (stale content is added alongside the old);
- `incremental` — delete the stale/misconfigured sources’ old documents;
- `full` / `scoped_full` — also delete orphans.

* **Parameters:**
  * **report** ([`StalenessReport`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.StalenessReport)) – the staleness report to act on.
  * **mode** ([`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[`'none'`, `'incremental'`, `'full'`, `'scoped_full'`]) – one of `REFRESH_MODES`.
  * **scope** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – an optional subset of source ids the plan is restricted to —
    sources outside it are left entirely alone. `None` means the whole
    report. (With `scope=None`, `full` and `scoped_full` coincide.)
* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – if `mode` is not a recognized `RefreshMode`.
* **Return type:**
  [`RefreshPlan`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.RefreshPlan)

```pycon
>>> from ef.diagnostics import StalenessReport
>>> report = StalenessReport(config='c0', orphan=('x',), missing=('a',),
...                          stale=('b',), misconfigured=('c',), fresh=('d',))
>>> plan_refresh(report, mode='full').to_materialize
('a', 'b', 'c')
>>> plan_refresh(report, mode='full').to_delete
('b', 'c', 'x')
>>> plan_refresh(report, mode='incremental').to_delete
('b', 'c')
>>> plan_refresh(report, mode='none').to_delete
()
>>> plan_refresh(report, mode='scoped_full', scope=['a', 'b']).to_delete
('b',)
```

### ef.precision_at_k(ranked, relevant, k)

Fraction of the top `k` results that are relevant.

```pycon
>>> precision_at_k(['d1', 'x', 'd2'], {'d1': 1.0, 'd2': 1.0}, 2)
0.5
```

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### ef.producer_spec(op, \*inputs, op_version, \*\*params)

Build a [`ProducerSpec`](_autosummary/ef.html.md#ef.ProducerSpec) ergonomically — inputs positional, params keyword.

The natural way to write a recipe: the input artifact ids are positional
(their order is significant — it is the order the op receives them), and
every keyword argument is an op parameter. `op_version` is keyword-only
and required — an op without a stated version cannot be content-addressed
safely.

```pycon
>>> spec = producer_spec('segment', 'doc-1', op_version='1', size=512, overlap=64)
>>> spec.op, spec.inputs
('segment', ('doc-1',))
>>> spec.params == {'size': 512, 'overlap': 64}
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`ProducerSpec`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec)

### ef.project(data, , dims=2, method='auto', embedder=None, n_neighbors=15, min_dist=0.1, metric='cosine', pca_components=50, random_state=42)

Project a corpus’s embeddings to `dims` coordinates for visualization.

The canonical “show me the shape of the corpus” operation (use cases §G1).
The default `method='auto'` runs the design-notes §8.4 recipe — \*\*PCA →
UMAP\*\*, `cosine` metric, seeded: PCA first compresses high-dimensional
embeddings to `pca_components` (cheap denoising), then UMAP lays them out
in `dims` dimensions.

* **Parameters:**
  * **data** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – what to project — anything `_resolve_vectors()` understands:
    an `ndarray` (or nested sequence) of vectors, an iterable of
    texts (embedded with `embedder`), a [`Corpus`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.Corpus)
    mapping, or a [`SearchableCorpus`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchableCorpus) /
    [`SourceManager`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager) (vectors pulled from the
    index).
  * **dims** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – target dimensionality — `2` or `3` for plotting.
  * **method** ([`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[`'auto'`, `'umap'`, `'pca'`]) – `'auto'` (UMAP when available and the corpus is large enough,
    else PCA), `'umap'` (force UMAP — needs the `ef[explore]`
    extra), or `'pca'` (numpy-only, always available).
  * **embedder** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – embedder used when `data` is raw text; defaults to the
    dependency-free [`DEFAULT_EMBEDDER`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.DEFAULT_EMBEDDER).
  * **n_neighbors** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – UMAP neighborhood size (clamped to `n_samples - 1`).
  * **min_dist** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – UMAP minimum point separation in the embedding.
  * **metric** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – UMAP distance metric — `'cosine'` for semantic embeddings.
  * **pca_components** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – PCA width for the pre-UMAP compression step; PCA is
    skipped when the source dimensionality is already smaller.
  * **random_state** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – seed — projection is reproducible.
* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`
* **Returns:**
  An `ndarray` of shape `(n_samples, dims)`, rows in input order.
* **Raises:**
  * [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – if there are fewer than 2 samples.
  * [**ImportError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ImportError) – if `method='umap'` and `umap-learn` is not installed.

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> vectors = np.random.RandomState(1).rand(20, 32)
>>> project(vectors, dims=3, method='pca').shape
(20, 3)
```

### ef.read_beir(directory, , qrels=None)

Load a BEIR-format dataset from disk into the in-memory evaluation triple.

Reads `corpus.jsonl` (records `{"_id", "title", "text"}`),
`queries.jsonl` (records `{"_id", "text"}`) and a `qrels` TSV
(`query-id`, `corpus-id`, `score` columns). The corpus text is the
record’s `title` and `text` joined — the BEIR convention.

* **Parameters:**
  * **directory** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the dataset directory.
  * **qrels** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the qrels file, relative to `directory`. `None` tries
    `_DEFAULT_QRELS_PATHS` in order.
* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]]]
* **Returns:**
  a `(corpus, queries, qrels)` triple — `corpus` and `queries` are
  `{id: text}` dicts, `qrels` is `{query_id: {doc_id: relevance}}`.
  Feed it straight to [`evaluate_retrieval()`](_autosummary/ef.html.md#ef.evaluate_retrieval) (after indexing `corpus`
  with [`ingest()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.ingest)).
* **Raises:**
  [**FileNotFoundError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#FileNotFoundError) – if `corpus.jsonl`, `queries.jsonl` or the qrels
      file is missing.

### ef.read_graded_cases(cases_path, named_sets_path=None, , grades={'core': 2.0, 'strong': 1.0}, probes=None)

Load an `ir.eval`-style graded case file (and named sets) as a benchmark.

Each theme is one query: its text comes from `probes` or, failing that, the
`__meta__` header’s `probes`; its qrels are the cases whose level for that
theme is in `grades`. A theme with no such case is left out.

* **Parameters:**
  * **cases_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)) – JSONL of `{"artifact_id", "labels": {theme: level}}`.
  * **named_sets_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – optional JSON `{theme: {"distractors", "hard_positives"}}`.
  * **grades** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]) – level -> relevance grade; other levels are not relevant.
  * **probes** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `{theme: query text}`, overriding the header’s.
* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – when a labelled theme has no query text.
* **Return type:**
  [`GradedBenchmark`](_autosummary/ef.ablation.html.md#ef.ablation.GradedBenchmark)

### ef.ready_handle(array)

Wrap an already-computed array in a finished [`BatchHandle`](_autosummary/ef.html.md#ef.BatchHandle).

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> h = ready_handle(np.zeros((2, 3)))
>>> h.poll()
'done'
>>> h.result().shape
(2, 3)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`BatchHandle`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.BatchHandle)

### ef.recall_at_k(ranked, relevant, k)

Fraction of the relevant docs that appear in the top `k` results.

```pycon
>>> recall_at_k(['d1', 'x', 'd2'], {'d1': 1.0, 'd2': 1.0}, 2)
0.5
>>> recall_at_k(['d1', 'x', 'd2'], {'d1': 1.0, 'd2': 1.0}, 3)
1.0
```

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### ef.reciprocal_rank(ranked, relevant, k=None)

Reciprocal of the rank of the first relevant result (`0` if none).

Averaged over queries this is MRR. `k` optionally caps how far down the
ranking to look.

```pycon
>>> reciprocal_rank(['x', 'd1', 'd2'], {'d1': 1.0})
0.5
>>> reciprocal_rank(['x', 'd1'], {'d1': 1.0}, k=1)       # relevant doc past the cutoff
0.0
```

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### ef.refresh_on_change(manager)

Build a [`ChangeEvent`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeEvent) handler that auto-refreshes `manager`.

The *auto* refresh seam. The returned callable is meant to be a
[`ChangeDetectingCorpus`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeDetectingCorpus)’s `on_change` — each detected
edit (through the wrapper, or surfaced out-of-band by `scan()`) is
incrementally applied to every materialized config of `manager`:
an `added` source is indexed, a `modified` one is re-indexed
(delete-then-add), a `deleted` one is removed.

[`SourceManager`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager) wires this automatically when
constructed with `auto_refresh=True`; call this directly only to attach a
manager to a corpus you build yourself.

* **Parameters:**
  **manager** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – a [`SourceManager`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager) (duck-typed — any
  object with an `_apply_change(event)` method).
* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`ChangeEvent`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeEvent)], [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]
* **Returns:**
  a `Callable[[ChangeEvent], None]` for `on_change`.

### ef.rerank(query, segments, reranker, , limit=None)

Re-score `segments` against `query` with `reranker` and re-order them.

The pure heart of the module — no I/O, no retrieval. The `reranker` is
called once with the whole candidate list; the segments are returned sorted
by descending score (ties keep their incoming order), optionally trimmed to
`limit`. Each returned segment is a copy carrying the reranker’s score in
`metadata["rerank_score"]` — so the new ranking is auditable.

* **Parameters:**
  * **query** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the search query the segments are scored against.
  * **segments** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)]) – the candidate segments (from a first-stage retriever).
  * **reranker** ([`Reranker`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#ef.reranking.Reranker)) – a [`Reranker`](_autosummary/ef.html.md#ef.Reranker) — a callable `(query, segments) -> scores`.
  * **limit** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – keep only the top `limit` after reranking; `None` keeps all.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)]
* **Returns:**
  the reranked segments — copies, best first.
* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – if the reranker returns a number of scores that does not
      match the number of segments.

```pycon
>>> segs = [{'text': 'a', 'id': '1'}, {'text': 'bbb', 'id': '2'}]
>>> ranked = rerank('q', segs, lambda q, s: [len(x['text']) for x in s])
>>> [r['text'] for r in ranked]
['bbb', 'a']
>>> ranked[0]['metadata']['rerank_score']
3.0
```

### ef.run_arms(corpus, arms, benchmark, , k_values=(10, 20), segmenter=None, doc_vectors=None)

Score every arm on the same segmented corpus; one row per arm.

* **Parameters:**
  * **corpus** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – `{doc_id: text}` (segmented with `segmenter`) or
    `{doc_id: [segment, ...]}` (used as is).
  * **arms** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Arm`](_autosummary/ef.ablation.html.md#ef.ablation.Arm) | [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]) – `{name: Arm}`; a bare embedder is taken as `Arm(embedder)`.
  * **benchmark** ([`GradedBenchmark`](_autosummary/ef.ablation.html.md#ef.ablation.GradedBenchmark)) – what to score against ([`read_graded_cases()`](_autosummary/ef.html.md#ef.read_graded_cases)).
  * **k_values** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]) – rank cutoffs.
  * **segmenter** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – for string documents; see `segment_corpus()`.
  * **doc_vectors** ([`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), `ndarray`] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – cache of segment matrices keyed by
    `"<document-side model_id>/<digest of the segmented corpus>"`, so a
    persistent store (e.g. a `dol` store) can be reused across runs and
    corpora. A fresh dict by default; embedders without a `model_id`
    are never cached.
* **Return type:**
  [`BenchmarkReport`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.BenchmarkReport)

```pycon
>>> from ef.embedders import HashingEmbedder
>>> bench = GradedBenchmark({'q': {'fruit': 1.0}}, {'q': 'apple'})
>>> rep = run_arms({'fruit': 'red apple', 'car': 'blue car'},
...                {'A': HashingEmbedder()}, bench, k_values=(1,))
>>> rep.rows[0]['embedder'], rep.rows[0]['recall@1']
('A', 1.0)
```

### ef.segment_id(text, metadata=None)

Content-derived id for a segment — `sha256` of its normalized content.

The id is `sha256(normalize(text) + canonical_json(metadata))` — the
normalization and hashing primitives live in [`ef.hashing`](_autosummary/ef.hashing.html.md#module-ef.hashing), the single
source of truth `ef` content-addresses through. Because the id depends
only on content, re-segmenting an unchanged document produces identical ids
— which is what makes ingestion idempotent (a re-run is a no-op, not a
duplicate). Pass `metadata` only when two segments could share identical
`text` yet must stay distinct (e.g. same boilerplate from different
sources).

```pycon
>>> segment_id('hello') == segment_id('hello')
True
>>> segment_id('hello') == segment_id('world')
False
>>> segment_id('x', {'source': 'a'}) == segment_id('x', {'source': 'b'})
False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### ef.segment_record(x)

Coerce `x` (`str` / `Mapping` / [`SegmentRecord`](_autosummary/ef.html.md#ef.SegmentRecord)) into a record.

The dataclass counterpart of [`as_segment()`](_autosummary/ef.html.md#ef.as_segment) — the convenience-surface
constructor.

```pycon
>>> segment_record('hello').text
'hello'
>>> segment_record({'text': 'hi', 'tokens': 1}).tokens
1
```

* **Return type:**
  [`SegmentRecord`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.SegmentRecord)

### ef.sentence_transformers_embedder(model_name='all-MiniLM-L6-v2', , device=None, normalize=False, batch_size=128, model_path=None, query_prompt=None, document_prompt=None, prompt_names=None, \*\*st_kwargs)

Build a local sentence-transformers [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder).

Instruction-tuned models (bge, gte, e5-instruct, Qwen3-Embedding…) are
conditioned per `input_type`: pass a literal `query_prompt` (and, rarely,
`document_prompt`), or map input types to prompts the model defines itself
with `prompt_names` (e.g. `{"query": "query"}` for Qwen3-Embedding). Those
roles are then advertised in `honored_input_types`, and the prompt text is
baked into `model_id`. Only trust prompts on genuinely instruction-tuned
models; on `all-MiniLM` they are expected to be a near no-op. Prefer these
over wrapping the adapter in [`InstructionEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_wrappers.html.md#ef.embedder_wrappers.InstructionEmbedder):
sentence-transformers knows the prompt’s length, so models that pool without
the prompt tokens (INSTRUCTOR, GRIT) stay correct. Needs
sentence-transformers >= 2.3.

* **Parameters:**
  * **model_name** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – A sentence-transformers model name (also used in
    `model_id`).
  * **device** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Torch device (`"cuda"` / `"cpu"` / `"mps"`); `None`
    auto-selects.
  * **normalize** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Whether to L2-normalize outputs. sentence-transformers does
    **not** normalize by default — set this truthfully.
  * **batch_size** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Encoding batch size (smaller on CPU).
  * **model_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – A local filesystem path to load from instead of the hub —
    for air-gapped use. Loading still records `model_name` in
    `model_id`.
  * **query_prompt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Prompt prepended to `input_type="query"` texts (passed
    as `encode(prompt=...)`).
  * **document_prompt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Prompt for `input_type="document"` texts (usually
    none: the asymmetric pattern leaves documents bare). `""` means an
    explicit empty prompt, which stops a model’s `default_prompt_name`
    from being applied to documents.
  * **prompt_names** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – `{input_type: name}` of prompts defined in the model’s
    own `prompts` config (passed as `encode(prompt_name=...)`).
    An explicit `prompt=` / `prompt_name=` in a call overrides both.
  * **\*\*st_kwargs** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – Forwarded to the `SentenceTransformer` constructor.
* **Return type:**
  [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder)

Requires `sentence-transformers` (`pip install 'ef[sentence-transformers]'`).

### ef.step_params(op, raw_params=None, , n_inputs=1)

The canonical *keyword* params of an op step — its inputs dropped.

An [`ef.ops`](_autosummary/ef.ops.html.md#module-ef.ops) op is called `op(*input_values, **params)`: the first
`n_inputs` positional parameters are upstream artifacts (they belong in
[`ProducerSpec.inputs`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec.inputs), not in
the params), and every remaining parameter is a hashable step param. This
runs [`full_kwargs()`](_autosummary/ef.html.md#ef.full_kwargs) with placeholder inputs, then drops those input
slots — leaving exactly the params, defaults filled, ready for a
[`TransformSpec`](_autosummary/ef.html.md#ef.TransformSpec).

* **Parameters:**
  * **op** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]) – the op callable whose signature is the param contract.
  * **raw_params** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the keyword params the caller actually supplied; anything
    omitted is defaulted.
  * **n_inputs** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – how many leading positional parameters are upstream inputs.
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

```pycon
>>> def embed(segments, *, input_type='document'): ...
>>> step_params(embed, {'input_type': 'query'})
{'input_type': 'query'}
>>> step_params(embed)                              # default filled in
{'input_type': 'document'}
>>> def segment(source): ...
>>> step_params(segment)                            # no params at all
{}
```

### ef.token_f1(response, reference)

Token-overlap F1 of `response` against `reference` (the SQuAD F1).

The harmonic mean of token precision and recall over the normalized token
bags — a graded credit where [`exact_match()`](_autosummary/ef.html.md#ef.exact_match) is all-or-nothing.

```pycon
>>> token_f1('the quick brown fox', 'a quick brown fox')
1.0
>>> round(token_f1('quick brown fox', 'quick brown dog'), 4)
0.6667
```

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### ef.voyage_embedder(model='voyage-3.5', , dim=None, api_key=None, batch_size=1000, timeout=60.0)

Build a Voyage AI [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder).

Talks to Voyage’s `/v1/embeddings` REST endpoint directly — no
`voyageai` SDK, no extra dependency. Voyage embeddings are L2-normalized.
Voyage distinguishes only `query` from `document`; a `classification`
or `clustering` hint is simply not sent.

* **Parameters:**
  * **model** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – A Voyage embedding model name.
  * **dim** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Matryoshka-truncated width (the `voyage-3.5` family and
    `voyage-code-3` only). Omit for the model’s native width.
  * **api_key** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Voyage API key. Falls back to `VOYAGE_API_KEY`.
  * **batch_size** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Texts per request (capped at Voyage’s 1000 limit).
  * **timeout** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Per-request timeout in seconds.
* **Return type:**
  [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder)
* **Returns:**
  An [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder) over the Voyage API.

### ef.with_overlap(segmenter, n_chars, /, \*, count_tokens=<function approx_token_count>, tokenizer='char-approx')

Wrap `segmenter` so consecutive segments overlap by `n_chars` characters.

Each segment is extended *forward* by up to `n_chars` characters (clamped
to the source length), so segment *K* shares its tail with segment *K+1*’s
head. A segment whose text changes has its `id` re-derived and its
`tokens` recounted; segments lacking `start` / `end` offsets pass
through untouched.

Overlap is expressed in *characters* here (this is a generic post-hoc
helper) — for token-measured overlap use a segmenter’s own `chunk_overlap`.

```pycon
>>> base = RecursiveCharacterSegmenter(chunk_size=3, chunk_overlap=0)
>>> [c['text'] for c in base('one two three four')]
['one two three', 'four']
>>> [c['text'] for c in with_overlap(base, 100)('one two three four')]
['one two three four', 'four']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.Segmenter)

### ef.with_reranker(retriever, reranker, , fetch_k=50)

Decorate a retrieve-style callable with a two-stage reranking pass.

Wraps `retriever` (e.g. [`SourceManager.retrieve`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.retrieve), or any callable
`query -> list[Segment]`) so every call over-fetches `fetch_k`
candidates cheaply, [`rerank()`](_autosummary/ef.html.md#ef.rerank)s them, and returns the top `limit`.
The decorated callable keeps the retriever’s interface — `query` plus a
keyword-only `limit` — so it is a drop-in replacement, including as the
`retriever` argument of [`evaluate_retrieval()`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.evaluate_retrieval).

* **Parameters:**
  * **retriever** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)]]) – the first-stage retriever — a callable
    `retriever(query, *, limit=...) -> segments`.
  * **reranker** ([`Reranker`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#ef.reranking.Reranker)) – the [`Reranker`](_autosummary/ef.html.md#ef.Reranker) applied to the over-fetched candidates.
  * **fetch_k** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – how many candidates to retrieve before reranking. Larger trades
    latency for recall headroom; it should comfortably exceed the
    `limit` callers ask for.
* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)]]
* **Returns:**
  a new callable `(query, *, limit=10, **kwargs) -> list[Segment]` —
  extra keyword arguments (e.g. `filter`) pass straight through to
  `retriever`.

```pycon
>>> pool = [{'text': t, 'id': t} for t in ['ab', 'abcd', 'abc']]
>>> def base(query, *, limit=10):
...     return pool[:limit]
>>> retrieve = with_reranker(
...     base, lambda q, segs: [len(s['text']) for s in segs], fetch_k=10)
>>> [s['text'] for s in retrieve('a query', limit=2)]
['abcd', 'abc']
```

### ef.write_beir(directory, corpus, queries, qrels)

Write an evaluation triple to disk in BEIR format — the inverse of [`read_beir()`](_autosummary/ef.html.md#ef.read_beir).

Creates `directory` (and parents) and writes `corpus.jsonl`,
`queries.jsonl` and `qrels.tsv`. Use it to snapshot an `ef` corpus as
a reusable benchmark (`ef_use_cases.md` §H4).

* **Parameters:**
  * **directory** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the output directory — created if absent.
  * **corpus** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – the documents — `{doc_id: text}`.
  * **queries** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – the queries — `{query_id: query_text}`.
  * **qrels** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]]) – the relevance judgements — `{query_id: {doc_id: relevance}}`.
* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

# _autosummary/ef.ops.html.md

# ef.ops

The pipeline ops — the callables an [`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph) runs.

The [`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph) resolves a [`ProducerSpec`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec)’s string `op` key to a callable through its
injectable `ops` registry, then calls `op(*input_values, **params)`. This
module supplies the two ops Phase 5’s pipeline needs and the machinery that
turns a *live component* (a [`Segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.Segmenter) /
[`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder)) into a serializable [`TransformSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.TransformSpec)
*plus* the bound callable to register.

The split is deliberate:

- a [`TransformSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.TransformSpec) is **data** — an op *key*, a version,
  params — so it can be persisted (the recipe is content-addressed);
- the callable is **not** data — it closes over a live component — so it is
  re-registered into the graph’s `ops` registry each process.

The op key carries the **component identity** ([`segmenter_identity()`](_autosummary/ef.ops.html.md#ef.ops.segmenter_identity),
`embedder.model_id`): `"segment:<identity>"` / `"embed:<model_id>"`.
Because `op` participates in [`artifact_id()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.artifact_id), two
configs with different components get disjoint artifact cones automatically,
and two configs with the *same* component share every upstream artifact — which
is what makes config branching free (design notes §3.1).

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from ef import as_embedder, as_segmenter
>>> seg = as_segmenter('recursive', chunk_size=128)
>>> seg_spec, seg_fn = segment_step(seg)
>>> seg_spec.op.startswith('segment:recursive-char')
True
>>> [s['text'] for s in seg_fn('hello world')]
['hello world']
>>> emb = as_embedder(lambda ts: np.ones((len(ts), 4)), model_id='ones@4')
>>> emb_spec, emb_fn = embed_step(emb)
>>> emb_spec.op, emb_spec.params
('embed:ones@4', {'input_type': 'document'})
>>> emb_fn([{'text': 'a'}, {'text': 'b'}]).shape
(2, 4)
```

### ef.ops.EMBED_OP_VERSION *= '1'*

Version of the [`make_embed_op()`](_autosummary/ef.ops.html.md#ef.ops.make_embed_op) wrapper. Bump on any behavior change —
see [`SEGMENT_OP_VERSION`](_autosummary/ef.ops.html.md#ef.ops.SEGMENT_OP_VERSION). (This is the *wrapper* version; the embedding
*model*’s identity already lives in the op key via `embedder.model_id`.)

### ef.ops.SEGMENT_OP_VERSION *= '1'*

Version of the [`make_segment_op()`](_autosummary/ef.ops.html.md#ef.ops.make_segment_op) wrapper. It participates in every
downstream [`artifact_id()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.artifact_id), so \*\*bump it on any
behavior change\*\* to how a segment artifact is produced — the graph trusts
the version and cannot inspect the code (a silent change serves stale cache).

### ef.ops.embed_step(embedder)

An embedder → its [`TransformSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.TransformSpec) and bound op callable.

The mirror of [`segment_step()`](_autosummary/ef.ops.html.md#ef.ops.segment_step) for the embed layer. The op key is
`"embed:<model_id>"` — the model identity already content-addresses the
vector — and `params` carries the defaults-filled `input_type`.

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from ef import as_embedder
>>> spec, fn = embed_step(as_embedder(lambda ts: np.ones((len(ts), 2)), model_id='m@2'))
>>> spec.op, spec.params
('embed:m@2', {'input_type': 'document'})
```

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`TransformSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.TransformSpec), [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)], [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]

### ef.ops.embedder_identity(embedder)

The content-addressing identity of an embedder — its `model_id`.

[`Embedder.model_id`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder.model_id) already bakes in
everything that changes the vector (provider, model, dimensionality), so it
*is* the identity — this function just names that fact for symmetry with
[`segmenter_identity()`](_autosummary/ef.ops.html.md#ef.ops.segmenter_identity).

```pycon
>>> from ef import as_embedder
>>> import numpy as np
>>> embedder_identity(as_embedder(lambda ts: np.ones((len(ts), 2)), model_id='m@2'))
'm@2'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### ef.ops.make_embed_op(embedder)

Build the **embed** op — a list of `Segment`s → an `(n, dim)` array.

The returned callable closes over `embedder` and embeds the segments’
`text` in caller order; row `i` of the result is the vector of segment
`i`. `input_type` is a hashable step param (it changes the vector for
task-aware embedders) — it defaults to `"document"`, the indexing role.

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from ef import as_embedder
>>> op = make_embed_op(as_embedder(lambda ts: np.ones((len(ts), 3)), model_id='m@3'))
>>> op([{'text': 'a'}, {'text': 'b'}]).shape
(2, 3)
>>> op([]).shape[0]                     # an empty doc embeds to zero rows
0
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)]], [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### ef.ops.make_segment_op(segmenter)

Build the **segment** op — a leaf source → its list of `Segment`s.

The returned callable closes over `segmenter`; it is what gets registered
into the [`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph)’s `ops` registry under
the key [`segment_step()`](_autosummary/ef.ops.html.md#ef.ops.segment_step) computes. It materializes the (streaming)
segmenter output into a `list` — a graph artifact must be a concrete,
re-readable value.

```pycon
>>> from ef import as_segmenter
>>> op = make_segment_op(as_segmenter('lines'))
>>> [s['text'] for s in op('one\ntwo')]
['one', 'two']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)], [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)]]

### ef.ops.segment_step(segmenter)

A segmenter → its [`TransformSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.TransformSpec) and bound op callable.

The [`TransformSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.TransformSpec) is serializable data (op key + version

+ params); the callable closes over the live `segmenter` and is registered
  into the graph’s `ops` registry under `spec.op`. Pair them: persist the
  spec, re-register the callable each process.

```pycon
>>> from ef import as_segmenter
>>> spec, fn = segment_step(as_segmenter('recursive', chunk_size=128))
>>> spec.op_version, spec.params
('1', {})
```

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`TransformSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.TransformSpec), [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)], [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]

### ef.ops.segmenter_identity(segmenter)

A stable identity string for a segmenter — the content-addressing key.

The segmenter’s counterpart of [`Embedder.model_id`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder.model_id). Two segmenters that segment identically
must return the *same* identity; any difference that changes the segments
(chunk size, overlap, separators, tokenizer) must change it. Resolution
order:

1. an explicit `segmenter_id` attribute, if the segmenter advertises one;
2. a [`RecursiveCharacterSegmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.RecursiveCharacterSegmenter) — identified by its
   config-bearing attributes (`chunk_size` / `chunk_overlap` /
   `separators` / `tokenizer`);
3. a [`FunctionSegmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.FunctionSegmenter) — by its wrapped callable;
4. otherwise the segmenter’s own `__qualname__` / `__name__` / type name.

```pycon
>>> from ef import as_segmenter
>>> a = segmenter_identity(as_segmenter('recursive', chunk_size=256))
>>> b = segmenter_identity(as_segmenter('recursive', chunk_size=512))
>>> a == b                              # different chunk_size → different id
False
>>> a == segmenter_identity(as_segmenter('recursive', chunk_size=256))
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)


# _autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md

# ef.refresh

Refresh — keeping an indexed corpus in sync as its sources change.

Phase 5 indexes a corpus *once*. This module makes the index **maintainable**:
when sources are added, edited or deleted, refresh brings the `vd` index back
into agreement with the corpus. It is the acting counterpart of the read-only
[`ef.diagnostics`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#module-ef.diagnostics) — diagnostics says *what drifted*, refresh *fixes it*.

The one idea, restated from [`ef.artifact_graph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#module-ef.artifact_graph):

> Refresh = diff source hashes → delete the stale/orphan documents →
> re-`materialize` what changed.

The `vd` collection is the single source of truth for *what is indexed*; the
[`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph) is only a *cache*. So refresh has two
kinds of effect, and they are not equally critical:

- **Collection edits are correctness.** Stale and orphaned documents must be
  removed precisely (by `source_id`), or a search returns wrong hits.
- **Graph pruning is housekeeping.** A content-addressed artifact keyed by a
  now-dead content hash is never *served* again (its source’s content — hence
  its leaf id — has moved on); it is merely wasted cache. So [`prune_dead_leaves()`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.prune_dead_leaves)
  is best-effort and only ever cascades leaves verified dead — no surviving
  source still hashes to them.

The four refresh modes (`ef_design_notes.md` §8.5, mirroring LangChain’s
indexing API) differ only in **how much they delete**:

[`plan_refresh()`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.plan_refresh) turns a [`StalenessReport`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.StalenessReport) + a mode
into a [`RefreshPlan`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.RefreshPlan) (which sources to (re-)materialize, which documents
to delete) — a pure function, the testable heart of the policy. The orchestration
that applies a plan lives on [`SourceManager`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager)
([`refresh()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.refresh)).

**Explicit vs. auto.** [`SourceManager.refresh`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.refresh) is the *explicit* path — it re-reads
and re-hashes the corpus, so it catches out-of-band edits on its own.
[`refresh_on_change()`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.refresh_on_change) is the *auto* path: a handler you hand to a
[`ChangeDetectingCorpus`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeDetectingCorpus)’s `on_change` so each edit is
incrementally re-indexed as it happens (`SourceManager(auto_refresh=True)`
wires this for you).

### Module Attributes

| [`RefreshMode`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.RefreshMode)   | The four refresh modes — see the module docstring and `ef_design_notes.md` §8.5.                  |
|----------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`REFRESH_MODES`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.REFRESH_MODES) | The accepted [`RefreshMode`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.RefreshMode) values, for validation. |

### Functions

| [`plan_refresh`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.plan_refresh)(report, \*[, mode, scope])           | Turn a [`StalenessReport`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.StalenessReport) into a [`RefreshPlan`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.RefreshPlan).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`delete_source_documents`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.delete_source_documents)(collection, indexed, ...) | Delete every `vd` document belonging to the given `source_ids`.                                                                                                               |
| [`prune_dead_leaves`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.prune_dead_leaves)(graph, live_leaves)             | Cascade out of `graph` every leaf no live source still hashes to.                                                                                                             |
| [`refresh_on_change`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.refresh_on_change)(manager)                        | Build a [`ChangeEvent`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeEvent) handler that auto-refreshes `manager`.                                             |

### ef.refresh.REFRESH_MODES *: [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)['none', 'incremental', 'full', 'scoped_full'], ...]* *= ('none', 'incremental', 'full', 'scoped_full')*

The four refresh modes — see the module docstring and `ef_design_notes.md`

### *class* ef.refresh.RefreshPlan(to_materialize=(), to_delete=())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

What a refresh will do — [`plan_refresh()`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.plan_refresh)’s output.

The two fields are disjoint in *intent* but may overlap in membership: a
stale source is in **both** — its old documents are deleted *and* it is
re-materialized. An orphan is only in `to_delete`; a brand-new source only
in `to_materialize`.

#### to_materialize

source ids to (re-)run through the pipeline.

* **Type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis)]

#### to_delete

source ids whose currently-indexed documents are removed
(before re-materializing, for the ones that also reappear above).

* **Type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis)]

### *class* ef.refresh.RefreshReport(config, mode, added=(), modified=(), deleted=(), unchanged=(), documents_written=0, documents_removed=0, artifacts_removed=0)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The outcome of a refresh — what `SourceManager.refresh()` returns.

`added` / `modified` / `deleted` / `unchanged` partition the
source ids the refresh considered (mirroring [`CorpusDiff`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.CorpusDiff)
field names): newly indexed, re-indexed (was stale/misconfigured), removed
(orphan), and already-fresh-left-alone. The three counts report the work
done. Truthiness reports whether anything changed.

```pycon
>>> r = RefreshReport(config='c0', mode='full', added=('a',), modified=('b',))
>>> bool(r), r.changed
(True, ('a', 'b'))
>>> bool(RefreshReport(config='c0', mode='full', unchanged=('a',)))
False
```

#### *property* changed *: [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), ...]*

The source ids that were added, modified or deleted.

### ef.refresh.delete_source_documents(collection, indexed, source_ids)

Delete every `vd` document belonging to the given `source_ids`.

The correctness half of a refresh: a stale or orphaned source’s documents
must leave the collection. `indexed` — an [`indexed_state()`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.indexed_state)
grouping — supplies each source’s document ids, so no per-source scan is
needed. A document already gone is silently tolerated (idempotent).

* **Parameters:**
  * **collection** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – the `vd` collection (a `MutableMapping`) to delete from.
  * **indexed** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`IndexedSource`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.IndexedSource)]) – the `{source_id: IndexedSource}` map of what is indexed.
  * **source_ids** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – the sources whose documents to remove.
* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)
* **Returns:**
  the number of documents actually deleted.

```pycon
>>> from ef.diagnostics import IndexedSource
>>> collection = {'s1#0': ..., 's1#1': ..., 's2#0': ...}
>>> indexed = {
...     's1': IndexedSource('s1', ('s1#0', 's1#1'), frozenset(), frozenset()),
...     's2': IndexedSource('s2', ('s2#0',), frozenset(), frozenset()),
... }
>>> delete_source_documents(collection, indexed, ['s1'])
2
>>> sorted(collection)
['s2#0']
```

### ef.refresh.plan_refresh(report, , mode='full', scope=None)

Turn a [`StalenessReport`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.StalenessReport) into a [`RefreshPlan`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.RefreshPlan).

The pure, side-effect-free core of the refresh policy. Every source that is
`missing`, `stale` or `misconfigured` is (re-)materialized; what gets
*deleted* is what the `mode` dictates:

- `none` — delete nothing (stale content is added alongside the old);
- `incremental` — delete the stale/misconfigured sources’ old documents;
- `full` / `scoped_full` — also delete orphans.

* **Parameters:**
  * **report** ([`StalenessReport`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.StalenessReport)) – the staleness report to act on.
  * **mode** ([`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[`'none'`, `'incremental'`, `'full'`, `'scoped_full'`]) – one of [`REFRESH_MODES`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.REFRESH_MODES).
  * **scope** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – an optional subset of source ids the plan is restricted to —
    sources outside it are left entirely alone. `None` means the whole
    report. (With `scope=None`, `full` and `scoped_full` coincide.)
* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – if `mode` is not a recognized [`RefreshMode`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.RefreshMode).
* **Return type:**
  [`RefreshPlan`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.RefreshPlan)

```pycon
>>> from ef.diagnostics import StalenessReport
>>> report = StalenessReport(config='c0', orphan=('x',), missing=('a',),
...                          stale=('b',), misconfigured=('c',), fresh=('d',))
>>> plan_refresh(report, mode='full').to_materialize
('a', 'b', 'c')
>>> plan_refresh(report, mode='full').to_delete
('b', 'c', 'x')
>>> plan_refresh(report, mode='incremental').to_delete
('b', 'c')
>>> plan_refresh(report, mode='none').to_delete
()
>>> plan_refresh(report, mode='scoped_full', scope=['a', 'b']).to_delete
('b',)
```

### ef.refresh.prune_dead_leaves(graph, live_leaves)

Cascade out of `graph` every leaf no live source still hashes to.

The housekeeping half of a refresh. A graph *leaf* (a node with a cached
value but no producer recipe) is an L0 source keyed by its content hash.
After a refresh, the set of leaves the graph *should* hold is exactly the
content hashes of the current corpus; any other leaf is dead — the source
that produced it was edited (new content → new leaf) or deleted. Each dead
leaf and its whole downstream cone (its segment + embed artifacts) is
[`delete_cascade()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.delete_cascade)d.

This is purely a cache reclaim: a dead leaf is never *served* (nothing
addresses it any more), so pruning it can never change a result — only free
memory. Dead leaves’ cones are disjoint (each produced artifact traces to
exactly one leaf), so the removed-count is exact.

* **Parameters:**
  * **graph** ([`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph)) – the [`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph) to prune.
  * **live_leaves** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – the content hashes that are still live (the current
    corpus’s source hashes).
* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)
* **Returns:**
  the number of artifacts (leaves + produced) removed.

```pycon
>>> from ef import ArtifactGraph, producer_spec
>>> graph = ArtifactGraph()
>>> _ = graph.register_op('id', lambda x: x)
>>> _ = graph.put('live', 'L')
>>> _ = graph.put('dead', 'D')
>>> artifact = graph.add(producer_spec('id', 'dead', op_version='1'))
>>> _ = graph.materialize(artifact)
>>> prune_dead_leaves(graph, ['live'])      # the 'dead' leaf + its artifact
2
>>> 'dead' in graph, 'live' in graph
(False, True)
```

### ef.refresh.refresh_on_change(manager)

Build a [`ChangeEvent`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeEvent) handler that auto-refreshes `manager`.

The *auto* refresh seam. The returned callable is meant to be a
[`ChangeDetectingCorpus`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeDetectingCorpus)’s `on_change` — each detected
edit (through the wrapper, or surfaced out-of-band by `scan()`) is
incrementally applied to every materialized config of `manager`:
an `added` source is indexed, a `modified` one is re-indexed
(delete-then-add), a `deleted` one is removed.

[`SourceManager`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager) wires this automatically when
constructed with `auto_refresh=True`; call this directly only to attach a
manager to a corpus you build yourself.

* **Parameters:**
  **manager** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – a [`SourceManager`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager) (duck-typed — any
  object with an `_apply_change(event)` method).
* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`ChangeEvent`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeEvent)], [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]
* **Returns:**
  a `Callable[[ChangeEvent], None]` for `on_change`.


# _autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md

# ef.reranking

Reranking — a precision pass over retrieved segments (use case F6).

First-stage retrieval (a dense ANN query over `vd`) is tuned for *recall*: it
casts a wide, cheap net. A **reranker** is the precision counterpart — a slower,
more accurate model that re-scores a handful of candidates against the query.
The standard two-stage pattern is “retrieve `fetch_k` cheaply, rerank, keep
the top `limit`”.

This module keeps reranking a *decorator over a retriever*, never a new pipeline
stage — it composes with the existing surface rather than complicating it:

- [`Reranker`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#ef.reranking.Reranker) — the structural protocol: a callable
  `(query, segments) -> one score per segment`. Any plain function of that
  shape *is* a reranker; no base class to subclass.
- [`rerank()`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#ef.reranking.rerank) — the pure operation: re-score and re-order a list of
  [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)s. The reranker’s score is folded into each
  > segment’s `metadata["rerank_score"]`.
- [`with_reranker()`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#ef.reranking.with_reranker) — the decorator: wrap a retrieve-style callable (such as
  [`SourceManager.retrieve`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.retrieve)) so
  > every call over-fetches, reranks, and trims — transparently.
- [`cross_encoder_reranker()`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#ef.reranking.cross_encoder_reranker) — a ready reranker backed by a
  sentence-transformers `CrossEncoder` (an optional heavy dependency, imported
  lazily — the protocol and [`rerank()`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#ef.reranking.rerank) cost nothing).

Example — rerank three segments by a toy length score, longest first:

```pycon
>>> segments = [
...     {'text': 'cat', 'id': '1'},
...     {'text': 'dog', 'id': '2'},
...     {'text': 'cathedral', 'id': '3'},
... ]
>>> def by_length(query, segments):
...     return [len(segment['text']) for segment in segments]
>>> [segment['text'] for segment in rerank('a query', segments, by_length, limit=2)]
['cathedral', 'cat']
```

### Functions

| [`rerank`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#ef.reranking.rerank)(query, segments, reranker, \*[, limit])    | Re-score `segments` against `query` with `reranker` and re-order them.                                              |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`with_reranker`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#ef.reranking.with_reranker)(retriever, reranker, \*[, fetch_k]) | Decorate a retrieve-style callable with a two-stage reranking pass.                                                 |
| [`cross_encoder_reranker`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#ef.reranking.cross_encoder_reranker)([model_name, device, ...]) | Build a [`Reranker`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#ef.reranking.Reranker) backed by a sentence-transformers `CrossEncoder`. |

### Classes

| [`Reranker`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#ef.reranking.Reranker)(\*args, \*\*kwargs)   | A callable that re-scores `(query, segments)` — higher means more relevant.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* ef.reranking.Reranker(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

A callable that re-scores `(query, segments)` — higher means more relevant.

The structural contract a reranker satisfies: given the query and a list of
candidate [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)s, return \*\*one score per
segment\*\*, in the same order. [`rerank()`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#ef.reranking.rerank) sorts by these scores. It is a
`@runtime_checkable Protocol`, not a base class — a plain function of the
right shape already *is* a [`Reranker`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#ef.reranking.Reranker).

```pycon
>>> def by_length(query, segments):
...     return [len(s['text']) for s in segments]
>>> isinstance(by_length, Reranker)
True
```

### ef.reranking.cross_encoder_reranker(model_name='cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2', , device=None, batch_size=32, \*\*predict_kwargs)

Build a [`Reranker`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#ef.reranking.Reranker) backed by a sentence-transformers `CrossEncoder`.

A cross-encoder scores a `(query, passage)` pair *jointly* — it is the
accurate, slower second stage two-stage retrieval is built for. The model is
a heavy, optional dependency: it is imported only when this factory is
called, so importing [`ef.reranking`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#module-ef.reranking) itself stays cheap.

Example:

```default
from ef import ingest, with_reranker, cross_encoder_reranker

index = ingest(corpus, embedder="st:all-MiniLM-L6-v2")
retrieve = with_reranker(index.retrieve, cross_encoder_reranker())
segments = retrieve("a query", limit=5)
```

* **Parameters:**
  * **model_name** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – a sentence-transformers `CrossEncoder` model name.
  * **device** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – torch device (`"cuda"` / `"cpu"` / `"mps"`); `None`
    auto-selects.
  * **batch_size** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – how many pairs to score per forward pass.
  * **predict_kwargs** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – extra keyword arguments forwarded to `CrossEncoder.predict`.
* **Return type:**
  [`Reranker`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#ef.reranking.Reranker)
* **Returns:**
  a [`Reranker`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#ef.reranking.Reranker) — `(query, segments) -> scores`.
* **Raises:**
  [**ImportError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ImportError) – if the optional `sentence-transformers` package is absent.

### ef.reranking.rerank(query, segments, reranker, , limit=None)

Re-score `segments` against `query` with `reranker` and re-order them.

The pure heart of the module — no I/O, no retrieval. The `reranker` is
called once with the whole candidate list; the segments are returned sorted
by descending score (ties keep their incoming order), optionally trimmed to
`limit`. Each returned segment is a copy carrying the reranker’s score in
`metadata["rerank_score"]` — so the new ranking is auditable.

* **Parameters:**
  * **query** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the search query the segments are scored against.
  * **segments** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)]) – the candidate segments (from a first-stage retriever).
  * **reranker** ([`Reranker`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#ef.reranking.Reranker)) – a [`Reranker`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#ef.reranking.Reranker) — a callable `(query, segments) -> scores`.
  * **limit** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – keep only the top `limit` after reranking; `None` keeps all.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)]
* **Returns:**
  the reranked segments — copies, best first.
* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – if the reranker returns a number of scores that does not
      match the number of segments.

```pycon
>>> segs = [{'text': 'a', 'id': '1'}, {'text': 'bbb', 'id': '2'}]
>>> ranked = rerank('q', segs, lambda q, s: [len(x['text']) for x in s])
>>> [r['text'] for r in ranked]
['bbb', 'a']
>>> ranked[0]['metadata']['rerank_score']
3.0
```

### ef.reranking.with_reranker(retriever, reranker, , fetch_k=50)

Decorate a retrieve-style callable with a two-stage reranking pass.

Wraps `retriever` (e.g. [`SourceManager.retrieve`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.retrieve), or any callable
`query -> list[Segment]`) so every call over-fetches `fetch_k`
candidates cheaply, [`rerank()`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#ef.reranking.rerank)s them, and returns the top `limit`.
The decorated callable keeps the retriever’s interface — `query` plus a
keyword-only `limit` — so it is a drop-in replacement, including as the
`retriever` argument of [`evaluate_retrieval()`](_autosummary/ef.evaluation.html.md#ef.evaluation.evaluate_retrieval).

* **Parameters:**
  * **retriever** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)]]) – the first-stage retriever — a callable
    `retriever(query, *, limit=...) -> segments`.
  * **reranker** ([`Reranker`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#ef.reranking.Reranker)) – the [`Reranker`](_autosummary/ef.reranking.html.md#ef.reranking.Reranker) applied to the over-fetched candidates.
  * **fetch_k** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – how many candidates to retrieve before reranking. Larger trades
    latency for recall headroom; it should comfortably exceed the
    `limit` callers ask for.
* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)]]
* **Returns:**
  a new callable `(query, *, limit=10, **kwargs) -> list[Segment]` —
  extra keyword arguments (e.g. `filter`) pass straight through to
  `retriever`.

```pycon
>>> pool = [{'text': t, 'id': t} for t in ['ab', 'abcd', 'abc']]
>>> def base(query, *, limit=10):
...     return pool[:limit]
>>> retrieve = with_reranker(
...     base, lambda q, segs: [len(s['text']) for s in segs], fetch_k=10)
>>> [s['text'] for s in retrieve('a query', limit=2)]
['abcd', 'abc']
```


# _autosummary/ef.segmenter_adapters.html.md

# ef.segmenter_adapters

The segmenter dependency-injection seam and the `imbed` registry bridge.

[`as_segmenter()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenter_adapters.html.md#ef.segmenter_adapters.as_segmenter) is the single place `ef` coerces a user-supplied
segmenter argument into a well-behaved [`Segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.Segmenter) — the
exact mirror of [`as_embedder()`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.as_embedder) for the embed layer.

[`imbed_segmenter()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenter_adapters.html.md#ef.segmenter_adapters.imbed_segmenter) builds a segmenter from `imbed`’s segmenter registry
(`imbed.components.segmentation`); `imbed` is imported lazily, so importing
this module costs nothing extra and `ef` works without `imbed` installed.

Example — the DI seam in action (no `imbed` needed):

```pycon
>>> from ef.segmenters import Segmenter, RecursiveCharacterSegmenter
>>> seg = as_segmenter('recursive', chunk_size=256)
>>> isinstance(seg, RecursiveCharacterSegmenter)
True
>>> as_segmenter(seg) is seg          # a ready segmenter passes straight through
True
>>> custom = as_segmenter(lambda text: text.split('|'))
>>> [s['text'] for s in custom('a|b|c')]
['a', 'b', 'c']
```

### Functions

| [`as_segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenter_adapters.html.md#ef.segmenter_adapters.as_segmenter)([x])       | Normalize `x` into a [`Segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.Segmenter) — the DI seam.        |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`imbed_segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenter_adapters.html.md#ef.segmenter_adapters.imbed_segmenter)([name]) | Build a [`Segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.Segmenter) from `imbed`'s segmenter registry. |

### ef.segmenter_adapters.as_segmenter(x=None, , \*\*kwargs)

Normalize `x` into a [`Segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.Segmenter) — the DI seam.

The single place every `ef` entry point coerces a user-supplied segmenter
argument. Accepts, in order:

1. `None` or `"default"` / `"recursive"` — a
   [`RecursiveCharacterSegmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.RecursiveCharacterSegmenter) (the default);
2. `"lines"` — [`line_segmenter()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.line_segmenter);
3. any other string — looked up in `imbed`’s registry via
   [`imbed_segmenter()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenter_adapters.html.md#ef.segmenter_adapters.imbed_segmenter);
4. a ready-made segmenter (a [`BaseSegmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.BaseSegmenter) or a
   callable marked by `ef`) — returned unchanged;
5. a bare callable — wrapped in [`FunctionSegmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.FunctionSegmenter).

Extra `**kwargs` are forwarded to the chosen factory (ignored when `x`
is already a segmenter).

* **Raises:**
  [**TypeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#TypeError) – if `x` is none of the above.
* **Return type:**
  [`Segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.Segmenter)

```pycon
>>> seg = as_segmenter(chunk_size=256, chunk_overlap=32)
>>> (seg.chunk_size, seg.chunk_overlap)
(256, 32)
```

### ef.segmenter_adapters.imbed_segmenter(name='default', , \*\*kwargs)

Build a [`Segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.Segmenter) from `imbed`’s segmenter registry.

`imbed`’s registered segmenters are bare `text -> Iterable[str]`
callables; this wraps the named one in a [`FunctionSegmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.FunctionSegmenter)
so it emits well-formed [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment) pieces.

* **Parameters:**
  * **name** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – A key in `imbed.components.segmentation.segmenters` (`"default"`
    resolves to `imbed`’s configured default segmenter).
  * **\*\*kwargs** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – Forwarded to [`FunctionSegmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.FunctionSegmenter).
* **Raises:**
  * [**ImportError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ImportError) – if `imbed` is not installed.
  * [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – if `name` is not a registered segmenter.
* **Return type:**
  [`Segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.Segmenter)

Requires the `imbed` package (`pip install 'ef[imbed]'`).


# _autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md

# ef.segmenters

The `Segmenter` facade — `ef`’s segment layer (L2).

A *segmenter* turns a document into a stream of [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)
pieces. Like the embedder facade, its core is a tiny structural contract:

```default
Segmenter = Callable[[str | Mapping], Iterable[Segment]]
```

Everything else — overlap, hierarchy, batching, the recursive splitting
algorithm — is *layered scaffolding* over that one shape.

This module defines:

- [`Segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.Segmenter) — the `@runtime_checkable` protocol (a callable). It is
  a protocol, **not** an ABC: any matching callable *is* a segmenter.
- [`BatchedSegmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.BatchedSegmenter) — an optional optimization trait (a `batch`
  method) for segmenters that can process many documents at once.
- [`BaseSegmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.BaseSegmenter) — an implementation-convenience base (a default
  [`batch()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.BaseSegmenter.batch) and a `repr`). Subclassing is optional.
- [`RecursiveCharacterSegmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.RecursiveCharacterSegmenter) — the **default segmenter**: recursive
  character splitting at ~512 tokens with ~12.5% overlap. The honest default —
  within a point or two of fancier methods on realistic corpora.
- [`line_segmenter()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.line_segmenter) — a builtin that splits a document into its non-empty
  lines (a plain function — proof that a bare callable *is* a segmenter).
- [`FunctionSegmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.FunctionSegmenter) — wraps a bare `text -> pieces` callable into a
  full segmenter; the bridge for `imbed`’s registered segmenters.
- Composition helpers — [`with_overlap()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.with_overlap), [`hierarchical()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.hierarchical),
  [`materialise()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.materialise).

Streaming is first-class: a segmenter returns an *iterable*, not a list, so the
heavy case (a huge corpus) never has to fit every segment in memory at once.

The dependency-injection seam [`as_segmenter()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenter_adapters.html.md#ef.segmenter_adapters.as_segmenter) and
the `imbed` registry bridge live in [`ef.segmenter_adapters`](_autosummary/ef.segmenter_adapters.html.md#module-ef.segmenter_adapters).

Example — split a document into ~4-token chunks with one token of overlap:

```pycon
>>> seg = RecursiveCharacterSegmenter(chunk_size=4, chunk_overlap=1)
>>> [c['text'] for c in seg('alpha beta gamma delta epsilon')]
['alpha beta gamma delta', 'delta epsilon']
>>> isinstance(seg, Segmenter)
True
```

### Module Attributes

| [`APPROX_TOKENIZER`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.APPROX_TOKENIZER)   | Identifier recorded as the `tokenizer` metadata key when token counts come from [`approx_token_count()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.approx_token_count).   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DEFAULT_SEPARATORS`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.DEFAULT_SEPARATORS) | Separators tried, in order, by [`RecursiveCharacterSegmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.RecursiveCharacterSegmenter).                                             |

### Functions

| [`line_segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.line_segmenter)(doc, /)                         | Segment a document into its non-empty lines.                                |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`with_overlap`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.with_overlap)(segmenter, n_chars, /, \*[, ...]) | Wrap `segmenter` so consecutive segments overlap by `n_chars` characters.   |
| [`hierarchical`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.hierarchical)(segmenters, /)                    | Compose segmenters into levels — each segments the previous level's output. |
| [`materialise`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.materialise)(x)                                 | Force a streaming segmenter (or segment stream) to a concrete list.         |
| [`approx_token_count`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.approx_token_count)(text)                       | Rough token count — the common `~4 characters per token` heuristic.         |

### Classes
