|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`BatchedSegmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.BatchedSegmenter)(\*args, \*\*kwargs)               | Optional trait: a segmenter that can process many documents at once.                                                      |
| [`BaseSegmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.BaseSegmenter)()                                    | Implementation base for segmenters (optional — [`Segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.Segmenter) is structural). |
| [`FunctionSegmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.FunctionSegmenter)(func, \*[, pass_doc, ...])       | Promote a bare `text -> pieces` callable to a full [`Segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.Segmenter).            |
| [`RecursiveCharacterSegmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.RecursiveCharacterSegmenter)(\*[, chunk_size, ...]) | The default segmenter — recursive character splitting.                                                                    |

### ef.segmenters.APPROX_TOKENIZER *= 'char-approx'*

Identifier recorded as the `tokenizer` metadata key when token counts come
from [`approx_token_count()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.approx_token_count). Recording *which* tokenizer counted a
segment is mandatory — a `tokens` number is meaningless without it.

### *class* ef.segmenters.BaseSegmenter

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Implementation base for segmenters (optional — [`Segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.Segmenter) is structural).

A subclass implements `__call__`; in return it gets a default
[`batch()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.BaseSegmenter.batch) (one-document-at-a-time — override it for a genuinely batched
backend) and a readable `repr`. Subclassing is purely a convenience;
satisfying [`Segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.Segmenter) structurally is what matters.

#### batch(docs,)

Default: segment each document independently.

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterator)[[`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)]]

### *class* ef.segmenters.BatchedSegmenter(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

Optional trait: a segmenter that can process many documents at once.

Plain [`Segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.Segmenter) handles one document per call. A segmenter that can
amortize per-call cost across documents (a shared model load, a vectorized
pass) also offers `batch`. [`BaseSegmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.BaseSegmenter) supplies a correct — if
un-optimized — default, so every [`BaseSegmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.BaseSegmenter) subclass is already
a [`BatchedSegmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.BatchedSegmenter).

#### batch(docs,)

Segment each document in `docs`, yielding one segment-stream each.

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)]]

### ef.segmenters.DEFAULT_SEPARATORS *: [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), ...]* *= ('\\n\\n', '\\n', '. ', ', ', ' ', '')*

Separators tried, in order, by [`RecursiveCharacterSegmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.RecursiveCharacterSegmenter). Earlier
(coarser) boundaries are preferred; the empty string is the last resort,
splitting between characters so an oversized run is never left unsplit.

### *class* ef.segmenters.FunctionSegmenter(func, \*, pass_doc=False, count_tokens=<function approx_token_count>, tokenizer='char-approx')

Bases: [`BaseSegmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.BaseSegmenter)

Promote a bare `text -> pieces` callable to a full [`Segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.Segmenter).

The bridge for segmenter *functions* that carry no segment schema — most
importantly `imbed`’s registered segmenters, which map text to an iterable
of plain strings. Each piece the callable yields is normalized:

- a `str` piece becomes a [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment); its character
  offsets are recovered by locating it in the source text, and a token
  count plus `tokenizer` metadata are attached;
- a `Mapping` / [`SegmentRecord`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.SegmentRecord) piece is coerced with
  [`as_segment()`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.as_segment), gaining only an `index` / `parent_id`
  > where it lacks them.

* **Parameters:**
  * **func** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]) – The callable to wrap. By default it receives the document’s
    *text*; with `pass_doc=True` it receives the whole document.
  * **pass_doc** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Pass the raw document instead of its text.
  * **count_tokens** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]]) – Token counter for `str` pieces (`None` disables the
    `tokens` / `tokenizer` annotation).
  * **tokenizer** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Name recorded as the `tokenizer` metadata key.

```pycon
>>> fs = FunctionSegmenter(lambda text: text.split(','))
>>> [s['text'] for s in fs('a,b,c')]
['a', 'b', 'c']
>>> s = list(fs('a,b,c'))[1]
>>> (s['start'], s['end'], s['index'])
(2, 3, 1)
```

### *class* ef.segmenters.RecursiveCharacterSegmenter(\*, chunk_size=512, chunk_overlap=64, separators=('\\n\\n', '\\n', '. ', ', ', ' ', ''), count_tokens=<function approx_token_count>, tokenizer='char-approx')

Bases: [`BaseSegmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.BaseSegmenter)

The default segmenter — recursive character splitting.

Splits a document on a descending ladder of separators (paragraph → line →
sentence → clause → word → character), merging the resulting pieces into
chunks of about `chunk_size` tokens with `chunk_overlap` tokens shared
between neighbours. This “good enough” default is, on realistic corpora,
within a point or two of far more elaborate methods — upgrade only if you
can measure the win.

Sizes are measured with `count_tokens`. The default counter is the
dependency-free [`approx_token_count()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.approx_token_count); inject a real tokenizer (and its
`tokenizer` name) when an exact count matters. Every emitted segment
records the tokenizer in its metadata and carries exact `start` / `end`
character offsets into the source.

* **Parameters:**
  * **chunk_size** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Target chunk size, in `count_tokens` units.
  * **chunk_overlap** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Tokens of overlap between consecutive chunks (must be
    smaller than `chunk_size`).
  * **separators** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – The separator ladder, coarsest first; the last should be
    `""` so an unsplittable run is still broken between characters.
  * **count_tokens** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]) – Maps a string to a token count.
  * **tokenizer** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Name recorded as the `tokenizer` metadata key.

```pycon
>>> seg = RecursiveCharacterSegmenter(chunk_size=3, chunk_overlap=1)
>>> [c['text'] for c in seg('one two three four')]
['one two three', 'three four']
```

### *class* ef.segmenters.Segmenter(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

Structural type for a segmenter: `str | Mapping -> Iterable[Segment]`.

A segmenter is *just a callable*. It accepts a document — a bare `str` or
a `Mapping` with a `text` key (and optionally an `id`, which becomes
the emitted segments’ `parent_id`) — and yields [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)
pieces. It returns an **iterable**, not a list: streaming is the default so
the heavy case scales.

Because the protocol’s only member is `__call__`, *every* callable
satisfies `isinstance(x, Segmenter)`. Treat it as documentation of intent,
not a discriminating check — [`as_segmenter()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenter_adapters.html.md#ef.segmenter_adapters.as_segmenter) is
the seam that turns an arbitrary callable into a *well-behaved* segmenter.

### ef.segmenters.approx_token_count(text)

Rough token count — the common `~4 characters per token` heuristic.

A dependency-free default so `ef` can talk in “tokens” without pulling in
`tiktoken` or a model tokenizer. Inject a real counter (and its name) into
a segmenter when an exact count matters.

```pycon
>>> approx_token_count('a' * 40)
10
>>> approx_token_count('')
0
```

* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

### ef.segmenters.hierarchical(segmenters,)

Compose segmenters into levels — each segments the previous level’s output.

Level 0 applies `segmenters[0]` to the document. Level *k* applies
`segmenters[k]` to every level- *(k-1)* segment’s text, setting each
child’s `parent_id` to that segment’s `id` and shifting its offsets to
stay absolute. The result is a flat stream of every segment of every level
(level 0 first), with the tree expressed purely through `parent_id`
pointers.

Each entry of `segmenters` is passed through
[`as_segmenter()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenter_adapters.html.md#ef.segmenter_adapters.as_segmenter), so strings (e.g. `"recursive"`)
and bare callables are accepted alongside ready-made segmenters.

* **Return type:**
  [`Segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.Segmenter)

### ef.segmenters.line_segmenter(doc,)

Segment a document into its non-empty lines.

Each line is stripped of surrounding whitespace; blank lines are dropped.
Character offsets point at the *stripped* content within the source.

A plain function — and therefore already a [`Segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.Segmenter). It carries
the marker [`as_segmenter()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenter_adapters.html.md#ef.segmenter_adapters.as_segmenter) uses to recognize a
ready-made segmenter.

```pycon
>>> [s['text'] for s in line_segmenter('  hello  \n\nworld\n')]
['hello', 'world']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterator)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)]

### ef.segmenters.materialise(x)

Force a streaming segmenter (or segment stream) to a concrete list.

Streaming is the default, but the light case often wants everything in
hand. [`materialise()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.materialise) is polymorphic:

- given a **segmenter** (a callable), it returns a new segmenter whose
  output is a `list` rather than a lazy iterator;
- given an **iterable of segments**, it returns a `list` of them.

```pycon
>>> eager = materialise(line_segmenter)
>>> out = eager('a\nb')
>>> isinstance(out, list)
True
>>> [s['text'] for s in out]
['a', 'b']
>>> materialise(s for s in [{'text': 'x'}])
[{'text': 'x'}]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

### ef.segmenters.with_overlap(segmenter, n_chars, /, \*, count_tokens=<function approx_token_count>, tokenizer='char-approx')

Wrap `segmenter` so consecutive segments overlap by `n_chars` characters.

Each segment is extended *forward* by up to `n_chars` characters (clamped
to the source length), so segment *K* shares its tail with segment *K+1*’s
head. A segment whose text changes has its `id` re-derived and its
`tokens` recounted; segments lacking `start` / `end` offsets pass
through untouched.

Overlap is expressed in *characters* here (this is a generic post-hoc
helper) — for token-measured overlap use a segmenter’s own `chunk_overlap`.

```pycon
>>> base = RecursiveCharacterSegmenter(chunk_size=3, chunk_overlap=0)
>>> [c['text'] for c in base('one two three four')]
['one two three', 'four']
>>> [c['text'] for c in with_overlap(base, 100)('one two three four')]
['one two three four', 'four']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.Segmenter)


# _autosummary/ef.segments.html.md

# ef.segments

The canonical `Segment` data model — `ef`’s interchange type for L2.

A *segment* is a piece of text carved out of a source document by a
[`Segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.Segmenter). This module defines the one shape every
segmenter, adapter and store in `ef` agrees on, so segments round-trip
losslessly across the whole pipeline.

Two surfaces over the same data:

- [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment) — a `TypedDict`: the lightweight, streaming-friendly
  *interchange* type. A segment is just a `dict`; the type is passive and
  every helper here is a free function over it.
- [`SegmentRecord`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.SegmentRecord) — a frozen dataclass: the *convenience* surface for
  code that prefers attribute access and immutability.

Only `text` is genuinely required; `id` is required by convention and is
**content-derived** by default ([`segment_id()`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.segment_id)) so that re-segmenting the
same document yields the same ids — the basis of idempotent ingestion.

The two field names that are *promoted to top level* (rather than buried in
`metadata`) are `parent_id` and `index` — hierarchy is expressed by a
flat list with `parent_id` pointers, never a nested structure.

Example — build a segment, derive its id, view it as a record:

```pycon
>>> seg = make_segment('Hello world.', index=0, tokens=3)
>>> seg['text']
'Hello world.'
>>> seg['id'] == segment_id('Hello world.')
True
>>> rec = segment_record(seg)
>>> rec.text, rec.index
('Hello world.', 0)
>>> rec.to_segment() == seg
True
```

### Module Attributes

| [`PROMOTED_METADATA_KEYS`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.PROMOTED_METADATA_KEYS)   | Metadata keys that, by convention, every `ef` adapter must round-trip faithfully.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`segment_id`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.segment_id)(text[, metadata])                 | Content-derived id for a segment — `sha256` of its normalized content.                                             |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`make_segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.make_segment)(text, \*[, id, parent_id, ...]) | Build a [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment), deriving a content-based `id` if none given.     |
| [`as_segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.as_segment)(x, \*\*defaults)                  | Coerce `x` into a [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment) — accepts a `str`, `Mapping` or record. |
| [`segment_record`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.segment_record)(x)                            | Coerce `x` (`str` / `Mapping` / [`SegmentRecord`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.SegmentRecord)) into a record.     |

### Classes

| [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)                                          | A piece of text carved from a source document — the interchange type.                                            |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`SegmentRecord`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.SegmentRecord)(text[, id, parent_id, start, ...]) | Frozen-dataclass view over a [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment) — the convenience surface. |

### ef.segments.PROMOTED_METADATA_KEYS *= ('source', 'source_type', 'tokenizer', 'token_count', 'embedding_model', 'page', 'license', 'ingestion_run_id')*

Metadata keys that, by convention, every `ef` adapter must round-trip
faithfully. They live inside `Segment["metadata"]` (they are *not* promoted
to top-level fields) but carry meaning the pipeline relies on. Recording
`tokenizer` in particular is mandatory — omitting it is the single most
common silent bug in chunking pipelines (a segment’s `tokens` count is
meaningless without knowing which tokenizer produced it).

### *class* ef.segments.Segment

Bases: [`TypedDict`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.TypedDict)

A piece of text carved from a source document — the interchange type.

A `TypedDict`: a [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment) *is* a plain `dict`, which keeps it
cheap to create and stream. `total=False` because most keys are optional;
by convention `text` is always present and `id` is always set (derived
from `text` if not supplied).

Keys:
: text: The segment’s text. **Required.**
  id: Stable identifier — content-derived by default ([`segment_id()`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.segment_id)).
  parent_id: Id of the source document or parent segment this came from.
  start: Character offset of the segment’s start in the source text.
  end: Character offset of the segment’s end (exclusive) in the source.
  index: Ordinal position of the segment in its segmenter’s output.
  tokens: Token count of `text` (meaningful only with `metadata` key
  <br/>
  > `tokenizer` recording which tokenizer counted it).
  <br/>
  metadata: Free-form mapping; framework-specific keys live here. See
  : [`PROMOTED_METADATA_KEYS`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.PROMOTED_METADATA_KEYS) for the conventional keys.

### *class* ef.segments.SegmentRecord(text, id='', parent_id=None, start=None, end=None, index=None, tokens=None, metadata=dict())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Frozen-dataclass view over a [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment) — the convenience surface.

Use this when attribute access and immutability read better than dict
access; use the [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment) `TypedDict` directly on the hot path.
The two convert losslessly via [`to_segment()`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.SegmentRecord.to_segment) and [`segment_record()`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.segment_record).

`id` is derived from `text` (and `metadata`) if left empty.

```pycon
>>> rec = SegmentRecord('hello', index=2)
>>> rec.id == segment_id('hello')
True
>>> rec.to_segment()['index']
2
```

#### to_segment()

Return an equivalent [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment) `dict` (dropping empty keys).

* **Return type:**
  [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)

### ef.segments.as_segment(x, \*\*defaults)

Coerce `x` into a [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment) — accepts a `str`, `Mapping` or record.

This is the segment-side normalizer that lets a `Segmenter` accept
loosely-typed output (a bare string, a partial `dict`) and still emit a
well-formed [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment). `**defaults` supplies *fallback* values:
a default fills a field only when `x` does not already carry it.

Accepts:

1. a [`SegmentRecord`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.SegmentRecord) — converted via [`SegmentRecord.to_segment()`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.SegmentRecord.to_segment);
2. a `str` — becomes the `text` of a fresh segment;
3. a `Mapping` with a `text` key — its keys are carried through.

The `id` is always present on the result (derived if absent).

* **Raises:**
  * [**TypeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#TypeError) – if `x` is none of the accepted forms.
  * [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – if `x` is a `Mapping` without a `text` key.
* **Return type:**
  [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)

```pycon
>>> as_segment('plain text', index=3)['index']
3
>>> as_segment({'text': 'kept', 'index': 0}, index=9)['index']  # x wins
0
```

### ef.segments.make_segment(text, , id=None, parent_id=None, start=None, end=None, index=None, tokens=None, metadata=None)

Build a [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment), deriving a content-based `id` if none given.

Optional fields are omitted from the result when `None` — a segment
`dict` carries only the keys it actually has.

```pycon
>>> seg = make_segment('chunk one', index=0, start=0, end=9)
>>> sorted(seg)
['end', 'id', 'index', 'start', 'text']
>>> seg['id'] == segment_id('chunk one')
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)

### ef.segments.segment_id(text, metadata=None)

Content-derived id for a segment — `sha256` of its normalized content.

The id is `sha256(normalize(text) + canonical_json(metadata))` — the
normalization and hashing primitives live in [`ef.hashing`](_autosummary/ef.hashing.html.md#module-ef.hashing), the single
source of truth `ef` content-addresses through. Because the id depends
only on content, re-segmenting an unchanged document produces identical ids
— which is what makes ingestion idempotent (a re-run is a no-op, not a
duplicate). Pass `metadata` only when two segments could share identical
`text` yet must stay distinct (e.g. same boilerplate from different
sources).

```pycon
>>> segment_id('hello') == segment_id('hello')
True
>>> segment_id('hello') == segment_id('world')
False
>>> segment_id('x', {'source': 'a'}) == segment_id('x', {'source': 'b'})
False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### ef.segments.segment_record(x)

Coerce `x` (`str` / `Mapping` / [`SegmentRecord`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.SegmentRecord)) into a record.

The dataclass counterpart of [`as_segment()`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.as_segment) — the convenience-surface
constructor.

```pycon
>>> segment_record('hello').text
'hello'
>>> segment_record({'text': 'hi', 'tokens': 1}).tokens
1
```

* **Return type:**
  [`SegmentRecord`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.SegmentRecord)


# _autosummary/ef.service.html.md

# ef.service

The HTTP-service bridge — [`EfService`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.EfService), a stateless-friendly facade.

`ef`’s query surface is **stateful**: [`ingest()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.ingest)
returns a live [`SearchableCorpus`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchableCorpus), and a
[`SourceManager`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager) holds a live corpus, an
[`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph) and `vd` collections. HTTP is
**stateless**. To serve `ef` over HTTP — so a frontend (`app_ef`) can reach
it through `qh.mk_app()` — something must map a JSON-friendly `corpus_id`
back to the live indexed object across requests.

[`EfService`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.EfService) is that bridge: a facade holding a **handle registry**
`{corpus_id: SourceManager}` **on the instance**. A single `EfService()` is
constructed once at server start-up, and its seven bound methods —
[`create_corpus()`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.EfService.create_corpus), [`search()`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.EfService.search),
[`retrieve()`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.EfService.retrieve), [`explore_corpus()`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.EfService.explore_corpus),
[`corpus_info()`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.EfService.corpus_info), [`list_corpora()`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.EfService.list_corpora),
[`delete_corpus()`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.EfService.delete_corpus) — are handed to `qh.mk_app()` as the HTTP
surface. The registry lives on the instance,
never as a module global: a process-wide mutable registry would be the
`ServiceContext` singleton anti-pattern `ef` rejects (`.claude/CLAUDE.md`
§6) — inject an [`EfService`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.EfService) explicitly instead.

Every method is JSON-friendly and fully type-annotated, because `qh` derives
the HTTP schema from the type hints. `ef`’s stateful objects never cross the
boundary: a corpus is addressed by its string `corpus_id`, an embedder /
segmenter by a string the DI seam resolves (`"hashing"`, `"openai:..."`,
`"cohere:..."`, …), and results are plain [`SearchHit`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchHit)
/ [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment) data.

This is *only* a transport bridge — it adds no orchestration. `ef` stays a
facade (`.claude/CLAUDE.md` §6); answer synthesis, agents and UI live outside.

Example — create a corpus, search it, then drop it, all offline:

```pycon
>>> from ef.service import EfService
>>> service = EfService()
>>> info = service.create_corpus(
...     ['the cat sat on the mat', 'dogs are loyal', 'felines and canines'],
...     corpus_id='animals',
... )
>>> info['corpus_id'], info['n_sources'], info['n_segments']
('animals', 3, 3)
>>> info['embedder'], info['dim']
('hashing:v1@512', 512)
>>> hits = service.search('animals', 'cat', limit=2)
>>> len(hits)
2
>>> isinstance(hits[0].score, float)
True
>>> segments = service.retrieve('animals', 'cat', limit=1)
>>> isinstance(segments[0]['text'], str)
True
>>> [c['corpus_id'] for c in service.list_corpora()]
['animals']
>>> service.delete_corpus('animals')
>>> service.list_corpora()
[]
```

### Classes

| [`CorpusInfo`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.CorpusInfo)                        | A JSON-friendly summary of one registered corpus.                         |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`EfService`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.EfService)(\*[, default_embedder]) | A registry-backed facade bridging stateful `ef` to a stateless transport. |

### *class* ef.service.CorpusInfo

Bases: [`TypedDict`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.TypedDict)

A JSON-friendly summary of one registered corpus.

The return shape shared by [`EfService.create_corpus()`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.EfService.create_corpus),
[`EfService.corpus_info()`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.EfService.corpus_info) and (as a list) [`EfService.list_corpora()`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.EfService.list_corpora)
— a plain `dict` an HTTP client and `qh`’s schema both understand.

Keys:
: corpus_id: the registry handle — how every other method addresses it.
  n_sources: the number of source documents in the corpus.
  n_segments: the number of indexed segments (sources cut by the segmenter).
  embedder: the embedder’s `model_id` (e.g. `"hashing:v1@512"`).
  dim: the embedding dimensionality.
  config_id: the content hash of the segmenter+embedder pipeline.

### *class* ef.service.EfService(, default_embedder=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A registry-backed facade bridging stateful `ef` to a stateless transport.

Construct one `EfService` per process, register corpora with
[`create_corpus()`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.EfService.create_corpus), then query them by `corpus_id`. Hand the seven
bound methods to `qh.mk_app()` to expose them over HTTP — see the module
docstring.

The handle registry is private instance state — never a module global.
Corpora are isolated: each [`create_corpus()`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.EfService.create_corpus) builds its own
[`SourceManager`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager) over its own in-memory `vd`
backend, so one corpus’s vectors never leak into another’s search.

`default_embedder` sets the embedder [`create_corpus()`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.EfService.create_corpus) resolves when
its own `embedder` argument is `None` — the per-instance hook a host
(e.g. `app_ef`) uses to pick a policy default without passing
`embedder=` on every call. It defaults to
[`DEFAULT_EMBEDDER`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.DEFAULT_EMBEDDER) (`"hashing"`), so a bare
`EfService()` stays dependency-free and offline.

```pycon
>>> service = EfService()
>>> len(service)
0
>>> _ = service.create_corpus(['hello world'], corpus_id='greetings')
>>> 'greetings' in service
True
>>> len(service)
1
```

A host can swap the default embedder at construction (the string is resolved
lazily, per corpus, by the DI seam — constructing the service touches no
network):

```pycon
>>> EfService(default_embedder='openai:text-embedding-3-small')
<EfService: 0 corpus(es) registered>
```

#### corpus_info(corpus_id)

Return the [`CorpusInfo`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.CorpusInfo) of a registered corpus.

* **Raises:**
  [**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) – if `corpus_id` is not registered.
* **Return type:**
  [`CorpusInfo`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.CorpusInfo)

#### create_corpus(sources, , embedder=None, segmenter=None, corpus_id=None, embedder_api_key=None)

Index `sources` into a new corpus, register it, return its [`CorpusInfo`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.CorpusInfo).

* **Parameters:**
  * **sources** ([`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – the corpus — a list of text documents.
  * **embedder** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the embedder, as a string the DI seam resolves
    ([`as_embedder()`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.as_embedder)) — `"hashing"`,
    `"openai:text-embedding-3-small"`, `"cohere:..."`, an
    `http(s)://` URL, …. `None` → the service’s
    `default_embedder` (chosen at construction; itself
    [`DEFAULT_EMBEDDER`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.DEFAULT_EMBEDDER), the dependency-free
    [`HashingEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.HashingEmbedder), unless a host overrode it).
  * **segmenter** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the segmenter, as a string
    ([`as_segmenter()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenter_adapters.html.md#ef.segmenter_adapters.as_segmenter)) — `None` → the
    recursive-character default.
  * **corpus_id** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the handle to register the corpus under; `None` → a
    fresh random id. Reusing a live id is an error.
  * **embedder_api_key** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – an optional API key for the embedder — the
    bring-your-own-key seam. When given and `embedder` is a
    hosted-API spec (`"openai:…"`, `"cohere:…"`, …), the key is
    forwarded to that adapter, so the service itself never needs to
    hold one. `None` → the adapter’s usual environment-variable
    resolution. Ignored for key-less embedders (e.g. `"hashing"`).
    The corpus’s embedder keeps the key for the life of the corpus,
    so [`search()`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.EfService.search) / [`retrieve()`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.EfService.retrieve) / [`explore_corpus()`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.EfService.explore_corpus)
    need no key of their own.
* **Return type:**
  [`CorpusInfo`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.CorpusInfo)
* **Returns:**
  the [`CorpusInfo`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.CorpusInfo) of the freshly indexed corpus.
* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – if `corpus_id` is already registered.

#### delete_corpus(corpus_id)

Drop a corpus from the registry, releasing its index.

* **Raises:**
  [**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) – if `corpus_id` is not registered.
* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### explore_corpus(corpus_id, , dims=2, projection_method='auto', cluster_method='kmeans', n_clusters=8, label=False)

Project & cluster a registered corpus — the corpus-map surface.

Runs [`ef.exploration.explore()`](_autosummary/ef.exploration.html.md#ef.exploration.explore) over the corpus: every indexed
segment is projected to `dims` coordinates and assigned a cluster,
returned as a row-aligned [`ExploreResult`](_autosummary/ef.exploration.html.md#ef.exploration.ExploreResult) (`ids` /
`coords` / `labels` / `cluster_titles`) — the JSON-friendly shape
an `app_ef` corpus map consumes.

* **Parameters:**
  * **corpus_id** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the corpus to explore.
  * **dims** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – projection target dimensionality — `2` or `3`.
  * **projection_method** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – `"auto"` / `"umap"` / `"pca"`.
  * **cluster_method** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – `"kmeans"` / `"hdbscan"`.
  * **n_clusters** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – number of k-means clusters.
  * **label** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – when `True`, also name each cluster with an LLM (needs the
    `ef[imbed]` extra and a key); default `False`.
* **Raises:**
  * [**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) – if `corpus_id` is not registered.
  * [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – if the corpus has fewer than 2 indexed segments.
* **Return type:**
  [`ExploreResult`](_autosummary/ef.exploration.html.md#ef.exploration.ExploreResult)

#### list_corpora()

Return the [`CorpusInfo`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.CorpusInfo) of every registered corpus.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`CorpusInfo`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.CorpusInfo)]

#### retrieve(corpus_id, query, , limit=10)

Retrieve ranked [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)s — the RAG-plug-in shape.

Like [`search()`](_autosummary/ef.service.html.md#ef.service.EfService.search), but returns plain segments in rank order (the
`score` dropped, the `source_id` folded into `metadata["source"]`)
— clean context to hand to an external RAG/agent framework. `ef`
returns context; it does not synthesize answers.

* **Raises:**
  [**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) – if `corpus_id` is not registered.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)]

#### search(corpus_id, query, , limit=10)

Search a registered corpus — up to `limit` ranked [`SearchHit`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchHit)s.

Each hit carries the matched [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment), its
similarity `score` (higher = closer) and the `source_id` it was cut
from.

* **Raises:**
  [**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) – if `corpus_id` is not registered.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`SearchHit`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchHit)]


# _autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md

# ef.source_manager

The search facade — one-shot [`ingest()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.ingest), [`SearchableCorpus`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchableCorpus), [`SourceManager`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager).

This is where `ef`’s layers come together. Phases 1–4 built the parts — a
[`Corpus`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.Corpus), a [`Segmenter`](_autosummary/ef.segmenters.html.md#ef.segmenters.Segmenter), an
[`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder), the content-addressed
[`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph) — and this module wires
**corpus → segment → embed → vd** into a usable search facade with the
progressive disclosure `ef` promises:

- **The light path** — [`ingest()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.ingest) — one line. A list of strings (or any
  corpus) in, a [`SearchableCorpus`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchableCorpus) out, `search(query)` ready.
- **The heavy path** — [`SourceManager`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager) — the same machinery with the
  components named explicitly and **multiple configs** (a config is one
  segmenter+embedder pipeline). Two configs that share a step share that step’s
  artifacts in the [`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph) for free — config
  branching costs only the divergent cone.
- **Keeping it fresh** — [`SourceManager.diagnose()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.diagnose) reports how far the
  index has drifted from the corpus (the four staleness conditions);
  [`SourceManager.refresh()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.refresh) re-syncs it. Pass `auto_refresh=True` to keep
  > the index live as the corpus is edited. See [`ef.diagnostics`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#module-ef.diagnostics) and

  [`ef.refresh`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#module-ef.refresh).

How the wiring works (one source, one config):

1. the source is a graph **leaf**, keyed by [`content_hash()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.content_hash);
2. a `segment` [`ProducerSpec`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec) over that leaf →
   a `list` of [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)s;
3. an `embed` [`ProducerSpec`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ProducerSpec) over the segment
   artifact → an `(n, dim)` array;
4. each `(segment, vector)` pair is written into a `vd` collection as a
   `vd.Document`, with `source_id` / `source_hash` / `config_hash`
   > recorded in its metadata.

`ef` owns the embedding: it always supplies vectors to `vd` (the index is
`vd`’s job, the vectors are `ef`’s — design notes §7), and at query time it
embeds the query with `input_type="query"` and hands `vd` the vector.

Example — the light path, end to end, offline:

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from ef import ingest, as_embedder
>>> toy = as_embedder(
...     lambda texts: np.array(
...         [[t.count('a'), t.count('e'), t.count('o')] for t in texts], dtype=float
...     ),
...     model_id='toy-vowels@3',
... )
>>> idx = ingest(['apple orchard', 'ocean breeze', 'green meadow'], embedder=toy)
>>> hits = idx.search('ocean breeze', limit=2)
>>> hits[0].segment['text']
'ocean breeze'
>>> round(hits[0].score, 6)
1.0
>>> hits[0].source_id is not None
True
```

And the true light path — no `embedder` at all, nothing to install beyond
`ef` itself (the default is the dependency-free
[`HashingEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.HashingEmbedder)):

```pycon
>>> idx = ingest(['apple orchard', 'ocean breeze', 'green meadow'])
>>> idx.search('ocean breeze', limit=1)[0].segment['text']
'ocean breeze'
```

### ef.source_manager.DEFAULT_EMBEDDER *= 'hashing'*

The model name [`ingest()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.ingest) / [`SourceManager`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager) resolve an absent
`embedder` to — [`HashingEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.HashingEmbedder), the dependency-free
default (numpy only, no extra to install). It is a lexical embedder; pass an
explicit `embedder` (`"st:..."`, `"openai:..."`, …) for neural
semantic quality.

### *class* ef.source_manager.SearchHit(segment, score, source_id=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One ranked search result — a [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment) and its score.

[`SearchableCorpus.search()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchableCorpus.search) / [`SourceManager.search()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.search) return a
ranked `list` of these. Keeping [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment) (the
interchange `TypedDict`) pure of a result-only `score` key, a
[`SearchHit`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchHit) *wraps* it alongside the similarity `score` and the
`source_id` of the document the segment was cut from.

#### segment

the matched segment — the canonical [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment).

* **Type:**
  [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)

#### score

the similarity score from the vector store (higher = closer).

* **Type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

#### source_id

the corpus key of the source document, if recorded.

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

```pycon
>>> hit = SearchHit(segment={'text': 'hi', 'id': 'x'}, score=0.9, source_id='doc-1')
>>> hit.segment['text'], hit.score, hit.source_id
('hi', 0.9, 'doc-1')
```

### *class* ef.source_manager.SearchableCorpus(collection, embedder, , config=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A ready-to-search view over one indexed config — the thin facade.

What [`ingest()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.ingest) returns and what [`SourceManager.searchable()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.searchable) hands
out: a small, read-mostly object that knows just enough to answer a query —
the `vd` collection holding the vectors and the [`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder)
that embeds the query. It does **not** re-index; mutation, refresh and
multi-config live on [`SourceManager`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager).

* **Parameters:**
  * **collection** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – the `vd` collection holding this config’s vectors.
  * **embedder** ([`Embedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.Embedder)) – the embedder — used to embed queries with `input_type="query"`.
  * **config** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the [`ConfigId`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.ConfigId) of the indexed pipeline, if known.

```pycon
>>> # built for you by ingest(); see the module docstring for a full example.
```

#### retrieve(query, , limit=10, filter=None)

Retrieve ranked [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)s — the RAG-plug-in surface.

The name an external RAG/agent framework reaches for. Where
[`search()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchableCorpus.search) returns scored [`SearchHit`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchHit)s (for inspecting the
ranking), `retrieve` returns **plain segments** in rank order — clean
context to hand to an LLM, with no `ef`-specific type to learn (design
notes §F5). `ef` returns the context; it does *not* synthesize answers.
See [`hits_to_segments()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.hits_to_segments) for how the score is dropped and the
`source_id` provenance is preserved in `metadata["source"]`.

```pycon
>>> # idx.retrieve('a query') -> [{'text': ..., 'id': ..., 'metadata': ...}, ...]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)]

#### search(query, , limit=10, filter=None)

Search the indexed corpus — return up to `limit` ranked [`SearchHit`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchHit)s.

`query` is text (embedded with `input_type="query"`) or an already
computed query vector. `filter` is a `vd` metadata filter
(MongoDB-style) — see `vd.filters`.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`SearchHit`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchHit)]

### *class* ef.source_manager.SourceManager(corpus=None, , segmenter=None, embedder=None, store=None, cache=None, auto_refresh=False, embedder_api_key=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The heavy search facade — multi-config corpus indexing over one corpus.

A [`SourceManager`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager) holds a corpus, an [`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph)
and one or more **configs**. A config is a named segmenter+embedder pipeline
([`PipelineSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.PipelineSpec)); [`register_config()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.register_config) adds one,
[`materialize()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.materialize) runs the corpus through it into a `vd` collection, and
[`search()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.search) queries it. Because every artifact is content-addressed in
the shared graph, two configs that share a step (e.g. the same segmenter)
compute that step’s artifacts **once** — config branching is free.

The constructor optionally registers a `"default"` config: pass an
`embedder` (and optionally a `segmenter`) and it is registered eagerly;
omit `embedder` to build every config explicitly via [`register_config()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.register_config).

* **Parameters:**
  * **corpus** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – the source corpus — coerced by [`as_corpus()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.as_corpus)
    (a mapping, a directory path, an iterable of sources, or `None`).
  * **segmenter** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – the default config’s segmenter — coerced by
    [`as_segmenter()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenter_adapters.html.md#ef.segmenter_adapters.as_segmenter) (`None` → the recursive
    default). Used only when `embedder` is also given.
  * **embedder** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – the default config’s embedder — coerced by
    [`as_embedder()`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.as_embedder). If given, a `"default"`
    config is registered; if `None`, no default config is registered.
  * **embedder_api_key** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – an optional API key for the default config’s embedder
    — forwarded to a hosted-API adapter (`"openai:…"` etc.) when the
    `embedder` is such a spec. The bring-your-own-key seam; ignored
    for key-less embedders. See [`register_config()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.register_config).
  * **store** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – where the vectors go. `None` → an in-memory `vd` backend; a
    `vd` client → collections are created on it; a `vd` collection →
    used directly (then only one config is supported); a backend-name
    string → `vd.connect` of that backend.
  * **cache** ([`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the [`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph)’s value cache — any
    `MutableMapping`; `None` → an in-RAM `dict`.
  * **auto_refresh** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – when `True`, the corpus is wrapped in a
    [`ChangeDetectingCorpus`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeDetectingCorpus) and every edit made
    *through* it is incrementally re-indexed into each materialized
    config — the index stays live without an explicit
    [`refresh()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.refresh). [`scan()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.scan) then also picks up out-of-band edits.

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from ef import as_embedder
>>> e1 = as_embedder(lambda ts: np.array([[len(t)] for t in ts], float), model_id='len@1')
>>> sm = SourceManager(['hello', 'hi there'], embedder=e1)
>>> report = sm.materialize()
>>> report['segments']
2
>>> len(sm.search('hello')) >= 1
True
```

#### *property* configs *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]*

The registered configs as a `{name: config_id}` mapping.

#### diagnose(config=None)

Report how far one config’s index has drifted from the corpus.

Computes the four staleness conditions — `orphan` / `missing` /
`stale` / `misconfigured` — by comparing the config’s `vd`
collection against the current corpus (see [`ef.diagnostics`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#module-ef.diagnostics)).
Read-only: it changes nothing. [`refresh()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.refresh) acts on the result.

```pycon
>>> sm = SourceManager({'a': 'alpha', 'b': 'beta'}, embedder='hashing')
>>> _ = sm.materialize()
>>> bool(sm.diagnose())                  # freshly indexed — in sync
False
>>> sm.corpus['a'] = 'alpha rewritten'
>>> sm.diagnose().stale
('a',)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`StalenessReport`](_autosummary/ef.diagnostics.html.md#ef.diagnostics.StalenessReport)

#### gc_orphans(config=None)

Delete the documents of sources that left the corpus — return the count.

The garbage-collection slice of [`refresh()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.refresh): it removes only
**orphan** documents (a source gone from the corpus) and prunes the
dead leaves out of the [`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph),
touching nothing else. `gc_orphans()` is the orphan-deletion half of
`refresh(mode='full')`.

* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

#### lineage(key)

The artifacts `key` was produced from — its provenance.

A thin pass-through to [`ArtifactGraph.ancestors`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.ancestors): “what produced this
vector / segment?”. The leaves of the returned set are the source
content hashes the artifact ultimately derives from.

* **Return type:**
  [`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### materialize(config=None, , sources=None)

Index the corpus through one config (or all) — corpus → segment → embed → `vd`.

For each source and each selected config: the source is added to the
[`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph) as a content-addressed leaf,
its `segment` and `embed` artifacts are [`materialize()`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph.materialize)d
(a cache hit if already computed — so a shared segment step runs once
across configs), and every `(segment, vector)` pair is written into
the config’s `vd` collection. Idempotent: re-materializing rewrites
identical documents.

* **Parameters:**
  * **config** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the config to index — a name, a [`ConfigId`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.ConfigId),
    or `None` for *every* registered config.
  * **sources** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – an optional subset of source ids to index — `None` (the
    default) indexes the whole corpus. [`refresh()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.refresh) uses this to
    re-index only the sources that changed; ids not in the corpus
    are skipped.
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]
* **Returns:**
  a report `dict` with `configs` / `sources` / `segments` counts.

#### pipeline(config=None)

The [`PipelineSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.PipelineSpec) of a registered config.

* **Return type:**
  [`PipelineSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.PipelineSpec)

#### rebuild(config=None)

Drop one config’s index entirely and re-index the whole corpus.

The heavy hammer: every document in the config’s `vd` collection is
deleted, then the whole corpus is re-[`materialize()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.materialize)d from
scratch. Use it to recover from a config whose `vd` documents were
produced by an earlier pipeline (every source `misconfigured`), or
whenever a guaranteed-clean index is wanted over the surgical
[`refresh()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.refresh). Every source is reported as `added` — the collection
was emptied and rebuilt.

* **Return type:**
  [`RefreshReport`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.RefreshReport)
* **Returns:**
  a [`RefreshReport`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.RefreshReport).

#### refresh(config=None, , sources=None, mode='full')

Re-sync one config’s `vd` index with the current corpus.

The explicit-refresh entry point. It [`diagnose()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.diagnose)s the config,
turns the staleness report into a [`RefreshPlan`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.RefreshPlan) for
the chosen `mode` ([`plan_refresh()`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.plan_refresh)), deletes the
stale/orphan documents, re-[`materialize()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.materialize)s what changed, and
prunes the dead leaves out of the [`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph).
Because it re-reads and re-hashes the corpus, it catches out-of-band
edits without any change-detection wrapper.

* **Parameters:**
  * **config** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the config to refresh (name / id / `None` for the default
    or sole config).
  * **sources** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – an optional subset of source ids to refresh — sources
    outside it are left untouched. Pair it with `mode='scoped_full'`
    (or `'incremental'`); `'full'` rejects it.
  * **mode** ([`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[`'none'`, `'incremental'`, `'full'`, `'scoped_full'`]) – one of [`REFRESH_MODES`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.REFRESH_MODES) — `'none'` (index
    new/changed content, delete nothing), `'incremental'` (also
    replace changed sources), `'full'` (also delete orphans — the
    corpus is authoritative), `'scoped_full'` (`full` over the
    `sources` subset). Default `'full'`.
* **Return type:**
  [`RefreshReport`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.RefreshReport)
* **Returns:**
  a [`RefreshReport`](_autosummary/ef.refresh.html.md#ef.refresh.RefreshReport).

```pycon
>>> sm = SourceManager({'a': 'alpha text', 'b': 'beta text'}, embedder='hashing')
>>> _ = sm.materialize()
>>> sm.corpus['b'] = 'beta rewritten'        # edit
>>> sm.corpus['c'] = 'gamma text'            # add
>>> del sm.corpus['a']                       # delete
>>> report = sm.refresh()
>>> report.added, report.modified, report.deleted
(('c',), ('b',), ('a',))
>>> bool(sm.diagnose())                      # in sync again
False
```

#### register_config(name='default', , segmenter=None, embedder=None, embedder_api_key=None)

Register a named segmenter+embedder pipeline; return its [`ConfigId`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.ConfigId).

The segmenter and embedder are coerced through `ef`’s DI seams
([`as_segmenter()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenter_adapters.html.md#ef.segmenter_adapters.as_segmenter) /
[`as_embedder()`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.as_embedder); an absent `embedder`
defaults to [`DEFAULT_EMBEDDER`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.DEFAULT_EMBEDDER)). Their ops are registered into the
shared [`ArtifactGraph`](_autosummary/ef.artifact_graph.html.md#ef.artifact_graph.ArtifactGraph) and a `vd` collection
is created for the config. Registering a config does *not* index it —
call [`materialize()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.materialize).

`embedder_api_key` is the per-call bring-your-own-key seam: when given
and `embedder` is a hosted-API provider spec (`"openai:…"` etc.),
the key is forwarded to that adapter instead of relying on a server
environment variable. Ignored for key-less embedders.

Re-registering the same `name` replaces it. Two configs that resolve
to the same [`PipelineSpec`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.PipelineSpec) share one
[`ConfigId`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.ConfigId) (and one collection).

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from ef import as_embedder
>>> sm = SourceManager(['a', 'b'])
>>> cid = sm.register_config(
...     'mini', embedder=as_embedder(
...         lambda ts: np.ones((len(ts), 2)), model_id='ones@2'))
>>> len(cid)
64
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### retrieve(query, , config=None, limit=10, filter=None)

Retrieve ranked [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)s — the RAG-plug-in surface.

The [`SourceManager`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager) counterpart of
[`SearchableCorpus.retrieve()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchableCorpus.retrieve): plain segments in rank order, the
clean context shape an external RAG/agent framework consumes (`ef`
does not synthesize answers). [`search()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.search) is the scored counterpart.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)]

#### scan()

Re-scan the corpus for out-of-band edits — needs `auto_refresh=True`.

Picks up changes made to the backing store *directly* (a file edited on
disk, an S3 object replaced) rather than through the corpus wrapper.
When the manager was built with `auto_refresh=True` the corpus is a
[`ChangeDetectingCorpus`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeDetectingCorpus); this calls its
[`scan()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeDetectingCorpus.scan), which fires a
[`ChangeEvent`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.ChangeEvent) per drift — each one auto-applied to
every materialized config. Returns the [`CorpusDiff`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.CorpusDiff).

For a large bulk of out-of-band edits, prefer [`refresh()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.refresh) (one
corpus pass) over `scan` (one collection pass per changed source).

* **Raises:**
  [**TypeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#TypeError) – if the corpus is not change-detecting (the manager was
      not built with `auto_refresh=True`).
* **Return type:**
  [`CorpusDiff`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.CorpusDiff)

#### search(query, , config=None, limit=10, filter=None)

Search one config’s index — return up to `limit` ranked [`SearchHit`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchHit)s.

`config` selects which config to query (a name / [`ConfigId`](_autosummary/ef.config.html.md#ef.config.ConfigId),
or `None` for the default or sole config). `query` is text or a
pre-computed query vector; `filter` is a `vd` metadata filter.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`SearchHit`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchHit)]

#### searchable(config=None)

Return a thin [`SearchableCorpus`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchableCorpus) bound to one config’s index.

* **Return type:**
  [`SearchableCorpus`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchableCorpus)

### ef.source_manager.hits_to_segments(hits)

Project [`SearchHit`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchHit)s to plain [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)s.

The shape [`SearchableCorpus.retrieve()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchableCorpus.retrieve) / [`SourceManager.retrieve()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.retrieve)
hand to an external RAG/agent framework — the RAG-plug-in surface (design
notes §F5). A [`SearchHit`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchHit) carries an `ef`-specific `score` and
`source_id`; a [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment) is a plain `TypedDict` an
external framework already understands (and trivially adapts to a LangChain
`Document` / LlamaIndex `TextNode` / a Ragas `retrieved_contexts`
`list[str]` via `[s["text"] for s in segments]`).

The similarity `score` is dropped — [`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment) is the
interchange type and stays pure of a result-only key (call `search()`
when the score matters). Provenance is *not* lost: each hit’s `source_id`
is folded into the segment’s `metadata` under the conventional `"source"`
key (one of [`PROMOTED_METADATA_KEYS`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.PROMOTED_METADATA_KEYS)), so a plain segment
still records which source document it was retrieved from. A segment that
already carries `metadata["source"]` keeps its own value.

```pycon
>>> hit = SearchHit(segment={'text': 'hi', 'id': 'x'}, score=0.9, source_id='doc-1')
>>> segs = hits_to_segments([hit])
>>> segs[0]['text'], segs[0]['metadata']['source']
('hi', 'doc-1')
>>> 'score' in segs[0]                          # the score is not a Segment key
False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/ef.segments.html.md#ef.segments.Segment)]

### ef.source_manager.ingest(sources, , segmenter=None, embedder=None, store=None, cache=None)

Index `sources` and return a ready-to-search [`SearchableCorpus`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchableCorpus) — one call.

The light path: corpus in, `search`-ready object out, every component
defaulted. `ingest(['a', 'b', 'c']).search('query')` is the whole story.
It builds a single-config [`SourceManager`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager), [`materialize()`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager.materialize)s
it, and hands back the thin [`SearchableCorpus`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchableCorpus).

* **Parameters:**
  * **sources** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – the corpus — coerced by [`as_corpus()`](_autosummary/ef.corpus.html.md#ef.corpus.as_corpus) (a mapping,
    a directory path, an iterable of strings/mappings, or `None`).
  * **segmenter** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – the segmenter — [`as_segmenter()`](_autosummary/ef.segmenter_adapters.html.md#ef.segmenter_adapters.as_segmenter)
    coerces it (`None` → the recursive default).
  * **embedder** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – the embedder — [`as_embedder()`](_autosummary/ef.embedder_adapters.html.md#ef.embedder_adapters.as_embedder)
    coerces it; `None` → [`DEFAULT_EMBEDDER`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.DEFAULT_EMBEDDER), the dependency-free
    [`HashingEmbedder`](_autosummary/ef.embedders.html.md#ef.embedders.HashingEmbedder) (so this call needs nothing
    beyond `pip install ef`). Pass an explicit embedder — e.g.
    `"st:all-MiniLM-L6-v2"` — for neural semantic quality.
  * **store** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – the vector store — `None` → an in-memory `vd` backend. See
    [`SourceManager`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SourceManager) for the other accepted forms.
  * **cache** ([`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the artifact-graph value cache — any `MutableMapping`.
* **Return type:**
  [`SearchableCorpus`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchableCorpus)
* **Returns:**
  a [`SearchableCorpus`](_autosummary/ef.source_manager.html.md#ef.source_manager.SearchableCorpus) over the freshly indexed corpus.

See the module docstring for a complete offline example.

# ai-agents.html.md

# For AI agents

`ef` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `ef-architecture`

Developer skill: the target architecture of the ef (Embedding Flow) package. Load at the start of any non-trivial task in the ef repository — refactoring, adding the Embedder/Segmenter facades, the Corpus abstraction, the ArtifactGraph indexing core, or the “ready search” surface. Covers the five-layer model, the core contracts, the light/heavy progressive-disclosure split, and the hard boundaries. Trigger on “work on ef”, “refactor ef”, “implement the embedder/segmenter/corpus/artifact graph”, “ef search”.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/ef ef-architecture --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/ef-architecture`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/ef/tree/HEAD/skills/ef-architecture).

## Instruction files

Files agents read before working in this repository.

- [`.claude/CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/ef/tree/HEAD/.claude/CLAUDE.md): read by Claude Code

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/ef/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`ef.md`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/ef/ef.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/ef/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
